1.90.m: accompanied by the mother-sounds, repeating it thrice, whose essence is nectar, / one should drink, remembering the Sarasvatī-vein [and] the tongue in the form of a flame.

1.90.s:
abdāñcaturvidhaṃ tasya pāṇḍityaṃ bhuvi jāyate /
evaṃ nityamuṣaḥ kāle yaḥ kuryācchuddhamānasaḥ //
1.90.d:
अब्दाञ्चतुर्विधं तस्य पाण्डित्यं भुवि जायते ।
एवं नित्यमुषः काले यः कुर्याच्छुद्धमानसः ॥
1.90.m: Within a year, the fourfold scholarship arises for him on earth. / Whoever acts thus daily at dawn, with a purified mind,

1.90.s:
sa yogī brahmavijñānī śivayogī tathātmavit /
anugrahoktacakrasthāṃ devīṃ tābhirvṛtāsmaret //
1.90.d:
स योगी ब्रह्मविज्ञानी शिवयोगी तथात्मवित् ।
अनुग्रहोक्तचक्रस्थां देवीं ताभिर्वृतास्मरेत् ॥
1.90.m: he is a yogin, a knower of Brahman, a Śiva-yogin, and a knower of the Self. / One should remember the goddess situated in the grace-conferring sacred diagram, surrounded by those [energies].

1.90.s:
caṃpakendīvarairmāsādārogyamupajāyate /
jvarabhūtagrahonmādaśītakākāmalākṣihṛt //
1.90.d:
चंपकेन्दीवरैर्मासादारोग्यमुपजायते ।
ज्वरभूतग्रहोन्मादशीतकाकामलाक्षिहृत् ॥
1.90.m: With campaka and blue water lilies, health is produced within a month, / taking away fever, spirits, planetary afflictions, insanity, cold, jaundice, and eye-disease.

1.90.s:
dantakarṇajvaraśiraḥ śūlagulmādi kukṣijāḥ /
vraṇapramehacchardyarśograhaṇyāmatridoṣajāḥ //
1.90.d:
दन्तकर्णज्वरशिरः शूलगुल्मादि कुक्षिजाः ।
व्रणप्रमेहच्छर्द्यर्शोग्रहण्यामत्रिदोषजाः ॥
1.90.m: Fever, headache, and ear-pain, toothache, abdominal tumors and the like arising in the belly, / ulcers, urinary ailments, vomiting, piles, dysentery, and those born from the three humors,

1.90.s:
sarve tathā śamaṃ yānti pūjayā parameśvarī /
dravyaṃ cakrasya nirmāṇe kāśmīraṃ samudī ritam //
1.90.d:
सर्वे तथा शमं यान्ति पूजया परमेश्वरी ।
द्रव्यं चक्रस्य निर्माणे काश्मीरं समुदी रितम् ॥
1.90.m: all these reach pacification through worship of the Supreme Mistress. / The substance for drawing the sacred diagram is said to be saffron,

1.90.s:
siṃdūraṃ gairikaṃ lākṣā daradaṃ candanadvayam /
biladvāre likhettryasraṃ ṣoḍaśatryasrasaṃyutam //
1.90.d:
सिंदूरं गैरिकं लाक्षा दरदं चन्दनद्वयम् ।
बिलद्वारे लिखेत्त्र्यस्रं षोडशत्र्यस्रसंयुतम् ॥
1.90.m: vermilion, red chalk, lac, cinnabar, and both kinds of sandalwood. / At the mouth of a cave, one should draw a triangle accompanied by sixteen triangles.

1.90.s:
daradenāsya madhyasthāṃ pūjayetparameśvarīm /
tābhistacchaktibhiḥ sākaṃ siddhadravyaiḥ sugandhibhiḥ //
1.90.d:
दरदेनास्य मध्यस्थां पूजयेत्परमेश्वरीम् ।
ताभिस्तच्छक्तिभिः साकं सिद्धद्रव्यैः सुगन्धिभिः ॥
1.90.m: With cinnabar, one should worship the Supreme Mistress seated in its center, / along with those powers of hers, with perfected substances and fragrant

1.90.s:
kusumairmāsamātreṇa nāgakanyāsamanvitam /
pātālādiṣu lokeṣu ramayatyaniśaṃ ciram //
1.90.d:
कुसुमैर्मासमात्रेण नागकन्यासमन्वितम् ।
पातालादिषु लोकेषु रमयत्यनिशं चिरम् ॥
1.90.m: flowers; within merely a month, accompanied by serpent maidens, / she delights him continuously for long in the nether worlds and other realms.

1.90.s:
yakṣarākṣasagandharvasiddhavidyādharāṅganāḥ /
piśācā guhyakā vīrāḥ kinnirā bhujagāstathā //
1.90.d:
यक्षराक्षसगन्धर्वसिद्धविद्याधराङ्गनाः ।
पिशाचा गुह्यका वीराः किन्निरा भुजगास्तथा ॥
1.90.m: Women of the yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, siddhas, and vidyādharas, / piśācas, guhyakas, heroes, kinnaras, and serpents as well,

1.90.s:
siddhyanti pūjanāttatra tathā tatproktakālataḥ /
kiṃśukairbhūṣaṇāvāptau pāṭalairgajasiddhaye //
1.90.d:
सिद्ध्यन्ति पूजनात्तत्र तथा तत्प्रोक्तकालतः ।
किंशुकैर्भूषणावाप्तौ पाटलैर्गजसिद्धये ॥
1.90.m: are mastered by worship there, and according to the time stated for that: / with kiṃśuka blossoms for obtaining ornaments; with pāṭala flowers for mastering elephants;

1.90.s:
raktotpalairaśvasiddhau kumudaiścarasiddhaye /
utpalairuṣṭrasaṃsiddhyai tagaraiḥ paśusiddhaye //
1.90.d:
रक्तोत्पलैरश्वसिद्धौ कुमुदैश्चरसिद्धये ।
उत्पलैरुष्ट्रसंसिद्ध्यै तगरैः पशुसिद्धये ॥
1.90.m: with red lotuses for mastering horses; with night-blooming white lotuses for mastering spies; / with blue lotuses for mastering camels; with tagara flowers for mastering cattle;

1.90.s:
jaṃbīrairmahiṣāvāptyai lakucairajasiddhaye /
dāḍimairnidhisaṃsiddhyai madhukairgānasiddhaye //
1.90.d:
जंबीरैर्महिषावाप्त्यै लकुचैरजसिद्धये ।
दाडिमैर्निधिसंसिद्ध्यै मधुकैर्गानसिद्धये ॥
1.90.m: with citrons for obtaining buffaloes; with lakuca fruits for mastering goats; / with pomegranates for mastering treasures; with madhuka flowers for mastering singing;

1.90.s:
bakulairaṅganāsiddhyai kahlāraiḥ putrasiddhaye /
śatapatrairjayāvāptyai ketakairvāhanāptaye //
1.90.d:
बकुलैरङ्गनासिद्ध्यै कह्लारैः पुत्रसिद्धये ।
शतपत्रैर्जयावाप्त्यै केतकैर्वाहनाप्तये ॥
1.90.m: with bakula blossoms for winning women; with white water lilies for obtaining a son; / with lotuses for obtaining victory; with ketakī blossoms for acquiring vehicles.

1.90.s:
saurabhāḍhyaiḥ prasūnaistu nityaṃ saubhāgyasiddhaye /
pūjayenmāsamātraṃ vā dviguṇaṃ triguṇaṃ tu vā //
1.90.d:
सौरभाढ्यैः प्रसूनैस्तु नित्यं सौभाग्यसिद्धये ।
पूजयेन्मासमात्रं वा द्विगुणं त्रिगुणं तु वा ॥
1.90.m: With intensely fragrant blossoms, one should worship continuously for the attainment of good fortune / for just a month, or twice that, or thrice that.

1.90.s:
yāvatphalāvāptikāṅkṣī śarkarāghṛtapāyasaiḥ /
sacakraparivārāṃ tāṃ devīṃ salilamadhyagām //
1.90.d:
यावत्फलावाप्तिकाङ्क्षी शर्कराघृतपायसैः ।
सचक्रपरिवारां तां देवीं सलिलमध्यगाम् ॥
1.90.m: As long as one desires the attainment of the fruit, with sugar, ghee, and milk-rice, / [one should satisfy] that goddess situated in the midst of water, together with the retinue of her cakra.

1.90.s:
tarppayetkusumaiḥ sārdhyaiḥ sarvopadravaśāntaye /
ghṛtaiḥ pūrṇāyuṣaḥ siddhyai kṣauddraiḥ saubhāgyasiddhaye //
1.90.d:
तर्प्पयेत्कुसुमैः सार्ध्यैः सर्वोपद्रवशान्तये ।
घृतैः पूर्णायुषः सिद्ध्यै क्षौद्द्रैः सौभाग्यसिद्धये ॥
1.90.m: One should offer libation with flowers and arghya water for the pacification of all afflictions, / with ghee for the attainment of a full lifespan, and with honey for the attainment of good fortune;

1.90.s:
dugdhairārogyasaṃsiddhyai tribhiraiśvaryasiddhaye /
nālikerodakaiḥ prītyai himatoyairnṛpāptaye /
sarvārthasiddhaya tauryairabhiṣiñcenmaheśvarīm //
1.90.d:
दुग्धैरारोग्यसंसिद्ध्यै त्रिभिरैश्वर्यसिद्धये ।
नालिकेरोदकैः प्रीत्यै हिमतोयैर्नृपाप्तये ।
सर्वार्थसिद्धय तौर्यैरभिषिञ्चेन्महेश्वरीम् ॥
1.90.m: With milk for the attainment of health, with the three [sweet substances] for the attainment of sovereignty, / with coconut water for affection, and with cold water for winning kings. / For the attainment of all purposes, one should bathe the great goddess with triple musical performances.

1.90.s:
pūgodyāne yajeddevīṃ siddhadravyairdivāniśam /
nivasaṃstatra tatpuṣpairjāyate manmathopamaḥ //
1.90.d:
पूगोद्याने यजेद्देवीं सिद्धद्रव्यैर्दिवानिशम् ।
निवसंस्तत्र तत्पुष्पैर्जायते मन्मथोपमः ॥
1.90.m: In a grove of betel-nut palms, one should worship the goddess day and night with perfected substances; / dwelling there, [worshiping] with their flowers, he becomes like the god of love.

1.90.s:
pūrṇāsu niyattaṃ devīṃ kanyakāyāṃ samarcayan /
kṛtyāḥ pareritā mantrā vimukhāṃstān grasaṃti vai //
1.90.d:
पूर्णासु नियत्तं देवीं कन्यकायां समर्चयन् ।
कृत्याः परेरिता मन्त्रा विमुखांस्तान् ग्रसंति वै ॥
1.90.m: Restrained, worshiping the goddess in a maiden on the Pūrṇā lunar days, / malevolent rites and mantras incited by others turn back and consume those [senders].

1.90.s:
liṅgatrayamayīṃ devīṃ cakrasthābhiśca śaktibhiḥ /
pūjayanniṣṭamakhilaṃ labhate 'tra paratra ca //
1.90.d:
लिङ्गत्रयमयीं देवीं चक्रस्थाभिश्च शक्तिभिः ।
पूजयन्निष्टमखिलं लभते ऽत्र परत्र च ॥
1.90.m: Worshiping the goddess composed of the three liṅgas along with the śaktis situated in the cakra, / one attains all desired things in this world and the next.

1.90.s:
śatamānakṛtaiḥ svarṇapuṣpaiḥ saurabhyavāsitaiḥ /
pūjayanmāsamātreṇa prāgjanmādyairvimucyate //
1.90.d:
शतमानकृतैः स्वर्णपुष्पैः सौरभ्यवासितैः ।
पूजयन्मासमात्रेण प्राग्जन्माद्यैर्विमुच्यते ॥
1.90.m: Worshiping for merely a month with golden flowers weighing a śatamāna / and scented with fragrances, one is liberated from [the sins of] previous births and the like.

1.90.s:
tathā ratnaiśca navabhirmāsaṃ tu yadi pūjayet /
vimuktasarvapāpaughaistāṃ ca paśyati cakṣuṣā //
1.90.d:
तथा रत्नैश्च नवभिर्मासं तु यदि पूजयेत् ।
विमुक्तसर्वपापौघैस्तां च पश्यति चक्षुषा ॥
1.90.m: Likewise, if one worships for a month with the nine jewels, / freed from the floods of all sins, he sees her with his own eyes.

1.90.s:
aṃśukairarcayeddevīṃ māsamātraṃ sugandhibhiḥ /
mucyate pāpakṛtyādiduḥkhaughairitarairapi //
1.90.d:
अंशुकैरर्चयेद्देवीं मासमात्रं सुगन्धिभिः ।
मुच्यते पापकृत्यादिदुःखौघैरितरैरपि ॥
1.90.m: One who worships the goddess for merely a month with fragrant garments / is released from the floods of sins, malevolent rites, and other miseries.

1.90.s:
devīrūpaṃ svamātmānaṃ cakraṃ śaktīḥ samantataḥ /
bhāvayanviṣayaiḥ puṣpaiḥ pūjayaṃstanmayo bhavet //
1.90.d:
देवीरूपं स्वमात्मानं चक्रं शक्तीः समन्ततः ।
भावयन्विषयैः पुष्पैः पूजयंस्तन्मयो भवेत् ॥
1.90.m: Contemplating oneself as having the form of the goddess, and the cakra and the śaktis all around, / worshiping with sensory objects as flowers, one becomes identified with her.

1.90.s:
ṣoḍaśānāṃ tu nityānāṃ pratyeka tithayaḥ kramāt /
tattittithau tadbhajanaṃ japahomādikaṃ caret //
1.90.d:
षोडशानां तु नित्यानां प्रत्येक तिथयः क्रमात् ।
तत्तित्तिथौ तद्भजनं जपहोमादिकं चरेत् ॥
1.90.m: There are lunar days in succession for each of the sixteen Nityās; / on each respective lunar day, one should perform their worship, recitation, fire oblation, and the like.

1.90.s:
ghṛtaṃ ca śarkarā dugdhamapūpaṃ kadalīpalam /
kṣaudraṃ guḍaṃ nālikeraphalaṃ lājā tilaṃ dadhi //
1.90.d:
घृतं च शर्करा दुग्धमपूपं कदलीपलम् ।
क्षौद्रं गुडं नालिकेरफलं लाजा तिलं दधि ॥
1.90.m: Ghee, sugar, milk, cakes, plantain fruit, / honey, jaggery, coconut fruit, parched grain, sesame seeds, curds,

1.90.s:
pṛthukaṃ caṇakaṃ mudgapāyasaṃ ca nivedayet /
kāmeśvaryādiśaktīnāṃ sarvāsāmapi coditam //
1.90.d:
पृथुकं चणकं मुद्गपायसं च निवेदयेत् ।
कामेश्वर्यादिशक्तीनां सर्वासामपि चोदितम् ॥
1.90.m: Flattened rice, chickpeas, and mung bean milk-rice should be offered; / this is prescribed for all the śaktis beginning with Kāmeśvarī.

1.90.s:
ādyāyā lalitāyāstu sarvāṇyetāni sarvadā /
nivedayeñca juhuyādvahnau dadyānnṛṇāmapi //
1.90.d:
आद्याया ललितायास्तु सर्वाण्येतानि सर्वदा ।
निवेदयेञ्च जुहुयाद्वह्नौ दद्यान्नृणामपि ॥
1.90.m: To the primordial Lalitā, however, one should constantly offer all these, / offer them into the fire, and give them to men as well.

1.90.s:
tattadvidyākṣaraproktamauṣadhaṃ tatpramāṇataḥ /
saṃpiṣya guṭikīkṛtya tābhiḥ sarvaṃ ca sādhayet //
1.90.d:
तत्तद्विद्याक्षरप्रोक्तमौषधं तत्प्रमाणतः ।
संपिष्य गुटिकीकृत्य ताभिः सर्वं च साधयेत् ॥
1.90.m: Crushing the medicinal herbs prescribed for each respective syllable of the vidyā in their proper measures / and making pills, one accomplishes everything through them.

1.90.s:
ravivāre 'ruṇāṃbhojaiḥ kumudaiḥ somavārake /
bhaume raktotpalaiḥ saumye vāre tagarasaṃbhavaiḥ //
1.90.d:
रविवारे ऽरुणांभोजैः कुमुदैः सोमवारके ।
भौमे रक्तोत्पलैः सौम्ये वारे तगरसंभवैः ॥
1.90.m: On Sunday with red lotuses, on Monday with white water lilies, / on Tuesday with red night-lotuses, on Wednesday with flowers born of the tagara,

1.90.s:
guruvāre sukahlāraiḥ śukravāre sitāṃbujaiḥ /
nīlotpalairmandavāre pūjayediṣṭamādarāt //
1.90.d:
गुरुवारे सुकह्लारैः शुक्रवारे सितांबुजैः ।
नीलोत्पलैर्मन्दवारे पूजयेदिष्टमादरात् ॥
1.90.m: On Thursday with fine white water lilies, on Friday with white lotuses, / and on Saturday with blue water lilies, one should reverently worship the chosen deity.

1.90.s:
nivedayetkramātteṣu ravivārādiṣu kramāt /
pāyasaṃ dugdhakadalīnavanītasitāghṛtam //
1.90.d:
निवेदयेत्क्रमात्तेषु रविवारादिषु क्रमात् ।
पायसं दुग्धकदलीनवनीतसिताघृतम् ॥
1.90.m: In succession on those days beginning with Sunday, one should offer in order: / milk-rice, milk, plantains, fresh butter, candied sugar, and ghee.

1.90.s:
evamiṣṭaṃ samārādhya devīṃ gandhādibhiryajet /
grahapīḍāṃ vijityāśusukhāni ca samaśnute //
1.90.d:
एवमिष्टं समाराध्य देवीं गन्धादिभिर्यजेत् ।
ग्रहपीडां विजित्याशुसुखानि च समश्नुते ॥
1.90.m: Having thus propitiated the chosen deity, one should worship the goddess with perfumes and other offerings; / conquering the affliction caused by planets, he quickly enjoys pleasures.

1.90.s:
ardharātre tu sādhyāṃ strīṃ smaranmadanavahninā /
dahyamānāṃ hṛtasvāntāṃ mastakasthāpitāñjalim //
1.90.d:
अर्धरात्रे तु साध्यां स्त्रीं स्मरन्मदनवह्निना ।
दह्यमानां हृतस्वान्तां मस्तकस्थापिताञ्जलिम् ॥
1.90.m: At midnight, meditating on the targeted woman burned by the fire of love, / her mind captivated, with hands folded in supplication placed upon her head,

1.90.s:
vikīrṇakeśīmālolalocanāmaruṇāruṇām /
vāyupreṅkhatpatākāsthapadā padmakalevarām //
1.90.d:
विकीर्णकेशीमालोललोचनामरुणारुणाम् ।
वायुप्रेङ्खत्पताकास्थपदा पद्मकलेवराम् ॥
1.90.m: Her hair disheveled, her eyes wildly rolling, deeply reddened, / her feet placed on a flag waving in the wind, her body like a lotus,

1.90.s:
vivekavidhurāṃ mattāṃ mānalajjābhayātigām /
cintayannarcayeñcakraṃ madhye devīṃ digaṃbarām //
1.90.d:
विवेकविधुरां मत्तां मानलज्जाभयातिगाम् ।
चिन्तयन्नर्चयेञ्चक्रं मध्ये देवीं दिगंबराम् ॥
1.90.m: Bereft of discrimination, intoxicated, having transcended pride, shame, and fear— / contemplating her, he should worship the cakra and, in its center, the sky-clad goddess.

1.90.s:
japādāḍimabandhūkakiṃśukādyaiḥ samarcayet /
anyaiḥ sugandhiśephaālīkusumādyaiḥ samarcayet //
1.90.d:
जपादाडिमबन्धूककिंशुकाद्यैः समर्चयेत् ।
अन्यैः सुगन्धिशेफआलीकुसुमाद्यैः समर्चयेत् ॥
1.90.m: One should worship with hibiscus, pomegranate, bandhūka, kiṃśuka, and other flowers, / and with other fragrant flowers such as the śephālī.

1.90.s:
trisaptarātrādāyāti proktarūpā madākulā /
yāvaccharīrapātaḥ syācchāpo vānapagāsya sā //
1.90.d:
त्रिसप्तरात्रादायाति प्रोक्तरूपा मदाकुला ।
यावच्छरीरपातः स्याच्छापो वानपगास्य सा ॥
1.90.m: After three times seven nights she arrives, of the description stated, overwhelmed by passion; / until the fall of his body or until a curse, she never departs from him.

1.90.s:
padmairaktaistrimadhvaktairhemāllakṣmīmavāpnuyāt /
tathaiva kairavai raktairaṅganāḥ svavaśaṃ nayet //
1.90.d:
पद्मैरक्तैस्त्रिमध्वक्तैर्हेमाल्लक्ष्मीमवाप्नुयात् ।
तथैव कैरवै रक्तैरङ्गनाः स्ववशं नयेत् ॥
1.90.m: Through red lotuses smeared with the three sweets, one attains fortune from gold; / likewise, through red water lilies, one brings women under one's control.

1.90.s:
samānarūpavatsāyāḥ śuklāyā goḥ payaḥplutaiḥ /
mallikāmālatījātīśatapatrairhutairbhavet //
1.90.d:
समानरूपवत्सायाः शुक्लाया गोः पयःप्लुतैः ।
मल्लिकामालतीजातीशतपत्रैर्हुतैर्भवेत् ॥
1.90.m: Through offering oblation of mallikā, mālatī, jātī, and lotus flowers / soaked in the milk of a white cow having a calf of the same color, there arises

1.90.s:
kīrtividyādhanārogyasaubhāgyavittapādikam /
āragvadhaprasūnaistu kṣaudrāktairhavanādbhavet //
1.90.d:
कीर्तिविद्याधनारोग्यसौभाग्यवित्तपादिकम् ।
आरग्वधप्रसूनैस्तु क्षौद्राक्तैर्हवनाद्भवेत् ॥
1.90.m: Fame, learning, wealth, health, good fortune, trees, and the like; / and from offering oblation of āragvadha blossoms smeared with honey arises

1.90.s:
svarṇādistaṃ bhanaṃ śatrornṛpādīnāṃ krudho 'pi ca /
ājyāktaiḥ karavīrotthaiḥ prasūnairaruṇairhutaiḥ //
1.90.d:
स्वर्णादिस्तं भनं शत्रोर्नृपादीनां क्रुधो ऽपि च ।
आज्याक्तैः करवीरोत्थैः प्रसूनैररुणैर्हुतैः ॥
1.90.m: Paralysis of enemies, gold, and also the anger of kings and others. / Through red karavīra blossoms smeared with ghee offered into the fire,

1.90.s:
raktāṃbarāṇi vanitā bhūpāmātyavaśaṃ tathā /
bhūṣāvāhanavāṇijyasiddhayaścāsya vāñchitāḥ //
1.90.d:
रक्तांबराणि वनिता भूपामात्यवशं तथा ।
भूषावाहनवाणिज्यसिद्धयश्चास्य वाञ्छिताः ॥
1.90.m: Red garments, women, and the subjugation of kings and ministers are achieved, / as well as his desired successes in ornaments, vehicles, and commerce.

1.90.s:
lavaṇaiḥ sarṣarpairairitarairvātha homataḥ /
satailāktairniśāmadhye tvānayedvāñchitāṃ vadhūm //
1.90.d:
लवणैः सर्षर्पैरैरितरैर्वाथ होमतः ।
सतैलाक्तैर्निशामध्ये त्वानयेद्वाञ्छितां वधूम् ॥
1.90.m: By offering oblations of salt, mustard seeds, or others / smeared with oil in the middle of the night, one brings the desired woman.

1.90.s:
tailāktairjuhuyātkṛṣṇadarapuṣpairniśātare /
māsādarātestasyārtirjvareṇa bhavati dhruvam //
1.90.d:
तैलाक्तैर्जुहुयात्कृष्णदरपुष्पैर्निशातरे ।
मासादरातेस्तस्यार्तिर्ज्वरेण भवति ध्रुवम् ॥
1.90.m: Deep in the night, one should offer dark dhattūra flowers smeared with oil; / within a month, severe suffering from fever certainly befalls the enemy.

1.90.s:
āruṣkarairdhṛtābhyaktaistadbījairniśi homataḥ /
śatrorddāhavraṇāni syurduḥsādhyāni cikitsakaiḥ //
1.90.d:
आरुष्करैर्धृताभ्यक्तैस्तद्बीजैर्निशि होमतः ।
शत्रोर्द्दाहव्रणानि स्युर्दुःसाध्यानि चिकित्सकैः ॥
1.90.m: From offering marking-nut fruits and their seeds smeared with ghee into the fire at night, / burning ulcers arise on the enemy that are difficult to cure by physicians.

1.90.s:
tathā tattailasaṃsiktairbījairaṅkolakairapi /
maricaiḥ sarṣapājyāktaunaśi homānusārataḥ //
1.90.d:
तथा तत्तैलसंसिक्तैर्बीजैरङ्कोलकैरपि ।
मरिचैः सर्षपाज्याक्तौनशि होमानुसारतः ॥
1.90.m: Likewise, with aṅkola seeds saturated with their oil, / with black pepper, and with mustard seeds smeared with ghee, in accordance with the midnight oblation,

1.90.s:
vāñchitāṃ vanitāṃ kāmajvarārtāmānayeddrutam /
śālibhiścājyasaṃsiktairhemācchālīnavāpnuyāt //
1.90.d:
वाञ्छितां वनितां कामज्वरार्तामानयेद्द्रुतम् ।
शालिभिश्चाज्यसंसिक्तैर्हेमाच्छालीनवाप्नुयात् ॥
1.90.m: One quickly brings the desired woman, afflicted with the fever of passion. / Through winter rice sprinkled with ghee, one obtains winter rice from gold.

1.90.s:
mudgairmudgaṃ ghṛtairājyaṃ siddhairitthaṃ hutairbhavet /
sādhyarkṣavṛkṣasaṃbhūtāṃ piṣṭapādarajaḥkṛtām //
1.90.d:
मुद्गैर्मुद्गं घृतैराज्यं सिद्धैरित्थं हुतैर्भवेत् ।
साध्यर्क्षवृक्षसंभूतां पिष्टपादरजःकृताम् ॥
1.90.m: Through mung beans, mung beans [are obtained]; through ghee, ghee is obtained by adepts when offered in this manner. / An effigy made of dust from the foot mixed with flour, born of a tree under the target's birth star,

1.90.s:
rājīmarīciloṇotthāṃ puttalīṃ juhuyānniśi /
prapadābhyāṃ ca jaṅghābhyāṃ jānubhyāmuruyugmataḥ //
1.90.d:
राजीमरीचिलोणोत्थां पुत्तलीं जुहुयान्निशि ।
प्रपदाभ्यां च जङ्घाभ्यां जानुभ्यामुरुयुग्मतः ॥
1.90.m: Produced from black mustard, black pepper, and salt, one should offer into the fire at night, / from the forefeet, the shanks, the knees, from the two thighs,

1.90.s:
nābheradhastāddhṛdayādbhinnenākaṇṭhastathā /
śirasā ca sutīkṣṇena cchitvā śastreṇa vai kramāt //
1.90.d:
नाभेरधस्ताद्धृदयाद्भिन्नेनाकण्ठस्तथा ।
शिरसा च सुतीक्ष्णेन च्छित्वा शस्त्रेण वै क्रमात् ॥
1.90.m: From below the navel, from the heart, and likewise through the severed throat, / and cutting off the head with a very sharp weapon in proper order.

1.90.s:
evaṃ dvādaśadhā homānnaranārīnarādhipāḥ /
vaśyā bhavanti saptāḍājjvarārttīścāsya vāñchayā //
1.90.d:
एवं द्वादशधा होमान्नरनारीनराधिपाः ।
वश्या भवन्ति सप्ताडाज्ज्वरार्त्तीश्चास्य वाञ्छया ॥
1.90.m: Thus, from the twelvefold fire oblation, men, women, and kings / become subjugated within seven days, and they are afflicted with fever by his wish.

1.90.s:
piṣṭena guḍayuktena maricairjīrakairyutām /
kṛtvā puttalikāṃ sādhyanāmayuktāmatho hṛdi //
1.90.d:
पिष्टेन गुडयुक्तेन मरिचैर्जीरकैर्युताम् ।
कृत्वा पुत्तलिकां साध्यनामयुक्तामथो हृदि ॥
1.90.m: Having made an effigy with flour mixed with jaggery, black pepper, and cumin seeds, / endowed with the name of the target in the heart,

1.90.s:
sanāmahomasaṃpātaghṛtepācyatāṃ punaḥ /
spṛśannijakarāgreṇa sahasraṃ prajapenmanum //
1.90.d:
सनामहोमसंपातघृतेपाच्यतां पुनः ।
स्पृशन्निजकराग्रेण सहस्रं प्रजपेन्मनुम् ॥
1.90.m: Then, having cooked it in the residue of the ghee of the fire oblation performed with the name, / touching it with the tip of his hand, he should recite the mantra a thousand times.

1.90.s:
abhyarcya tad ghṛtābhyaktaṃ bhakṣayettaddhiyā japan /
naranārīnṛpāstasya vaśyāḥ syurmaraṇāvadhiṃ //
1.90.d:
अभ्यर्च्य तद् घृताभ्यक्तं भक्षयेत्तद्धिया जपन् ।
नरनारीनृपास्तस्य वश्याः स्युर्मरणावधिं ॥
1.90.m: Having worshipped it, smeared it with ghee, he should eat it while reciting with his mind on that person; / men, women, and kings will remain subjugated to him until death.

1.90.s:
śaktayaṣṭagandhaṃ saṃpiṣya kanyayā śiśire jale /
tena vai tilakaṃ bhāle dhārayanvaśayejjagat //
1.90.d:
शक्तयष्टगन्धं संपिष्य कन्यया शिशिरे जले ।
तेन वै तिलकं भाले धारयन्वशयेज्जगत् ॥
1.90.m: Having crushed the eightfold perfume of the Śakti in cold water by means of a maiden, / wearing a sectarian mark on the forehead with it, one subjugates the universe.

1.90.s:
śālitandulamādāya prasthaṃ bhāṇḍe nave bhipet /
samānavarṇevatsāyā raktāyā goḥ payastathā //
1.90.d:
शालितन्दुलमादाय प्रस्थं भाण्डे नवे भिपेत् ।
समानवर्णेवत्साया रक्ताया गोः पयस्तथा ॥
1.90.m: Taking a prastha measure of winter rice grains, one should place it in a new vessel; / likewise, taking milk from a red cow having a calf of the same color

1.90.s:
dvuguṇaṃ tatra nikṣipya śrapayetsaṃskṛte 'nale /
ghṛtena siktaṃ sikthaṃ tu kṛtvā tatsasitaṃ kare //
1.90.d:
द्वुगुणं तत्र निक्षिप्य श्रपयेत्संस्कृते ऽनले ।
घृतेन सिक्तं सिक्थं तु कृत्वा तत्ससितं करे ॥
1.90.m: Twice that in measure, pouring it in, one should cook it on a consecrated fire. / Then, making a lump of boiled rice moistened with ghee, placing it in the hand with white sugar,

1.90.s:
vidhāya vidyāmaṣṭorddhūśataṃ jasvā hunettataḥ /
evaṃ homo mahālakṣmīmāvahetpratipatkṛtaḥ //
1.90.d:
विधाय विद्यामष्टोर्द्धूशतं जस्वा हुनेत्ततः ।
एवं होमो महालक्ष्मीमावहेत्प्रतिपत्कृतः ॥
1.90.m: Repeating the vidyā one hundred and eight times, one should then offer it into the fire; / such a fire oblation, performed on the first lunar day, brings Mahālakṣmī.

1.90.s:
śukravāreṣvapi tathā varṣānnṛpasamo bhavet /
pañcamyāṃ tu viśeṣeṇa prāgvaddhomaṃ samācaret //
1.90.d:
शुक्रवारेष्वपि तथा वर्षान्नृपसमो भवेत् ।
पञ्चम्यां तु विशेषेण प्राग्वद्धोमं समाचरेत् ॥
1.90.m: Likewise on Fridays, within a year one becomes equal to a king; / on the fifth lunar day in particular, one should perform the fire oblation as before.

1.90.s:
tasyāṃ tithau trimadhvaktairmallikādyaiḥ sitairhunet /
annājyābhyāṃ ca niyataṃ hutvānnāḍhyo bhavennaraḥ //
1.90.d:
तस्यां तिथौ त्रिमध्वक्तैर्मल्लिकाद्यैः सितैर्हुनेत् ।
अन्नाज्याभ्यां च नियतं हुत्वान्नाढ्यो भवेन्नरः ॥
1.90.m: On that lunar day, one should offer [in the fire] white flowers such as jasmine smeared with the three sweets. / By constantly offering food and ghee, a man becomes rich in food.

1.90.s:
yadyaddhi vāñchitaṃ vastu tattatsarvaṃ tu sarvadā /
ghṛtahomādavāpnoti tathaiva tilatandulaiḥ //
1.90.d:
यद्यद्धि वाञ्छितं वस्तु तत्तत्सर्वं तु सर्वदा ।
घृतहोमादवाप्नोति तथैव तिलतन्दुलैः ॥
1.90.m: Whatever object is desired, one attains all of that at all times / through an oblation of ghee, and likewise with sesame and rice-grains.

1.90.s:
aruṇaiḥ paṅkajairhemaṃ kurvaṃstrimadhurāplutaiḥ /
maṇḍalāllabhate lakṣmīṃ mahatīṃ ślādhyavigrahām //
1.90.d:
अरुणैः पङ्कजैर्हेमं कुर्वंस्त्रिमधुराप्लुतैः ।
मण्डलाल्लभते लक्ष्मीं महतीं श्लाध्यविग्रहाम् ॥
1.90.m: Offering oblations with red lotuses immersed in the three sweets, / one obtains great fortune and a praiseworthy body after a cycle of forty days.

1.90.s:
kahlāraiḥ kṣaudrasaṃsiktaiḥ pūrṇādyaṃ taddināvadhi /
juhuyānnityaśo bhaktyā sahasraṃ vikacaiḥ śubhaiḥ //
1.90.d:
कह्लारैः क्षौद्रसंसिक्तैः पूर्णाद्यं तद्दिनावधि ।
जुहुयान्नित्यशो भक्त्या सहस्रं विकचैः शुभैः ॥
1.90.m: Starting from the full moon day up to that day, with water-lilies sprinkled with honey, / one should constantly offer with devotion a thousand blooming, auspicious [flowers].

1.90.s:
sa tu kīrtiṃ dhanaṃ putrānprāpnuyānnātra saṃśayaḥ /
caṃpakaiḥ kṣaudrasaṃsiktaiḥ sahasrahavanāddhruvam //
1.90.d:
स तु कीर्तिं धनं पुत्रान्प्राप्नुयान्नात्र संशयः ।
चंपकैः क्षौद्रसंसिक्तैः सहस्रहवनाद्ध्रुवम् ॥
1.90.m: He indeed obtains fame, wealth, and sons, without doubt. / By offering a thousand campaka blossoms sprinkled with honey, surely,

1.90.s:
labhate svarṇaniṣkāṇāṃ śataṃ māsena nārada /
pāṭalairghṛtasaṃsiktaistrisahasraṃ hutaistathā //
1.90.d:
लभते स्वर्णनिष्काणां शतं मासेन नारद ।
पाटलैर्घृतसंसिक्तैस्त्रिसहस्रं हुतैस्तथा ॥
1.90.m: he obtains a hundred golden niṣkas within a month, O Nārada! / Likewise, by offering three thousand pāṭala flowers sprinkled with ghee,

1.90.s:
darśādimāsāllabhate citrāṇi vasanāni ca /
karpūracandanādyāni sugandhāni tu māsataḥ //
1.90.d:
दर्शादिमासाल्लभते चित्राणि वसनानि च ।
कर्पूरचन्दनाद्यानि सुगन्धानि तु मासतः ॥
1.90.m: he obtains variegated garments in a month starting from the new moon; / and within a month, fragrant substances such as camphor and sandalwood.

1.90.s:
vastūni labhate hṛdyairanyairbhogopayogibhiḥ /
śālibhiḥ kṣīrasiktābhiḥ saptamīṣu śataṃ hutam //
1.90.d:
वस्तूनि लभते हृद्यैरन्यैर्भोगोपयोगिभिः ।
शालिभिः क्षीरसिक्ताभिः सप्तमीषु शतं हुतम् ॥
1.90.m: He obtains delightful objects suitable for various enjoyments. / A hundred oblations offered on seventh lunar days with winter-rice sprinkled with milk,

1.90.s:
tena śālisamṛddhiḥ syājmāsaiḥ ṣaḍrabhirasaṃśayam /
tilairhutaistu divasairvarṣādārogyamāpnuyāt //
1.90.d:
तेन शालिसमृद्धिः स्याज्मासैः षड्रभिरसंशयम् ।
तिलैर्हुतैस्तु दिवसैर्वर्षादारोग्यमाप्नुयात् ॥
1.90.m: brings about an abundance of winter-rice within six months, undoubtedly. / By oblations of sesame seeds performed daily, one attains health within a year.

1.90.s:
svajanmarkṣatriṣu tathā dūrvābhirjjuhuyānnaraḥ /
nirātaṅko mahābhogaḥ śataṃ varṣāṇi jīvati //
1.90.d:
स्वजन्मर्क्षत्रिषु तथा दूर्वाभिर्ज्जुहुयान्नरः ।
निरातङ्को महाभोगः शतं वर्षाणि जीवति ॥
1.90.m: Likewise, on his three birth-asterisms, a man should offer dūrvā grass; / free from affliction, possessing great enjoyment, he lives for a hundred years.

1.90.s:
guḍūcītiladūrvābhistriṣu janmasu vā hunet /
tenāyuḥśrīyaśobhogapuṇyanidhyādimānbhavet //
1.90.d:
गुडूचीतिलदूर्वाभिस्त्रिषु जन्मसु वा हुनेत् ।
तेनायुःश्रीयशोभोगपुण्यनिध्यादिमान्भवेत् ॥
1.90.m: Or he should offer oblation on his three birth-asterisms with guḍūcī, sesame, and dūrvā grass; / thereby he becomes endowed with long life, fortune, fame, enjoyment, and a treasury of merit.

1.90.s:
ghṛtapāyasadugdhaistu hutaisteṣu triṣu kramāt /
āyurārogyavibhavairnṛpāmātyo bhavettathā //
1.90.d:
घृतपायसदुग्धैस्तु हुतैस्तेषु त्रिषु क्रमात् ।
आयुरारोग्यविभवैर्नृपामात्यो भवेत्तथा ॥
1.90.m: By offerings of ghee, milk-rice, and milk in those three [birth-asterisms] in succession, / endowed with long life, health, and majesty, he becomes a royal minister.

1.90.s:
saptamyāṃ kadalīhomātsaubhāgyaṃ labhate 'nvaham /
dūrvātrikaistu prādeśamānaistrisvādusaṃyutaiḥ //
1.90.d:
सप्तम्यां कदलीहोमात्सौभाग्यं लभते ऽन्वहम् ।
दूर्वात्रिकैस्तु प्रादेशमानैस्त्रिस्वादुसंयुतैः ॥
1.90.m: From offering plantains on the seventh lunar day, one obtains good fortune daily. / With triads of dūrvā grass measuring a span, combined with the three sweets,

1.90.s:
juhuyāddinaśo ghore sannipātajvare tathā /
taddineṣu japedvidyāṃ nityaśaḥ salilaṃ spṛśan //
1.90.d:
जुहुयाद्दिनशो घोरे सन्निपातज्वरे तथा ।
तद्दिनेषु जपेद्विद्यां नित्यशः सलिलं स्पृशन् ॥
1.90.m: one should offer daily in a dreadful fever caused by the vitiation of all three humours; / on those days, one should recite the mantra constantly while touching water.

1.90.s:
sahasravāraṃ tattoyaiḥ snānaṃ pānaṃ samācaret /
pākādyamapi tairava kuryādrogavimuktaye //
1.90.d:
सहस्रवारं तत्तोयैः स्नानं पानं समाचरेत् ।
पाकाद्यमपि तैरव कुर्याद्रोगविमुक्तये ॥
1.90.m: A thousand times [he recites it]; with that water one should bathe and drink; / one should also prepare food and the like with it for release from disease.

1.90.s:
sādhyarkṣavṛkṣasaṃcūrṇaṃ tryūṣaṇaṃ sarṣapaṃ tilam /
piṣṭaṃ ca sādhyapādottharajasā ca samanvitam //
1.90.d:
साध्यर्क्षवृक्षसंचूर्णं त्र्यूषणं सर्षपं तिलम् ।
पिष्टं च साध्यपादोत्थरजसा च समन्वितम् ॥
1.90.m: Powder of the tree of the target's asterism, the three pungents, mustard seeds, sesame, / and flour combined with dust from the target's foot—

1.90.s:
kṛtvā puttalikāṃ samyagdhṛdaye nāmasaṃyutām /
prāgvacchitvāyasaistīkṣṇaiḥ śastraiḥ puttalikāṃ hanet //
1.90.d:
कृत्वा पुत्तलिकां सम्यग्धृदये नामसंयुताम् ।
प्राग्वच्छित्वायसैस्तीक्ष्णैः शस्त्रैः पुत्तलिकां हनेत् ॥
1.90.m: having made an effigy properly with the [target's] name written on the chest, / as before, having cut it, he should strike the effigy with sharp iron weapons.

1.90.s:
evaṃ dinaiḥ saptabhistu sādhyo vaśyo bhaveddṛḍham /
tathāvidhāṃ puttalikāṃ kuṇḍamadhye nikhanya ca //
1.90.d:
एवं दिनैः सप्तभिस्तु साध्यो वश्यो भवेद्दृढम् ।
तथाविधां पुत्तलिकां कुण्डमध्ये निखन्य च ॥
1.90.m: Thus, within seven days, the target is firmly subjugated. / Having buried such an effigy in the middle of the fire-pit,

1.90.s:
uparyagniṃ nidhāyātha vidyayā dinaśo hunet /
trisahasraṃ triyamāyāṃ sarṣapaistadrasāplutaiḥ //
1.90.d:
उपर्यग्निं निधायाथ विद्यया दिनशो हुनेत् ।
त्रिसहस्रं त्रियमायां सर्षपैस्तद्रसाप्लुतैः ॥
1.90.m: and placing the fire above it, he should then make oblations daily with the mantra, / three thousand times during the three watches of the night, with mustard seeds soaked in its juice.

1.90.s:
śatayojanadūrādapyānayedvanitāṃ balāt /
vaśayedvanitāṃ hāeṃmātkauśikairmadhumiśritaiḥ //
1.90.d:
शतयोजनदूरादप्यानयेद्वनितां बलात् ।
वशयेद्वनितां हाएंमात्कौशिकैर्मधुमिश्रितैः ॥
1.90.m: He can forcibly bring a woman even from a distance of a hundred yojanas. / He can subjugate a woman through oblations of night-flowering jasmine mixed with honey.

1.90.s:
nālikeraphalope tairguḍairlakṣmīmavāpnuyāt /
tathājyasiktaiḥ kahlāraiḥ kṣīrāktairaruṇotpalaiḥ //
1.90.d:
नालिकेरफलोपे तैर्गुडैर्लक्ष्मीमवाप्नुयात् ।
तथाज्यसिक्तैः कह्लारैः क्षीराक्तैररुणोत्पलैः ॥
1.90.m: With jaggery accompanied by coconut fruits, he obtains fortune. / Likewise, with kahlāra water-lilies sprinkled with ghee, with red lotuses smeared with milk,

1.90.s:
trimadhvaktaiścaṃparkaśca prasūnairbakulodbhavaiḥ /
madhūkajaiḥ prasūnaiśca hutaiḥ kanyāmavāpnuyāt //
1.90.d:
त्रिमध्वक्तैश्चंपर्कश्च प्रसूनैर्बकुलोद्भवैः ।
मधूकजैः प्रसूनैश्च हुतैः कन्यामवाप्नुयात् ॥
1.90.m: with campaka flowers smeared with the three sweets, with flowers from the bakula, / and with flowers from the madhūka offered, he obtains a maiden.

1.90.s:
punnāgajairhutairvastrāṇyājyairiṣṭamavāpnuyāt /
māhiṣairmahiṣīrājairajān gavyaiśca gāstathā //
1.90.d:
पुन्नागजैर्हुतैर्वस्त्राण्याज्यैरिष्टमवाप्नुयात् ।
माहिषैर्महिषीराजैरजान् गव्यैश्च गास्तथा ॥
1.90.m: With oblations of punnāga flowers, [he obtains] garments; with ghee, he obtains his desire. / With buffalo-ghee [he obtains] she-buffaloes; with goat-ghee, goats; and with cow-ghee, cows;

1.90.s:
avāpnoti hutairājyaiḥ ratnai ratnaṃ ca sādhakaḥ /
śālipiṣṭamayīṃ kṛtvā puttalīṃ sasitāṃ tataḥ //
1.90.d:
अवाप्नोति हुतैराज्यैः रत्नै रत्नं च साधकः ।
शालिपिष्टमयीं कृत्वा पुत्तलीं ससितां ततः ॥
1.90.m: with offered ghees, the practitioner obtains jewels with gems. / Having then made an effigy consisting of rice-flour with sugar,

1.90.s:
hṛddeśanyastanāmārṇāṃ pacettailājyayorniśi /
tanmanāśca divārātrau vidyājaptāṃ tu bhakṣayet //
1.90.d:
हृद्देशन्यस्तनामार्णां पचेत्तैलाज्ययोर्निशि ।
तन्मनाश्च दिवारात्रौ विद्याजप्तां तु भक्षयेत् ॥
1.90.m: with the letters of the [target's] name placed on the heart area, he should cook it in oil and ghee at night. / Fixed upon that [person] day and night, he should eat it once it has been consecrated with the mantra.

1.90.s:
saptarātraprayogeṇa naro nārī nṛpo 'pi vā /
dāsavadvaśamāyāti cittaprāṇādi cārpayet //
1.90.d:
सप्तरात्रप्रयोगेण नरो नारी नृपो ऽपि वा ।
दासवद्वशमायाति चित्तप्राणादि चार्पयेत् ॥
1.90.m: By the application of this for seven nights, a man, a woman, or even a king / comes under control like a slave, and surrenders mind, life-breath, and all else.

1.90.s:
hayāripuṣpairaruṇaiḥ sitairvā juhuyāttathā /
trisaptarātrānmahatīmavāpnoti śriyannaraḥ //
1.90.d:
हयारिपुष्पैररुणैः सितैर्वा जुहुयात्तथा ।
त्रिसप्तरात्रान्महतीमवाप्नोति श्रियन्नरः ॥
1.90.m: Likewise, one should offer oblations with red or white oleander flowers; / after thrice seven nights, a man obtains great prosperity.

1.90.s:
chāgamāṃsaistrimadhvaktairhemātsvarṇamavāpnuyāt /
kṣīrāktaiḥ sasyasaṃpannāṃ bhuvamāpnoti maṇḍalāt //
1.90.d:
छागमांसैस्त्रिमध्वक्तैर्हेमात्स्वर्णमवाप्नुयात् ।
क्षीराक्तैः सस्यसंपन्नां भुवमाप्नोति मण्डलात् ॥
1.90.m: By offering goat meat smeared with the three sweets, he obtains gold. / With [substances] smeared with milk, he obtains within a forty-day period land abundant in crops.

1.90.s:
padmākṣairhavanāllakṣmīmavāpnoti tribhirdinaiḥ /
bilvairdaśāṃśaṃ juhuyānmantrādyaiḥ sādhane jape //
1.90.d:
पद्माक्षैर्हवनाल्लक्ष्मीमवाप्नोति त्रिभिर्दिनैः ।
बिल्वैर्दशांशं जुहुयान्मन्त्राद्यैः साधने जपे ॥
1.90.m: Through oblations of lotus-seeds, he obtains fortune in three days. / He should offer one-tenth with bilva fruits in the recitation for mastery of mantras and the like.

1.90.s:
evaṃ saṃsiddhamantrastu mantritaiśculukodakaiḥ /
phaṇidaṣṭamṛtānāṃ tu mukhe saṃtāḍya jīvayet //
1.90.d:
एवं संसिद्धमन्त्रस्तु मन्त्रितैश्चुलुकोदकैः ।
फणिदष्टमृतानां तु मुखे संताड्य जीवयेत् ॥
1.90.m: Thus, when his mantra is perfected, striking the mouths of those dead from snake-bites / with water from his cupped hands consecrated by the mantra, he brings them to life.

1.90.s:
tatkarṇayorjapanvidyāṃ yaṣṭyā vā japasiddhayā /
saṃtāḍyaśīrṣaṃ sahasā mṛtamutthāpayediti //
1.90.d:
तत्कर्णयोर्जपन्विद्यां यष्ट्या वा जपसिद्धया ।
संताड्यशीर्षं सहसा मृतमुत्थापयेदिति ॥
1.90.m: Reciting the mantra in their ears, or striking their head quickly / with a staff empowered by recitation, he raises the dead.

1.90.s:
kṛtvā yoniṃ kuṇḍamadhye tatrāgnau vidhivaddhrunet /
tilasarṣapagodhūmaśālidhānyayavairhunet //
1.90.d:
कृत्वा योनिं कुण्डमध्ये तत्राग्नौ विधिवद्ध्रुनेत् ।
तिलसर्षपगोधूमशालिधान्ययवैर्हुनेत् ॥
1.90.m: Having fashioned a vulva-shaped hearth in the middle of the fire-pit, he should offer into the fire there according to rule; / he should offer with sesame, mustard, wheat, winter-rice, grain, and barley,

1.90.s:
trimadhvaktairekaśo vā sametairvā samṛddhaye /
bakulaiścaṃpakairabjaiḥ kahlārairaruṇotpalaiḥ //
1.90.d:
त्रिमध्वक्तैरेकशो वा समेतैर्वा समृद्धये ।
बकुलैश्चंपकैरब्जैः कह्लारैररुणोत्पलैः ॥
1.90.m: smeared with the three sweets, either individually or combined together, for prosperity; / with bakula, campaka, lotuses, kahlāras, red water-lilies,

1.90.s:
kairavairmallikākundamadhūkairindirāptaye /
aśokaiḥ pāṭalairvilvairjātīvikaṅkataiḥ sitaiḥ //
1.90.d:
कैरवैर्मल्लिकाकुन्दमधूकैरिन्दिराप्तये ।
अशोकैः पाटलैर्विल्वैर्जातीविकङ्कतैः सितैः ॥
1.90.m: white water-lilies, jasmine, kunda, and madhūka, to attain fortune; / with aśoka, pāṭala, bilva, white jātī, and vikaṅkata;

1.90.s:
navanīlotpalairaśvaripujaiḥ karṇikārajaiḥ /
homāllakṣmīṃ ca saubhāgyaṃ nidhimāyuryaśo labhet //
1.90.d:
नवनीलोत्पलैरश्वरिपुजैः कर्णिकारजैः ।
होमाल्लक्ष्मीं च सौभाग्यं निधिमायुर्यशो लभेत् ॥
1.90.m: with fresh blue lotuses, oleander flowers, and flowers of the karṇikāra. / From oblations [of these], he obtains fortune, good luck, treasure, long life, and fame.

1.90.s:
dūrvāṃ guḍūcīmaśvatthaṃ vaṭamāragvadhaṃ tathā /
sitārkaplakṣajaṃ hutvā cirānmucyeta rogataḥ //
1.90.d:
दूर्वां गुडूचीमश्वत्थं वटमारग्वधं तथा ।
सितार्कप्लक्षजं हुत्वा चिरान्मुच्येत रोगतः ॥
1.90.m: Having offered dūrvā grass, guḍūcī, aśvattha, banyan, and āragvadha, / as well as the white arka and plakṣa, he is freed from disease after a long time.

1.90.s:
ikṣujaṃbūnālikeramocāguḍasitāyutaiḥ /
acalāṃ labhate lakṣmīṃ bhoktā ca bhavati dhruvam //
1.90.d:
इक्षुजंबूनालिकेरमोचागुडसितायुतैः ।
अचलां लभते लक्ष्मीं भोक्ता च भवति ध्रुवम् ॥
1.90.m: With sugarcane, jambu fruit, coconut, banana, combined with jaggery and sugar, / he obtains steady fortune, and he surely becomes an enjoyer.

1.90.s:
sarṣapājyairhute mṛtyuḥ kāṣṭhāgnau vairimṛtyave /
caturaṅgulajairhemāñcaturaṅgabale ripoḥ //
1.90.d:
सर्षपाज्यैर्हुते मृत्युः काष्ठाग्नौ वैरिमृत्यवे ।
चतुरङ्गुलजैर्हेमाञ्चतुरङ्गबले रिपोः ॥
1.90.m: When an oblation of mustard and ghee is made in a wood-fire, there is death to bring death to the enemy; / by oblations of four-finger-long [sticks] into the enemy's four-fold army,

1.90.s:
saptāhādrogaduḥkhārtirbhavatyeva na saṃśayaḥ /
nityaṃ nityārcanaṃ kuryāttathā homaṃ ghṛtena vai //
1.90.d:
सप्ताहाद्रोगदुःखार्तिर्भवत्येव न संशयः ।
नित्यं नित्यार्चनं कुर्यात्तथा होमं घृतेन वै ॥
1.90.m: within seven days affliction by disease and sorrow definitely occurs, there is no doubt. / One should daily perform the regular worship and also fire oblations with ghee.

1.90.s:
vidyābhimantritaṃ toyaṃ pibetprātastadāptaye /
candanośīrakarpūrakastūrīrocanānvitaiḥ //
1.90.d:
विद्याभिमन्त्रितं तोयं पिबेत्प्रातस्तदाप्तये ।
चन्दनोशीरकर्पूरकस्तूरीरोचनान्वितैः ॥
1.90.m: He should drink water consecrated by the mantra in the morning for that attainment. / With sandalwood, uśīra, camphor, musk, and rocanā,

1.90.s:
kāśmīrakālāgurubhirmṛgasvedamayairapi /
pūjayecca śivāmetairgandhaiḥ sarvārthasiddhaye //
1.90.d:
काश्मीरकालागुरुभिर्मृगस्वेदमयैरपि ।
पूजयेच्च शिवामेतैर्गन्धैः सर्वार्थसिद्धये ॥
1.90.m: with saffron, black agarwood, and musk, / one should worship the auspicious goddess with these perfumes for the accomplishment of all aims.

1.90.s:
sarvābhirapi nityābhiḥ prātarmātṛkayā samam /
trijaptābhiḥ pibettoyaṃ tathā vāksidvaye śivam //
1.90.d:
सर्वाभिरपि नित्याभिः प्रातर्मातृकया समम् ।
त्रिजप्ताभिः पिबेत्तोयं तथा वाक्सिद्वये शिवम् ॥
1.90.m: Recited thrice in the morning along with the phonemes and all the Nityā goddesses, / one should drink the auspicious water likewise for the perfection of speech.

1.90.s:
vidadhyātsādhanaṃ prāgvadvarṇalakṣaṃ payovrataḥ /
trisvādusiktairaruṇairaṃbujairhavanaṃ caret //
1.90.d:
विदध्यात्साधनं प्राग्वद्वर्णलक्षं पयोव्रतः ।
त्रिस्वादुसिक्तैररुणैरंबुजैर्हवनं चरेत् ॥
1.90.m: Living on milk, one should perform the practice as before, a hundred thousand times per syllable; / he should perform fire oblation with red lotuses sprinkled with the three sweets.

1.90.s:
japatarpaṇahomārcāsekasiddhamanurnaraḥ /
kuryāduktānprayogāṃśca na cettanmanudevatāḥ //
1.90.d:
जपतर्पणहोमार्चासेकसिद्धमनुर्नरः ।
कुर्यादुक्तान्प्रयोगांश्च न चेत्तन्मनुदेवताः ॥
1.90.m: A man whose mantra is perfected through recitation, water libation, fire oblation, worship, and sprinkling / may perform the stated magical rites; otherwise, the deities of that mantra

1.90.s:
prāṇāṃstasya grasaṃtyeva kupitāstatkṣaṇānmune /
anayā vidyayā loke yadasādhyaṃ na tatkvacit //
1.90.d:
प्राणांस्तस्य ग्रसंत्येव कुपितास्तत्क्षणान्मुने ।
अनया विद्यया लोके यदसाध्यं न तत्क्वचित् ॥
1.90.m: will indeed devour his life-breaths, enraged in an instant, O sage! / There is nothing in this world that cannot be accomplished by this mantra.

1.90.s:
araṇyavaṭamūle ca parvatāgraguhāsu ca /
udyānamadhyakāntāre mātṛpādapamūlataḥ //
1.90.d:
अरण्यवटमूले च पर्वताग्रगुहासु च ।
उद्यानमध्यकान्तारे मातृपादपमूलतः ॥
1.90.m: At the root of a banyan tree in the forest, in caves on mountain peaks, / in a grove in the middle of a garden, at the base of a mother-tree,

1.90.s:
siṃdhutīre vane caitā yakṣiṇīḥ sādhayennaraḥ /
kamalaiḥ kairavai raktaiḥ sitaiḥ saugandhikotpalaiḥ //
1.90.d:
सिंधुतीरे वने चैता यक्षिणीः साधयेन्नरः ।
कमलैः कैरवै रक्तैः सितैः सौगन्धिकोत्पलैः ॥
1.90.m: on the bank of a river, and in the forest, a man should master these yakṣiṇīs / with lotuses, white water-lilies, red and white fragrant water-lilies.

1.90.s:
sugandhiśiphaālikayā trimadhvaktairyathāvidhi /
homātsaptasu vāreṣu tanmaṇḍalata eva vai //
1.90.d:
सुगन्धिशिफआलिकया त्रिमध्वक्तैर्यथाविधि ।
होमात्सप्तसु वारेषु तन्मण्डलत एव वै ॥
1.90.m:
with fragrant śephālikā flowers smeared with the three sweets, through fire oblations according to rule
performed during the seven days of the week, truly from that very maṇḍala,

1.90.s:
vijayaṃ samavāproti samare dvandvayuddhake /
mallayuddhe śastrayuddhe vāde dyūtahnaye 'pi ca //
1.90.d:
विजयं समवाप्रोति समरे द्वन्द्वयुद्धके ।
मल्लयुद्धे शस्त्रयुद्धे वादे द्यूतह्नये ऽपि च ॥
1.90.m:
one attains victory in battle, in single combat,
in wrestling, in armed conflict, in debate, and in the calling of dice,

1.90.s:
vyavahāreṣu sarvatra jayamāpnoti niścitam /
caturaṅgulajaiḥ puppairhemātsaṃstaṃbhayedarīn //
1.90.d:
व्यवहारेषु सर्वत्र जयमाप्नोति निश्चितम् ।
चतुरङ्गुलजैः पुप्पैर्हेमात्संस्तंभयेदरीन् ॥
1.90.m:
and in legal disputes everywhere one definitely obtains victory.
Through fire oblations with the flowers of the caturaṅgula, one paralyzes one's enemies;

1.90.s:
tathaiva karṇikārotthaiḥ punnāgotthairnamerujaiḥ /
caṃpakaiḥ ketakai rājavṛkṣajairmādhavodbhavaiḥ //
1.90.d:
तथैव कर्णिकारोत्थैः पुन्नागोत्थैर्नमेरुजैः ।
चंपकैः केतकै राजवृक्षजैर्माधवोद्भवैः ॥
1.90.m:
likewise with those born of the karṇikāra, the punnāga, and the nameru,
with campakas, ketakas, those born of the rājavṛkṣa, and those springing from the mādhavī.

1.90.s:
prāgvaddāreṣu juhuyātkramātpuṣpaistu saptabhiḥ /
prokteṣu staṃbhanaṃ śatrorbhaṅgo vā bhavati dhruvam //
1.90.d:
प्राग्वद्दारेषु जुहुयात्क्रमात्पुष्पैस्तु सप्तभिः ।
प्रोक्तेषु स्तंभनं शत्रोर्भङ्गो वा भवति ध्रुवम् ॥
1.90.m:
As before, one should offer fire oblations on the [respective] days of the week in order with these seven flowers;
in the stated [matters], paralysis or defeat of the enemy definitely occurs.

1.90.s:
śatrornakṣatravṛkṣāgnau tatsamiddhistu homataḥ /
sarṣapājyaplutābhiste praṇamantyeva pādayoḥ //
1.90.d:
शत्रोर्नक्षत्रवृक्षाग्नौ तत्समिद्धिस्तु होमतः ।
सर्षपाज्यप्लुताभिस्ते प्रणमन्त्येव पादयोः ॥
1.90.m:
In a fire made from the wood of the enemy's birth-star tree, through fire oblation with its kindling-sticks
smeared with mustard and ghee, they bow down at one's feet.

1.90.s:
mṛtyukāṣṭhānale mṛtyupatrapuṣpaphalairapi /
samidbhirjuhuyātsamyagvāre śārcanapūrvakam //
1.90.d:
मृत्युकाष्ठानले मृत्युपत्रपुष्पफलैरपि ।
समिद्भिर्जुहुयात्सम्यग्वारे शार्चनपूर्वकम् ॥
1.90.m:
In a fire of the wood of death, one should properly offer kindling-sticks, leaves, flowers, and fruits of the death-tree
on that [inauspicious] day of the week, preceded by worship of the deity.

1.90.s:
arāteścaturaṅgaṃ tu balaṃ rogārdditaṃ bhavet /
tenāsya vijayo bhūyānnidhanenāpi vā punaḥ //
1.90.d:
अरातेश्चतुरङ्गं तु बलं रोगार्द्दितं भवेत् ।
तेनास्य विजयो भूयान्निधनेनापि वा पुनः ॥
1.90.m:
Then the enemy's fourfold army will be afflicted by disease;
by that means, or else by their death, one's victory will come to pass.

1.90.s:
arkavārer'kajairidhmaiḥ samiddhe 'gnau tadudbhavaiḥ /
patraiḥ puṣpaiḥ phalaiḥ kāṇḍairmūlaiścāpi hunetkramāt //
1.90.d:
अर्कवारेर्ऽकजैरिध्मैः समिद्धे ऽग्नौ तदुद्भवैः ।
पत्रैः पुष्पैः फलैः काण्डैर्मूलैश्चापि हुनेत्क्रमात् ॥
1.90.m:
On Sunday, in a fire kindled with fuel from the arka plant, one should offer in order
its leaves, flowers, fruits, stems, and roots

1.90.s:
savarṇāruṇavatsāyā ghṛtasiktaistu maṇḍalāt /
arātidiṅmukho bhūtvā kuṇḍe tryasre vidhānataḥ //
1.90.d:
सवर्णारुणवत्साया घृतसिक्तैस्तु मण्डलात् ।
अरातिदिङ्मुखो भूत्वा कुण्डे त्र्यस्रे विधानतः ॥
1.90.m:
smeared with ghee from a cow of uniform color with a reddish calf, from the maṇḍala,
facing the direction of the enemy, in a triangular fire-pit according to rule.

1.90.s:
palāyate vā rogārtaḥ praṇamedvā bhayānvitaḥ /
palāśedhmānale tasya pañcāṅgaistadghṛtāplutaiḥ //
1.90.d:
पलायते वा रोगार्तः प्रणमेद्वा भयान्वितः ।
पलाशेध्मानले तस्य पञ्चाङ्गैस्तद्घृताप्लुतैः ॥
1.90.m:
The enemy either flees afflicted with disease, or, filled with fear, bows down.
In a fire fueled by palāśa wood, through fire oblation with its five parts smeared with that [same] ghee,

1.90.s:
homena somavāre ca bhavetprāgvanna saṃśayaḥ /
khādiredhmānale tasya pañcāṅgaistadghṛtāplutaiḥ //
1.90.d:
होमेन सोमवारे च भवेत्प्राग्वन्न संशयः ।
खादिरेध्मानले तस्य पञ्चाङ्गैस्तद्घृताप्लुतैः ॥
1.90.m:
on Monday, the result will be as before, without a doubt.
In a fire fueled by khadira wood, through fire oblation with its five parts smeared with that ghee,

1.90.s:
vāre bhaumasya havanāttadāpnoti suniścitam /
apāmārgasya saumye 'hni pippalasya gurordine //
1.90.d:
वारे भौमस्य हवनात्तदाप्नोति सुनिश्चितम् ।
अपामार्गस्य सौम्ये ऽह्नि पिप्पलस्य गुरोर्दिने ॥
1.90.m:
on Tuesday, one definitely achieves that result.
With the apāmārga on Wednesday, with the pippala on Thursday,

1.90.s:
uduṃbarasya bhṛguje śamyā mānde 'hni goghṛtaiḥ /
śubhrapītasitaśyāmavarṇādyāḥ pūrvavattathā //
1.90.d:
उदुंबरस्य भृगुजे शम्या मान्दे ऽह्नि गोघृतैः ।
शुभ्रपीतसितश्यामवर्णाद्याः पूर्ववत्तथा ॥
1.90.m:
with the udumbara on Friday, and with the śamī on Saturday, using cow's ghee
[from cows] of white, yellow, white, and dark colors respectively, as before,

1.90.s:
tatphalaṃ samavāpnoti tatsamiddīpite 'nale /
pratipattithimārabhya pañcamyantaṃ krameṇa vai //
1.90.d:
तत्फलं समवाप्नोति तत्समिद्दीपिते ऽनले ।
प्रतिपत्तिथिमारभ्य पञ्चम्यन्तं क्रमेण वै ॥
1.90.m:
one obtains that result in a fire kindled by fuel from those [trees].
Beginning from the first lunar day and up to the fifth lunar day in succession,

1.90.s:
śālīcaṇakamudgaiśca yavamāṣaiśca homataḥ /
māhiṣājyaplutaistābhistithibhiḥ samavāpnuyāt //
1.90.d:
शालीचणकमुद्गैश्च यवमाषैश्च होमतः ।
माहिषाज्यप्लुतैस्ताभिस्तिथिभिः समवाप्नुयात् ॥
1.90.m:
through fire oblations of winter rice, chickpeas, mung beans, barley, and black gram,
smeared with buffalo ghee on those lunar days, one obtains [that result].

1.90.s:
ṣaṣṭhyādisaptamyantaṃ tu cājābhavaghṛtaistathā /
prāguktairnistuṣairhemātprāguktaphalamāpnuyāt //
1.90.d:
षष्ठ्यादिसप्तम्यन्तं तु चाजाभवघृतैस्तथा ।
प्रागुक्तैर्निस्तुषैर्हेमात्प्रागुक्तफलमाप्नुयात् ॥
1.90.m:
From the sixth up to the seventh lunar day, with goat ghee
and the previously mentioned husked grains, through fire oblation one obtains the previously stated fruit.

1.90.s:
tadvarddhaṃ pañcake tvetaiḥ samastaiśca tiladvayaiḥ /
sitānnaiḥ pāyasaiḥ siktairāvikaistu ghṛtaistathā //
1.90.d:
तद्वर्द्धं पञ्चके त्वेतैः समस्तैश्च तिलद्वयैः ।
सितान्नैः पायसैः सिक्तैराविकैस्तु घृतैस्तथा ॥
1.90.m:
In that half-part, during the five [days], with all these together and both kinds of sesame,
sprinkled with white cooked rice, milk-rice, and sheep's ghee,

1.90.s:
havanāttadavāpnoti yadādau phalamīritam /
evaṃ nakṣatravṛkṣotthavahnau taistairmadhuplutaiḥ //
1.90.d:
हवनात्तदवाप्नोति यदादौ फलमीरितम् ।
एवं नक्षत्रवृक्षोत्थवह्नौ तैस्तैर्मधुप्लुतैः ॥
1.90.m:
through fire oblation one obtains that fruit which was spoken of at the beginning.
In this way, in a fire produced from the birth-star tree, through fire oblation

1.90.s:
havanādapi tatprāptirbhavatyeva na saṃśayaḥ /
vidyāṃ saṃsādhya pūrvaṃ tu paścāduktānaśeṣataḥ //
1.90.d:
हवनादपि तत्प्राप्तिर्भवत्येव न संशयः ।
विद्यां संसाध्य पूर्वं तु पश्चादुक्तानशेषतः ॥
1.90.m:
with those various [substances] smeared with honey, that attainment definitely comes to pass, without doubt.
Having first accomplished the vidyā, the wise man should subsequently accomplish in full

1.90.s:
prayogānsādhayeddhīmān maṅgalāyāḥ prasādataḥ /
saṃpūjya devatāṃ viprakumārīṃ kanyakāṃ tu vā //
1.90.d:
प्रयोगान्साधयेद्धीमान् मङ्गलायाः प्रसादतः ।
संपूज्य देवतां विप्रकुमारीं कन्यकां तु वा ॥
1.90.m:
the ritual applications through the favor of Maṅgalā.
Having worshipped the deity, or a brahmin virgin girl,

1.90.s:
saśubhāvayavāṃ mugdhāṃ snātāṃ dhautāṃbarāṃ śubhām /
tathāvidhaṃ kumāraṃ vā saṃsthāpyabhyarcya vidyayā //
1.90.d:
सशुभावयवां मुग्धां स्नातां धौतांबरां शुभाम् ।
तथाविधं कुमारं वा संस्थाप्यभ्यर्च्य विद्यया ॥
1.90.m:
endowed with auspicious limbs, innocent, bathed, wearing washed garments, auspicious,
or a young boy of the same kind, seating them and worshipping them with the vidyā,

1.90.s:
spṛṣṭaśīrṣo japedvidyāṃ śatavāraṃ tathārcayet /
prasūnairaruṇaiḥ śubhraiḥ saurabhāḍhyairathāpi vā //
1.90.d:
स्पृष्टशीर्षो जपेद्विद्यां शतवारं तथार्चयेत् ।
प्रसूनैररुणैः शुभ्रैः सौरभाढ्यैरथापि वा ॥
1.90.m:
touching the head, one should recite the vidyā a hundred times and worship in that way
with red, white, or delightfully fragrant blossoms.

1.90.s:
dadyādgugguladhūpaṃ ca yāvatkarmāvasānakam /
tato devyā samāviṣṭe tasminsaṃpūjya bhaktitaḥ //
1.90.d:
दद्याद्गुग्गुलधूपं च यावत्कर्मावसानकम् ।
ततो देव्या समाविष्टे तस्मिन्संपूज्य भक्तितः ॥
1.90.m:
One should offer guggulu incense until the completion of the rite.
Then, when the child is possessed by the goddess, worshipping her with devotion,

1.90.s:
tatastāmupacāraistaiḥ prāguktairvidyayā vratī /
prajapaṃstāṃ tataḥ pṛcchedabhīṣṭaṃ kathayecca sā //
1.90.d:
ततस्तामुपचारैस्तैः प्रागुक्तैर्विद्यया व्रती ।
प्रजपंस्तां ततः पृच्छेदभीष्टं कथयेच्च सा ॥
1.90.m:
and then [worshipping] her with the previously stated articles of worship through the vidyā, the observer of the vow,
reciting [the mantra], should then ask her the desired matter, and she will speak:

1.90.s:
bhūtaṃ bhavadbhaviṣyaṃ ca yadanyanmanasi sthitam /
janmāntarāṇyatītāni sarvaṃ sā pūjitā vadet //
1.90.d:
भूतं भवद्भविष्यं च यदन्यन्मनसि स्थितम् ।
जन्मान्तराण्यतीतानि सर्वं सा पूजिता वदेत् ॥
1.90.m:
past, present, and future, and whatever else is in one's mind,
as well as past lifetimes—worshipped, she will declare it all.

1.90.s:
tatastāṃ prāgvadabhyarcya svātmanyudvāsya tāṃ japet /
sahasravāraṃ sthiradhīḥ pūrṇātmā vicaretsukhī //
1.90.d:
ततस्तां प्राग्वदभ्यर्च्य स्वात्मन्युद्वास्य तां जपेत् ।
सहस्रवारं स्थिरधीः पूर्णात्मा विचरेत्सुखी ॥
1.90.m:
Then, having worshipped her as before, and dismissing her into oneself, one should recite it
a thousand times with a steady mind; fulfilled in self, one wanders happily.

1.90.s:
madhuratrayasaṃsiktairaruṇairaṃbajaiḥ śriyam /
prāpnoti maṇḍalaṃ homātsitaiśca mahadyaśaḥ //
1.90.d:
मधुरत्रयसंसिक्तैररुणैरंबजैः श्रियम् ।
प्राप्नोति मण्डलं होमात्सितैश्च महद्यशः ॥
1.90.m:
Through fire oblation with red lotuses sprinkled with the three sweets,
one attains fortune for a maṇḍala period, and with white ones, great fame.

1.90.s:
kṣaudrāktairuptalai raktairhavanātproktakālataḥ /
suvarṇaṃ samavāpnoti nidhiṃ vā vasudhāṃ tu vā //
1.90.d:
क्षौद्राक्तैरुप्तलै रक्तैर्हवनात्प्रोक्तकालतः ।
सुवर्णं समवाप्नोति निधिं वा वसुधां तु वा ॥
1.90.m:
Through fire oblation with red lotuses smeared with honey at the stated time,
one obtains gold, or a treasure, or land.

1.90.s:
kṣīrāktaiḥ kairavairhemātproktaṃ kāmamavāpnuyāt /
dhānyāni vividhānyāśu subhagaḥ sa bhavennaraḥ //
1.90.d:
क्षीराक्तैः कैरवैर्हेमात्प्रोक्तं काममवाप्नुयात् ।
धान्यानि विविधान्याशु सुभगः स भवेन्नरः ॥
1.90.m:
Through fire oblation with white water lilies smeared with milk, one attains the desired wish;
that man quickly gains various grains and becomes charming.

1.90.s:
ājyāktairutpalairhemādvāñchitaṃ samavāpnuyāt /
tadaktairapi kahlārairhavanādrājavallabhaḥ //
1.90.d:
आज्याक्तैरुत्पलैर्हेमाद्वाञ्छितं समवाप्नुयात् ।
तदक्तैरपि कह्लारैर्हवनाद्राजवल्लभः ॥
1.90.m:
Through fire oblation with blue lotuses smeared with ghee, one obtains what is desired;
and through fire oblation with white water lilies smeared with it, one becomes beloved of kings.

1.90.s:
palāśapuṣpaistrisvāduyuktaistatkālahomataḥ /
caturvidhaṃ tu pāṇḍityaṃ bhavatyeva na saṃśayaḥ //
1.90.d:
पलाशपुष्पैस्त्रिस्वादुयुक्तैस्तत्कालहोमतः ।
चतुर्विधं तु पाण्डित्यं भवत्येव न संशयः ॥
1.90.m:
Through fire oblation at that time with palāśa flowers accompanied by the three sweets,
fourfold scholarship definitely arises, without a doubt.

1.90.s:
lājaistrimadhuropetaistatkālahavanena vai /
kanyakāṃ labhate patnīṃ samastaguṇasaṃyutām //
1.90.d:
लाजैस्त्रिमधुरोपेतैस्तत्कालहवनेन वै ।
कन्यकां लभते पत्नीं समस्तगुणसंयुताम् ॥
1.90.m:
Through fire oblation at that time with parched grain endowed with the three sweets,
one obtains a maiden wife endowed with all good qualities.

1.90.s:
nālikeraphalakṣodaṃ sasitaṃ saguḍaṃ tu vā /
kṣaudrākṣaṃ juhuyāttadvadayatnāddhanadopamaḥ //
1.90.d:
नालिकेरफलक्षोदं ससितं सगुडं तु वा ।
क्षौद्राक्षं जुहुयात्तद्वदयत्नाद्धनदोपमः ॥
1.90.m:
One should offer coconut-fruit shreds with sugar or molasses,
smeared with honey, in the same way; effortlessly, he becomes like the Giver of Wealth [Kubera].

1.90.s:
tathaivānnājyahomena satandulatilairapi /
prasūnairaruṇaistadvattathā bandhūkasaṃbhavaiḥ //
1.90.d:
तथैवान्नाज्यहोमेन सतन्दुलतिलैरपि ।
प्रसूनैररुणैस्तद्वत्तथा बन्धूकसंभवैः ॥
1.90.m:
Likewise, through fire oblation of cooked food and ghee with rice-grains and sesame seeds,
and similarly with red blossoms, as well as those born of the bandhūka,

1.90.s:
sitaiḥ prasūnarvāksiddhiṃ havanātsamavāpnuyāt /
sitaraktaistumilitairāyurārogyamāpnuyāt //
1.90.d:
सितैः प्रसूनर्वाक्सिद्धिं हवनात्समवाप्नुयात् ।
सितरक्तैस्तुमिलितैरायुरारोग्यमाप्नुयात् ॥
1.90.m:
and with white blossoms, one obtains mastery of speech through fire oblation;
with white and red mingled together, one obtains longevity and health.

1.90.s:
dūrvātrikaistrimadhvaktairhavanāttu jayecca tān /
tathā guḍūcyā homena pāyasena tilena ca //
1.90.d:
दूर्वात्रिकैस्त्रिमध्वक्तैर्हवनात्तु जयेच्च तान् ।
तथा गुडूच्या होमेन पायसेन तिलेन च ॥
1.90.m:
Through fire oblation with triads of dūrvā grass smeared with the three sweets, one conquers them;
likewise, through fire oblation with guḍūcī, milk-rice, and sesame seeds,

1.90.s:
śrīkhaṇḍapaṅkakarpūramilitaiḥ śatapatrakaiḥ /
havanācchriyamāpnoti yāvadanvayagā bhavet //
1.90.d:
श्रीखण्डपङ्ककर्पूरमिलितैः शतपत्रकैः ।
हवनाच्छ्रियमाप्नोति यावदन्वयगा भवेत् ॥
1.90.m:
and through fire oblation with hundred-petaled lotuses mixed with sandalwood paste and camphor,
one attains fortune that lasts as long as one's lineage persists.

1.90.s:
kuṅkumaṃ himatoyena piṣṭvā karpūrasaṃyutam /
tatpaṅka mardditairhemātkahlārairvikacaiḥ sumaiḥ //
1.90.d:
कुङ्कुमं हिमतोयेन पिष्ट्वा कर्पूरसंयुतम् ।
तत्पङ्क मर्द्दितैर्हेमात्कह्लारैर्विकचैः सुमैः ॥
1.90.m:
Having ground saffron with cool water combined with camphor,
through fire oblation with blooming kahlāra flowers rubbed with that paste,

1.90.s:
rājakalpaḥ śriyā bhūyājjīvedvarṣaśataṃ bhuvi /
niḥsapatno nirātaṅko nirdrando nirmalāśayaḥ //
1.90.d:
राजकल्पः श्रिया भूयाज्जीवेद्वर्षशतं भुवि ।
निःसपत्नो निरातङ्को निर्द्रन्दो निर्मलाशयः ॥
1.90.m:
one becomes equal to a king in fortune, lives a hundred years on earth,
free of rivals, free of affliction, free of dualities, and of pure mind.

1.90.s:
ikṣukāṇḍasya śakalairhavanādvastramāpnuyāt /
tathaiva karavīrotthaiḥ prasūnairaruṇaiḥ sitaiḥ //
1.90.d:
इक्षुकाण्डस्य शकलैर्हवनाद्वस्त्रमाप्नुयात् ।
तथैव करवीरोत्थैः प्रसूनैररुणैः सितैः ॥
1.90.m:
Through fire oblation with pieces of sugarcane, one obtains clothing;
likewise with red and white blossoms originating from the karavīra.

1.90.s:
kṣaudrāktaiḥ pāṭalāpuṣpairhavanādvaśayedvadhūḥ /
tathaiva paṅkajairhemādrūpājīvāṃ vaśaṃ nayet //
1.90.d:
क्षौद्राक्तैः पाटलापुष्पैर्हवनाद्वशयेद्वधूः ।
तथैव पङ्कजैर्हेमाद्रूपाजीवां वशं नयेत् ॥
1.90.m:
Through fire oblation with pāṭalā flowers smeared with honey, one subjugates brides;
likewise through fire oblation with lotuses, one brings a courtesan under control.

1.90.s:
sarūpavatsāsitagokṣīrāktasitahomataḥ /
labhate 'nupamāṃ lakṣmīmapi pāpiṣṭhacetanaḥ //
1.90.d:
सरूपवत्सासितगोक्षीराक्तसितहोमतः ।
लभते ऽनुपमां लक्ष्मीमपि पापिष्ठचेतनः ॥
1.90.m:
Through fire oblation of white [flowers] smeared with the milk of a white cow with a calf of identical appearance,
even a person of sinful mind obtains peerless fortune.

1.90.s:
sauvīrāktaistu kārpāsabījastatkālahomataḥ /
arddhendukuṇḍe niyataṃ vaśagā ripavo mune //
1.90.d:
सौवीराक्तैस्तु कार्पासबीजस्तत्कालहोमतः ।
अर्द्धेन्दुकुण्डे नियतं वशगा रिपवो मुने ॥
1.90.m:
Through fire oblation at that time of cotton seeds smeared with sour gruel
in a crescent-shaped fire-pit, enemies are surely brought under control, O sage.

1.90.s:
ariṣṭapatraistadbījaistadvahnau taistathā hutaiḥ /
mṛtyubījairnimbatailasiktairhemānnihṝnti tān //
1.90.d:
अरिष्टपत्रैस्तद्बीजैस्तद्वह्नौ तैस्तथा हुतैः ।
मृत्युबीजैर्निम्बतैलसिक्तैर्हेमान्निहॄन्ति तान् ॥
1.90.m:
Through those leaves of the ariṣṭa tree and its seeds offered into that fire,
and through fire oblation with seeds of the death-tree smeared with neem oil, he slays them;

1.90.s:
rogārtāṃsturagāṃstadvatpañcagavyairhutairdhruvam /
akṣabījaistu tailāktairhemaḥ sarvavināśanaḥ //
1.90.d:
रोगार्तांस्तुरगांस्तद्वत्पञ्चगव्यैर्हुतैर्ध्रुवम् ।
अक्षबीजैस्तु तैलाक्तैर्हेमः सर्वविनाशनः ॥
1.90.m:
likewise, horses afflicted by disease [are cured] through fire oblations of pañcagavya, definitely.
A fire oblation with akṣa seeds smeared with oil causes total destruction.

1.90.s:
karañjabījaiḥ saṃsiktairhemādvairī piśācavān /
tathaivākṣatarūdbhūtapañcāṅgahavanādapi //
1.90.d:
करञ्जबीजैः संसिक्तैर्हेमाद्वैरी पिशाचवान् ।
तथैवाक्षतरूद्भूतपञ्चाङ्गहवनादपि ॥
1.90.m:
Through fire oblation with smeared karañja seeds, an enemy is possessed by a piśāca;
likewise also through fire oblation of the five parts originating from the akṣata tree.

1.90.s:
niṃbatailānvitairakṣadrumabījaistu homataḥ /
taddine syādapasmārī vairī bhavati niścitam //
1.90.d:
निंबतैलान्वितैरक्षद्रुमबीजैस्तु होमतः ।
तद्दिने स्यादपस्मारी वैरी भवति निश्चितम् ॥
1.90.m: By offering [in fire] the seeds of the akṣa tree combined with neem oil, / on that very day the enemy certainly becomes an epileptic.

1.90.s:
arāterjanmanakṣatravṛkṣendhanagate 'nale /
tadyonipiśitaistaiśca havanānmṛtyukṛdripoḥ //
1.90.d:
अरातेर्जन्मनक्षत्रवृक्षेन्धनगते ऽनले ।
तद्योनिपिशितैस्तैश्च हवनान्मृत्युकृद्रिपोः ॥
1.90.m: When the fire is fed with wood from the tree of the enemy's birth-star, / by offering the meat of the animal belonging to that [star's] category, death is inflicted on the enemy.

1.90.s:
padmākṣabījaiḥ sarṣapatailāktairhavanāttathā /
jāyante vairiṇaḥ kuṣṭharogā dehavilopakāḥ //
1.90.d:
पद्माक्षबीजैः सर्षपतैलाक्तैर्हवनात्तथा ।
जायन्ते वैरिणः कुष्ठरोगा देहविलोपकाः ॥
1.90.m: Likewise, from the offering of lotus seeds smeared with mustard oil, / leprosy diseases that ruin the body arise for the enemy.

1.90.s:
maricaiḥ sarṣapairhemāttailāktairmadhyarājake /
dāhajvareṇa grastaḥ syādarātistaddine dhruvam //
1.90.d:
मरिचैः सर्षपैर्हेमात्तैलाक्तैर्मध्यराजके ।
दाहज्वरेण ग्रस्तः स्यादरातिस्तद्दिने ध्रुवम् ॥
1.90.m: From offering black pepper smeared with mustard oil at midnight, / the enemy will surely be afflicted with a burning fever on that very day.

1.90.s:
evaṃ nigrahahomeṣu svarakṣāyai tathānvaham /
snigdhaiḥ saṃprāptasadvidyairjapahomādi kārayet //
1.90.d:
एवं निग्रहहोमेषु स्वरक्षायै तथान्वहम् ।
स्निग्धैः संप्राप्तसद्विद्यैर्जपहोमादि कारयेत् ॥
1.90.m: In this way, during fire oblations of subjugation, for self-protection every day, / one should have recitation, fire oblations, and the like performed by friendly people who have acquired the true knowledge,

1.90.s:
mṛtyuñjayena vā tattatprayogasthābhireva vā /
vidyābhiranyathāsiddhamantramasyāśu nāśayet //
1.90.d:
मृत्युञ्जयेन वा तत्तत्प्रयोगस्थाभिरेव वा ।
विद्याभिरन्यथासिद्धमन्त्रमस्याशु नाशयेत् ॥
1.90.m: or through the Mṛtyuñjaya [mantra], or through the mantras belonging to those respective rituals; / one should swiftly destroy his counter-effective accomplished mantra.

1.90.s:
lakṣatrayaṃ kṛte proktaṃ tretāyāṃ dviguṇaṃ tathā /
dvāpare triguṇaṃ proktaṃ kalautattu caturguṇam //
1.90.d:
लक्षत्रयं कृते प्रोक्तं त्रेतायां द्विगुणं तथा ।
द्वापरे त्रिगुणं प्रोक्तं कलौतत्तु चतुर्गुणम् ॥
1.90.m: Three hundred thousand [recitations] are prescribed in the Kṛta age, twice that in the Tretā, / thrice that is declared in the Dvāpara, and four times that in the Kali.

1.90.s:
daśāṃśaṃ havanaṃ kāryaṃ tarpaṇaṃ taddaśāṃśataḥ /
taddaśāṃśaṃ mārjanaṃ syāddaśāṃśaṃ dvijabhojanam //
1.90.d:
दशांशं हवनं कार्यं तर्पणं तद्दशांशतः ।
तद्दशांशं मार्जनं स्याद्दशांशं द्विजभोजनम् ॥
1.90.m: A tenth part should be done as fire oblation, and water offering a tenth part of that; / a tenth of that should be sprinkling, and a tenth [of that] feeding the twice-born.

1.90.s:
evaṃ krameṇa sarvāsāṃ yā yā saṃkhyā japasya sā /
kāryā siddhyai tu vidyāyāstataḥ kuryātprayogakān //
1.90.d:
एवं क्रमेण सर्वासां या या संख्या जपस्य सा ।
कार्या सिद्ध्यै तु विद्यायास्ततः कुर्यात्प्रयोगकान् ॥
1.90.m: In this order, whatever is the number of recitation for all [the mantras], / that should be performed for the attainment of the mantra; then one should perform the rituals.

1.90.s:
dviguṇo hi japaḥ kāryaḥ kāmeśvaryā munīśvara /
siddhe mantre prayogāṃstu vidadhīta yathā tathā //
1.90.d:
द्विगुणो हि जपः कार्यः कामेश्वर्या मुनीश्वर ।
सिद्धे मन्त्रे प्रयोगांस्तु विदधीत यथा तथा ॥
1.90.m: A double recitation should indeed be performed for Kāmeśvarī, O lord of sages; / once the mantra is accomplished, one may carry out the rituals as prescribed.

1.90.s:
japo lakṣaṃ samākhyāto homādistaddhaśāṃśataḥ /
kartavyo bhagamālāyā vidyāsiddhyaimunīśvara //
1.90.d:
जपो लक्षं समाख्यातो होमादिस्तद्धशांशतः ।
कर्तव्यो भगमालाया विद्यासिद्ध्यैमुनीश्वर ॥
1.90.m: The recitation of Bhagamālā is declared to be one hundred thousand, and fire oblation and the rest a tenth of that; / it should be performed for the attainment of the mantra, O lord of sages.

1.90.s:
nityaklinnājapaḥ prokto lakṣaṃ homo haśāṃśataḥ /
kāryaḥ siddhyai tu vidyāyāḥ prayogānsādhayettataḥ //
1.90.d:
नित्यक्लिन्नाजपः प्रोक्तो लक्षं होमो हशांशतः ।
कार्यः सिद्ध्यै तु विद्यायाः प्रयोगान्साधयेत्ततः ॥
1.90.m: The recitation of Nityaklinnā is declared as one hundred thousand, and fire oblation a tenth part; / it should be performed for the attainment of the mantra, and then one should execute the rituals.

1.90.s:
tato maunī payobhakṣaḥ prajapennavalakṣakam /
bheruḍāmantramuktaṃ tu śeṣaṃ kuryātprayatnataḥ //
1.90.d:
ततो मौनी पयोभक्षः प्रजपेन्नवलक्षकम् ।
भेरुडामन्त्रमुक्तं तु शेषं कुर्यात्प्रयत्नतः ॥
1.90.m: Then, maintaining silence and subsisting on milk, he should recite nine hundred thousand [times] / what has been spoken of as the Bheruḍā mantra; he should perform the rest with care.

1.90.s:
lakṣatrayaṃ japo vahnivāsinyāḥ samudīritaḥ /
anyatsarvaṃ purāvacca kāryyaṃ sādhakasattamaiḥ //
1.90.d:
लक्षत्रयं जपो वह्निवासिन्याः समुदीरितः ।
अन्यत्सर्वं पुरावच्च कार्य्यं साधकसत्तमैः ॥
1.90.m: The recitation for Vahnivāsinī is stated to be three hundred thousand; / everything else should be performed as before by the best of practitioners.

1.90.s:
mahāvajreśvarīvidyājapo lakṣatrayo mataḥ /
havanādi daśāṃśena kāryaṃ proktakrameṇa hi //
1.90.d:
महावज्रेश्वरीविद्याजपो लक्षत्रयो मतः ।
हवनादि दशांशेन कार्यं प्रोक्तक्रमेण हि ॥
1.90.m: The recitation of the Mahāvajreśvarī mantra is considered to be three hundred thousand; / fire oblation and the rest are to be performed with a tenth part, indeed according to the stated procedure.

1.90.s:
atandrito japellakṣamitaṃ dūtīmanuṃ mune /
taddaśāṃśakrameṇaiva homādiḥ proktamārgataḥ //
1.90.d:
अतन्द्रितो जपेल्लक्षमितं दूतीमनुं मुने ।
तद्दशांशक्रमेणैव होमादिः प्रोक्तमार्गतः ॥
1.90.m: Unwearied, O sage, one should recite the Dūtī mantra to the amount of one hundred thousand; / fire oblation and the rest are to be done in the order of a tenth of that, according to the stated path.

1.90.s:
tvaritāṃ prajapellakṣapramitāṃ taddaśāṃśataḥ /
kṛtvā homādikaṃ sarvaṃ vidyāsiddhiyaimunīśvara //
1.90.d:
त्वरितां प्रजपेल्लक्षप्रमितां तद्दशांशतः ।
कृत्वा होमादिकं सर्वं विद्यासिद्धियैमुनीश्वर ॥
1.90.m: He should recite Tvaritā to the amount of one hundred thousand, / having performed all [rites] such as fire oblation with a tenth of that, for the attainment of the mantra, O lord of sages.

1.90.s:
japo lakṣaṃ samākhyāto homādistaddaśāṃśataḥ /
vidyāyāḥ kulasundaryāḥ kartavyo dvijasattama //
1.90.d:
जपो लक्षं समाख्यातो होमादिस्तद्दशांशतः ।
विद्यायाः कुलसुन्दर्याः कर्तव्यो द्विजसत्तम ॥
1.90.m: The recitation of the mantra of Kulasundarī is declared to be one hundred thousand, and fire oblation and the rest a tenth of that; / it should be performed, O best of the twice-born.

1.90.s:
nityānityājapo vipratrilakṣapramito mataḥ /
homādistaddaśāṃśena proktaḥ proktavidhānataḥ //
1.90.d:
नित्यानित्याजपो विप्रत्रिलक्षप्रमितो मतः ।
होमादिस्तद्दशांशेन प्रोक्तः प्रोक्तविधानतः ॥
1.90.m: The recitation of Nityā and Anityā, O brāhmaṇa, is considered to measure three hundred thousand; / fire oblation and the rest are declared as a tenth of that according to the stated procedure.

1.90.s:
tripañcāśallakṣamukto niyamena munīśvara /
japo nityapatākāyā homādistaddaśāṃśataḥ //
1.90.d:
त्रिपञ्चाशल्लक्षमुक्तो नियमेन मुनीश्वर ।
जपो नित्यपताकाया होमादिस्तद्दशांशतः ॥
1.90.m: The recitation of Nityapatākā is declared with observance, O lord of sages, / to be fifty-three hundred thousand [times], and fire oblation and the rest a tenth of that.

1.90.s:
vijayāyā jayaḥ prokto lakṣamānena nārada /
anyatpūrvavadākhyātaṃ vidyāsiddhyai tu sādhanam //
1.90.d:
विजयाया जयः प्रोक्तो लक्षमानेन नारद ।
अन्यत्पूर्ववदाख्यातं विद्यासिद्ध्यै तु साधनम् ॥
1.90.m: The recitation of Vijayā is declared to the measure of one hundred thousand, O Nārada; / the rest of the practice for the attainment of the mantra is explained as before.

1.90.s:
dantalakṣapramāṇena sarvamaṅgālikāṃ japet /
taddaśāṃśakrameṇaiva homādi samudīritam //
1.90.d:
दन्तलक्षप्रमाणेन सर्वमङ्गालिकां जपेत् ।
तद्दशांशक्रमेणैव होमादि समुदीरितम् ॥
1.90.m: One should recite Sarvamaṅgalā to the measure of thirty-two hundred thousand; / fire oblation and the rest are spoken of in the sequence of a tenth of that.

1.90.s:
aṣṭalakṣaṃ haviṣyāśī jvālāmālinikāṃ japet /
homādistaddaśāṃśena proktadravyaiḥ samīritaḥ //
1.90.d:
अष्टलक्षं हविष्याशी ज्वालामालिनिकां जपेत् ।
होमादिस्तद्दशांशेन प्रोक्तद्रव्यैः समीरितः ॥
1.90.m: Subsisting on sacrificial food, one should recite Jvālāmālinī eight hundred thousand [times]; / fire oblation and the rest are stated to be a tenth of that, using the prescribed substances.

1.90.s:
citrāyā bhūpalakṣaṃ tu japo homādikastataḥ /
proktena vidhinā kāryo vidyāsiddhyai munīśvara //
1.90.d:
चित्राया भूपलक्षं तु जपो होमादिकस्ततः ।
प्रोक्तेन विधिना कार्यो विद्यासिद्ध्यै मुनीश्वर ॥
1.90.m: The recitation of Citrā is sixteen hundred thousand; then fire oblation and the rest / should be performed according to the stated procedure for the attainment of the mantra, O lord of sages.

1.90.s:
etatsaṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ nityāpaṭalamādita /
jñātavyaṃ sarvamevātra yantrasādhanapūrvakam //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne tṛtīyapāde nityāpaṭalakathanaṃ nāma navatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.90.d:
एतत्संक्षेपतः प्रोक्तं नित्यापटलमादित ।
ज्ञातव्यं सर्वमेवात्र यन्त्रसाधनपूर्वकम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने तृतीयपादे नित्यापटलकथनं नाम नवतितमो ऽध्यायः
1.90.m:
This chapter on the Nityās has been declared in brief from the beginning; / all this is to be known here following the practice with the diagram.

Thus ends the ninetieth chapter, named 'The Discourse on the Chapter of the Nityās', in the third quarter of the Great Narrative in the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.91.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca
atha vakṣye maheśasya mantraṃ sarvārthasādhakam /
yaṃ samārādhya manujo bhuktiṃ muktiṃ ca vindati //
1.91.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
अथ वक्ष्ये महेशस्य मन्त्रं सर्वार्थसाधकम् ।
यं समाराध्य मनुजो भुक्तिं मुक्तिं च विन्दति ॥
1.91.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Now I shall speak of the mantra of Maheśa, which accomplishes all purposes, / by propitiating which a mortal attains both worldly enjoyment and liberation.

1.91.s:
hṛdayaṃ sabakaḥ sūkṣmo lānto 'nantānvito marut /
pañcākṣaro manuḥ proktastārādyo 'yaṃ ṣaḍakṣaraḥ //
1.91.d:
हृदयं सबकः सूक्ष्मो लान्तो ऽनन्तान्वितो मरुत् ।
पञ्चाक्षरो मनुः प्रोक्तस्ताराद्यो ऽयं षडक्षरः ॥
1.91.m:
The heart [namaḥ], [then] Śabaka [śi], subtle [va], the l-ending with Ananta [ya], and the wind [om]—
this is stated to be the five-syllable mantra; with Tāra [oṃ] at the beginning, it is six-syllabled.

1.91.s:
vāmadevī munīśchandaḥ paṅktirīśo 'sya devatā /
ṣaḍbhirvarṇaiḥ ṣaḍaṅgāni kuryānmantreṇa deśikaḥ //
1.91.d:
वामदेवी मुनीश्छन्दः पङ्क्तिरीशो ऽस्य देवता ।
षड्भिर्वर्णैः षडङ्गानि कुर्यान्मन्त्रेण देशिकः ॥
1.91.m:
Vāmadeva is the sage, the metre is paṅkti, and Īśa is its deity.
With its six syllables, the preceptor should perform the six limbs through the mantra.

1.91.s:
mantravarṇādikānnyasyenmantramūrtiryathākramam /
tarjanīmadhyayorantyānāmikāṅguṣṭhake punaḥ //
1.91.d:
मन्त्रवर्णादिकान्न्यस्येन्मन्त्रमूर्तिर्यथाक्रमम् ।
तर्जनीमध्ययोरन्त्यानामिकाङ्गुष्ठके पुनः ॥
1.91.m:
A person embodying the mantra should place the syllables of the mantra and the rest in order:
on the forefinger and middle finger, then on the little finger, the ring finger, and the thumb.

1.91.s:
tāḥ syustatpuruṣāghorabhavavāmeśasaṃjñikāḥ /
vaktrahṛtpādaguhyeṣu nijamūrddhani tāḥ punaḥ //
1.91.d:
ताः स्युस्तत्पुरुषाघोरभववामेशसंज्ञिकाः ।
वक्त्रहृत्पादगुह्येषु निजमूर्द्धनि ताः पुनः ॥
1.91.m:
These [fingers] bear the names of Tatpuruṣa, Aghora, Sadyojāta, Vāmadeva, and Īśāna.
Then, [he should place] them on his own head, face, heart, feet, and privities,

1.91.s:
prāgyāmyavāruṇodīcyamadhyavaktreṣu pañcasu /
mantrāṅgāninyasetpaścājjātiyuktāni ṣaṭ kramāt //
1.91.d:
प्राग्याम्यवारुणोदीच्यमध्यवक्त्रेषु पञ्चसु ।
मन्त्राङ्गानिन्यसेत्पश्चाज्जातियुक्तानि षट् क्रमात् ॥
1.91.m:
on the five faces: eastern, southern, western, northern, and central.
Thereafter, he should place in order the six limbs of the mantra endowed with their ritual calls.

1.91.s:
kurvīta golakanyāsaṃ rakṣāyai tadanantaram /
hṛdi vaktreṃ'sayorūrvoḥ kaṇṭhe nābhau dvipārśvayoḥ //
1.91.d:
कुर्वीत गोलकन्यासं रक्षायै तदनन्तरम् ।
हृदि वक्त्रेंऽसयोरूर्वोः कण्ठे नाभौ द्विपार्श्वयोः ॥
1.91.m:
Immediately after that, he should perform the placement of the globes (golakanyāsa) for protection:
on the heart, face, shoulders, thighs, throat, navel, both flanks,

1.91.s:
pṛṣṭhe hṛdi tathā mūrdhni vadane netrayornasoḥ /
doḥpatsaṃdhiṣu sāgreṣu vinyasettadanantaram //
1.91.d:
पृष्ठे हृदि तथा मूर्ध्नि वदने नेत्रयोर्नसोः ।
दोःपत्संधिषु साग्रेषु विन्यसेत्तदनन्तरम् ॥
1.91.m:
back, heart, and likewise on the head, face, eyes, nostrils,
and on the joints of the arms and feet along with their tips, he should place [them] after that.

1.91.s:
śirovadanahṛtkukṣisorupādadvaye punaḥ /
hṛdi vaktrāṃbuje ṭaṅkamṛgā bhayavareṣvatha //
1.91.d:
शिरोवदनहृत्कुक्षिसोरुपादद्वये पुनः ।
हृदि वक्त्रांबुजे टङ्कमृगा भयवरेष्वथ ॥
1.91.m:
Again, on the head, face, heart, belly, and on both thighs and feet;
then on the heart, lotus-face, axe, deer, gesture of fearlessness, and boon.

1.91.s:
vaktrāṃsahṛtsapādorujaṭhareṣu kramānnyaset /
mūlamantrasya ṣaḍa varṇānyathāvaddeśikottamaḥ //
1.91.d:
वक्त्रांसहृत्सपादोरुजठरेषु क्रमान्न्यसेत् ।
मूलमन्त्रस्य षड वर्णान्यथावद्देशिकोत्तमः ॥
1.91.m:
The best of preceptors should place in order the six syllables of the root mantra
on the face, shoulders, heart, feet, thighs, and belly, according to rule.

1.91.s:
mūrdhni bhālodarāṃseṣu hṛdaye tāḥ punarnyaset /
paścādanena mantreṇa kurvīta vyāpakaṃ sudhīḥ //
1.91.d:
मूर्ध्नि भालोदरांसेषु हृदये ताः पुनर्न्यसेत् ।
पश्चादनेन मन्त्रेण कुर्वीत व्यापकं सुधीः ॥
1.91.m:
He should place them again on the head, forehead, belly, shoulders, and heart.
Afterward, the wise person should perform the pervasive placement with this mantra:

1.91.s:
namostvanantarūpāya jyotirliṅgāmṛtātmane /
caturmūrtivapuśchāyābhāsitāṅgāya śaṃbhave //
1.91.d:
नमोस्त्वनन्तरूपाय ज्योतिर्लिङ्गामृतात्मने ।
चतुर्मूर्तिवपुश्छायाभासिताङ्गाय शंभवे ॥
1.91.m:
“Homage be to Śambhu of infinite forms, the nectarous essence of the Liṅga of light,
whose limbs are illuminated by the splendor of the four bodily forms.”

1.91.s:
evaṃ nyastaśarīro 'sau cintayetpārvatīpatim /
dhyāyennityaṃ maheśānaṃ raupyaparvatasannibham //
1.91.d:
एवं न्यस्तशरीरो ऽसौ चिन्तयेत्पार्वतीपतिम् ।
ध्यायेन्नित्यं महेशानं रौप्यपर्वतसन्निभम् ॥
1.91.m:
Having thus placed [the mantras on] his body, he should meditate on the Lord of Pārvatī.
He should constantly meditate on Maheśāna, resembling a mountain of silver,

1.91.s:
cārucandrāvataṃsaṃ ca ratnākalpojjvalāṅgakam /
paraśvadhavarābhītimṛgahastaṃ śubhānanam //
1.91.d:
चारुचन्द्रावतंसं च रत्नाकल्पोज्ज्वलाङ्गकम् ।
परश्वधवराभीतिमृगहस्तं शुभाननम् ॥
1.91.m:
adorned with the charming crescent moon, his limbs radiant with jewel-ornaments,
holding an axe, a boon, freedom from fear, and a deer in his hands, with an auspicious face,

1.91.s:
padmāsīnaṃ samantāttu stutaṃ sumanasāṃ gaṇaiḥ /
vyāghrakṛtiṃ vasānaṃ ca viśvādyaṃ viśvarūpakam //
1.91.d:
पद्मासीनं समन्तात्तु स्तुतं सुमनसां गणैः ।
व्याघ्रकृतिं वसानं च विश्वाद्यं विश्वरूपकम् ॥
1.91.m:
seated on a lotus, praised on all sides by the hosts of the gods,
wearing a tiger skin, the primal cause of the universe, universal in form,

1.91.s:
trinetraṃ pañcavaktraṃ ca sarvabhītiharaṃ śivam /
tattvalakṣaṃ japenmantraṃ dīkṣitaḥ śaivavartmanā //
1.91.d:
त्रिनेत्रं पञ्चवक्त्रं च सर्वभीतिहरं शिवम् ।
तत्त्वलक्षं जपेन्मन्त्रं दीक्षितः शैववर्त्मना ॥
1.91.m:
three-eyed, five-faced, removing all fear, auspicious (Śiva).
Initiated according to the Śaiva path, he should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times per syllable.

1.91.s:
tāvatsaṃkhyasahasrāṇi juhuyātpāyasaiḥ śubhaiḥ /
tataḥ siddho bhavenmantraḥ sādhakābhīṣṭasiddhidaḥ //
1.91.d:
तावत्संख्यसहस्राणि जुहुयात्पायसैः शुभैः ।
ततः सिद्धो भवेन्मन्त्रः साधकाभीष्टसिद्धिदः ॥
1.91.m:
He should offer as oblations into the fire that many thousands [of offerings] of auspicious milk-rice.
Then the mantra becomes perfected, bestowing the fulfillment of the practitioner's desires.

1.91.s:
devaṃ saṃpūjayetpīṭhe vāmādinavaśaktike /
vāmā jyeṣṭhā tathā raudrī kālī kalapadādikā //
1.91.d:
देवं संपूजयेत्पीठे वामादिनवशक्तिके ।
वामा ज्येष्ठा तथा रौद्री काली कलपदादिका ॥
1.91.m:
He should worship the deity upon the seat with the nine powers beginning with Vāmā:
Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, and Raudrī; Kālī, the one beginning with the word Kala—

1.91.s:
vikāriṇyāhvayā proktā balādyā vikariṇyatha /
balapramathanī paścātsarvabhūtadamanyatha //
1.91.d:
विकारिण्याह्वया प्रोक्ता बलाद्या विकरिण्यथ ।
बलप्रमथनी पश्चात्सर्वभूतदमन्यथ ॥
1.91.m:
namely, called Kalavikarṇī; then Balavikarṇī,
thereafter Balapramathanī, and next Sarvabhūtadamanī,

1.91.s:
manonmanīti saṃproktāḥ śaivapīṭhasya śaktayaḥ /
namo bhagavate paścātsakalādi vadettataḥ //
1.91.d:
मनोन्मनीति संप्रोक्ताः शैवपीठस्य शक्तयः ।
नमो भगवते पश्चात्सकलादि वदेत्ततः ॥
1.91.m:
and Manonmanī—these are declared to be the powers of the Śaiva seat.
Then one should utter: “Homage to the Blessed One, the all-inclusive...”

1.91.s:
guṇātmaśaktibhaktāya tato 'nantāya tatparam /
yogapīṭhātmane bhūyo namastārādiko manuḥ //
1.91.d:
गुणात्मशक्तिभक्ताय ततो ऽनन्ताय तत्परम् ।
योगपीठात्मने भूयो नमस्तारादिको मनुः ॥
1.91.m:
“...devoted to the power that is the nature of qualities, then to Ananta, and after that
to the essence of the seat of yoga, homage again”—the mantra begins with Tāra [oṃ].

1.91.s:
amunā manunā dadyādāsanaṃ girijāpateḥ /
mūrtiṃ mūlena saṃkalpya tatrāvāhya yajecchivam //
1.91.d:
अमुना मनुना दद्यादासनं गिरिजापतेः ।
मूर्तिं मूलेन संकल्प्य तत्रावाह्य यजेच्छिवम् ॥
1.91.m:
With this mantra he should present a seat to the Lord of the Mountain's Daughter.
Having conceived the form through the root mantra and invoked Śiva there, he should worship him.

1.91.s:
karṇikāyāṃ yajenmūrtirīśamīśānadiggajam /
śuddhasphaṭikasaṃkāśaṃ dikṣu tatpuruṣādikā //
1.91.d:
कर्णिकायां यजेन्मूर्तिरीशमीशानदिग्गजम् ।
शुद्धस्फटिकसंकाशं दिक्षु तत्पुरुषादिका ॥
1.91.m:
In the pericarp he should worship the forms of Īśa, the quarter-elephant in the northeast;
resembling pure crystal. In the cardinal directions [he should worship] Tatpuruṣa and the others,

1.91.s:
pītāñjanaśvetaraktāḥ pradhānasadṛśāyudhāḥ /
caturvaktrasamāyuktā yathāvattāḥ prapūjayet //
1.91.d:
पीताञ्जनश्वेतरक्ताः प्रधानसदृशायुधाः ।
चतुर्वक्त्रसमायुक्ता यथावत्ताः प्रपूजयेत् ॥
1.91.m:
yellow, black, white, and red, bearing weapons resembling those of the principal deity,
endowed with four faces; he should worship them properly.

1.91.s:
koṇeṣvarcennivṛttyādyāstejorūpāḥ kalāḥ kramāt /
aṅgāni kesarasthāni vighneśānpannagānyajet //
1.91.d:
कोणेष्वर्चेन्निवृत्त्याद्यास्तेजोरूपाः कलाः क्रमात् ।
अङ्गानि केसरस्थानि विघ्नेशान्पन्नगान्यजेत् ॥
1.91.m:
In the corners he should worship in order the parts (kalās) beginning with Nivṛtti, which are forms of light.
He should worship the limbs situated on the filaments, the lords of obstacles, and the serpents:

1.91.s:
anantaṃ sukhanāmānaṃ śivottamamanantaram /
ekanetramekarudraṃ trimūrtiṃ tadanantaram //
1.91.d:
अनन्तं सुखनामानं शिवोत्तममनन्तरम् ।
एकनेत्रमेकरुद्रं त्रिमूर्तिं तदनन्तरम् ॥
1.91.m:
Ananta, the one named Sukha, Śivottama thereafter,
Ekanetra, Ekarudra, Trimūrti thereafter,

1.91.s:
paścācchīkaṇṭhanāmānaṃ śikhaṇḍinamiti kramāt /
raktapītasitāraktakṛṣṇaraktāñjanāsitān //
1.91.d:
पश्चाच्छीकण्ठनामानं शिखण्डिनमिति क्रमात् ।
रक्तपीतसितारक्तकृष्णरक्ताञ्जनासितान् ॥
1.91.m:
and then the one named Śrīkaṇṭha, and Śikhaṇḍin, in that order:
red, yellow, white, reddish, black, red, collyrium-colored, and dark,

1.91.s:
kirīṭārpitabālendūnpadmasthānbhūṣaṇānvitān /
trinetrāñchūlavajrāstracāpahastānmanoramān //
1.91.d:
किरीटार्पितबालेन्दून्पद्मस्थान्भूषणान्वितान् ।
त्रिनेत्राञ्छूलवज्रास्त्रचापहस्तान्मनोरमान् ॥
1.91.m:
bearing the young moon set upon their crowns, seated on lotuses, endowed with ornaments,
three-eyed, holding a trident, a thunderbolt, missiles, and a bow in their hands, delightful.

1.91.s:
uttarādi yajetpaścādrudraṃ caṇḍeśvaraṃ punaḥ /
tato nandimahākālau gaṇeśaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ punaḥ //
1.91.d:
उत्तरादि यजेत्पश्चाद्रुद्रं चण्डेश्वरं पुनः ।
ततो नन्दिमहाकालौ गणेशं वृषभं पुनः ॥
1.91.m:
Beginning from the north, he should then worship Rudra, and Caṇḍeśvara again;
then Nandin and Mahākāla, Gaṇeśa, and the Bull again;

1.91.s:
atha bhṛṅgiṃ riṭiṃ skandametānpadmāsanasthitān /
svarṇatoyāruṇaśyāmamuktendusitapāṭalān //
1.91.d:
अथ भृङ्गिं रिटिं स्कन्दमेतान्पद्मासनस्थितान् ।
स्वर्णतोयारुणश्याममुक्तेन्दुसितपाटलान् ॥
1.91.m:
then Bhṛṅgin, Riṭi, and Skanda—these seated on lotus-seats,
golden, water-colored, dawn-red, dark, pearl-colored, moon-white, and pale red.

1.91.s:
indrādayastataḥ pūjyā vajrādyāyudhasaṃyutāḥ /
itthaṃ saṃpūjayeddevaṃ sahasraṃ nityaśo japet //
1.91.d:
इन्द्रादयस्ततः पूज्या वज्राद्यायुधसंयुताः ।
इत्थं संपूजयेद्देवं सहस्रं नित्यशो जपेत् ॥
1.91.m:
Then Indra and the other [guardians] are to be worshipped, endowed with weapons beginning with the thunderbolt.
Worshipping the deity in this way, he should recite [the mantra] a thousand times daily.

1.91.s:
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ prāpnuyādvāñchitaṃ śriyam /
dvisahasraṃ japan rogānmucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
1.91.d:
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तः प्राप्नुयाद्वाञ्छितं श्रियम् ।
द्विसहस्रं जपन् रोगान्मुच्यते नात्र संशयः ॥
1.91.m:
Freed from all sins, he shall obtain the wealth he desires;
reciting it two thousand times, he is freed from diseases—of this there is no doubt.

1.91.s:
trisanmantraṃ japanmantraṃ dīrghamāyuravāpnuyāt /
sahasravṛddhayā prajapansarvakāmānavāpnuyāt //
1.91.d:
त्रिसन्मन्त्रं जपन्मन्त्रं दीर्घमायुरवाप्नुयात् ।
सहस्रवृद्धया प्रजपन्सर्वकामानवाप्नुयात् ॥
1.91.m:
Reciting the mantra three times a day, he shall attain a long life;
reciting it with increments of a thousand, he shall obtain all desires.

1.91.s:
ājyānvitaistilaiḥ śuddhairjuhuyāllakṣamādarāt /
utpātajanitān kleśānnāśayennātra saṃśayaḥ //
1.91.d:
आज्यान्वितैस्तिलैः शुद्धैर्जुहुयाल्लक्षमादरात् ।
उत्पातजनितान् क्लेशान्नाशयेन्नात्र संशयः ॥
1.91.m:
He should devoutly make fire oblations of a hundred thousand [offerings] of pure sesame seeds with ghee;
he destroys afflictions caused by portents—of this there is no doubt.

1.91.s:
śatalakṣaṃ japansākṣācchivo bhavati mānavaḥ /
ṣaḍakṣaraḥ śaktiruddhaḥ kathito 'ṣṭākṣaro manuḥ //
1.91.d:
शतलक्षं जपन्साक्षाच्छिवो भवति मानवः ।
षडक्षरः शक्तिरुद्धः कथितो ऽष्टाक्षरो मनुः ॥
1.91.m:
Reciting it ten million times, a mortal becomes Śiva himself.
The six-syllable mantra enclosed with Śakti is declared to be the eight-syllable mantra.

1.91.s:
ṛṣiśchandaḥ purā prokto devatā syādumāpatiḥ /
aṅgāni pūrvamuktāni saumyamīśaṃ vicintayet //
1.91.d:
ऋषिश्छन्दः पुरा प्रोक्तो देवता स्यादुमापतिः ।
अङ्गानि पूर्वमुक्तानि सौम्यमीशं विचिन्तयेत् ॥
1.91.m:
The sage and the metre are as stated before; the deity is the Lord of Umā.
The limbs are as previously mentioned; he should meditate on the gentle Īśa,

1.91.s:
bandhūkābhaṃ trinetraṃ ca śaśikhaṇḍadharaṃ vibhum /
smerāsyaṃ svakaraiḥ śūlaṃ kaṃpālaṃ varadābhaye //
1.91.d:
बन्धूकाभं त्रिनेत्रं च शशिखण्डधरं विभुम् ।
स्मेरास्यं स्वकरैः शूलं कंपालं वरदाभये ॥
1.91.m:
