resembling a bandhūka flower, three-eyed, the all-pervading lord bearing a crescent moon,
with a smiling face, in his own hands [holding] a trident, a skull-cup, and the gestures of bestowing boons and fearlessness,

1.91.s:
vahṝntaṃ cārubhūpāḍhyaṃ vāmorusthādrikanyayā /
bhujenāśliṣṭadehaṃ taṃ cintayenmanasā hṛdi //
1.91.d:
वहॄन्तं चारुभूपाढ्यं वामोरुस्थाद्रिकन्यया ।
भुजेनाश्लिष्टदेहं तं चिन्तयेन्मनसा हृदि ॥
1.91.m:
bearing [these], richly adorned with charming ornaments, his body embraced by the arm
of the Daughter of the Mountain seated on his left thigh—he should meditate on him mentally in his heart.

1.91.s:
manulakṣaṃ japenmantraṃ tatsahasraṃ yathāvidhi /
juhuyānmānmadhusasiktairāragvadhasamidvaraiḥ //
1.91.d:
मनुलक्षं जपेन्मन्त्रं तत्सहस्रं यथाविधि ।
जुहुयान्मान्मधुससिक्तैरारग्वधसमिद्वरैः ॥
1.91.m:
He should recite the mantra a hundred thousand times; according to rule, a thousand times that
he should offer into the fire with excellent firewood of āragvadha moistened with honey.

1.91.s:
prākprokte pūjayetpīṭhe gandhapuṣpairumāpatim /
aṅgāvṛtairbahiḥ pūjyā hṛllekhādyā yathāpurā //
1.91.d:
प्राक्प्रोक्ते पूजयेत्पीठे गन्धपुष्पैरुमापतिम् ।
अङ्गावृतैर्बहिः पूज्या हृल्लेखाद्या यथापुरा ॥
1.91.m:
On the previously mentioned seat, he should worship the Lord of Umā with fragrant pastes and flowers.
Outside, surrounded by the limbs, Hṛllekhā and the others should be worshipped as before.

1.91.s:
madhyaprāgdakṣiṇodīcyapaścimeṣu vidhānataḥ /
yajetpūrvādipatreṣu vṛṣabhādyānanukramāt //
1.91.d:
मध्यप्राग्दक्षिणोदीच्यपश्चिमेषु विधानतः ।
यजेत्पूर्वादिपत्रेषु वृषभाद्याननुक्रमात् ॥
1.91.m:
In the center, east, south, north, and west, according to rule,
he should worship the Bull and the others on the petals beginning in the east in sequence.

1.91.s:
śūlaṭaṅkākṣavalayakamaṇḍalulasatkaram /
raktākāraṃ trinayanaṃ caṇḍeśamatha pūjayet //
1.91.d:
शूलटङ्काक्षवलयकमण्डलुलसत्करम् ।
रक्ताकारं त्रिनयनं चण्डेशमथ पूजयेत् ॥
1.91.m:
With shining hands holding a trident, an axe, a rosary, and a water-pot,
red-bodied and three-eyed, he should then worship Caṇḍeśa.

1.91.s:
cakraśaṅkhābhayābhīṣṭakarāṃ marakataprabhām /
durgāṃ prapūjayetsaumyāṃ trinetrāṃ cārubhūṣaṇām //
1.91.d:
चक्रशङ्खाभयाभीष्टकरां मरकतप्रभाम् ।
दुर्गां प्रपूजयेत्सौम्यां त्रिनेत्रां चारुभूषणाम् ॥
1.91.m:
Holding a discus, a conch, and the gestures of fearlessness and boon-granting, with the radiance of an emerald,
he should worship gentle Durgā, three-eyed and beautifully adorned.

1.91.s:
kalpaśākhāntare ghaṇṭāṃ dadhānaṃ dvādaśekṣaṇam /
bālārkābhaṃ śiśuṃ kāntaṃṣaṇmukhaṃ pūjayettataḥ //
1.91.d:
कल्पशाखान्तरे घण्टां दधानं द्वादशेक्षणम् ।
बालार्काभं शिशुं कान्तंषण्मुखं पूजयेत्ततः ॥
1.91.m:
Holding a bell in a bower of wish-fulfilling branches, twelve-eyed,
resembling the rising sun, youthful and lovely—then he should worship the six-faced [Skanda].

1.91.s:
nanditaṃ ca yajetsaumyāṃ ratnabhūṣaṇamaṇḍitam /
paraśvadhavarābhītiṭaṅkinaṃ śyāmavigraham //
1.91.d:
नन्दितं च यजेत्सौम्यां रत्नभूषणमण्डितम् ।
परश्वधवराभीतिटङ्किनं श्यामविग्रहम् ॥
1.91.m:
He should worship Nandita, gentle, adorned with jewel-ornaments,
holding an axe, a boon, freedom from fear, and a chisel, with a dark form.

1.91.s:
pāśāṅkuśavarābhīṣṭadhāriṇaṃ kuṅkumaprabham /
vighnanāyakamabhyarceccandrārddhakṛtaśekharam //
1.91.d:
पाशाङ्कुशवराभीष्टधारिणं कुङ्कुमप्रभम् ।
विघ्ननायकमभ्यर्चेच्चन्द्रार्द्धकृतशेखरम् ॥
1.91.m:
Holding a noose, a goad, a boon, and freedom from fear, radiant as saffron,
he should worship the Lord of Obstacles, who has the crescent moon as his crest.

1.91.s:
śyāmaṃ raktotpalakaraṃ vāmāṅkanyastatatkaram /
dvinetraṃ raktavastrāḍhyaṃ senāpatimathārcayet //
1.91.d:
श्यामं रक्तोत्पलकरं वामाङ्कन्यस्ततत्करम् ।
द्विनेत्रं रक्तवस्त्राढ्यं सेनापतिमथार्चयेत् ॥
1.91.m:
Dark, holding a red lotus, his hand resting on his left hip,
two-eyed and dressed in red garments—then he should worship the Army-Commander.

1.91.s:
tato 'ṣṭamātaraḥ pūjyā brāhmādyāḥ proktalakṣaṇāḥ /
indrādikānlokapālānsvasvadikṣu samarcayet //
1.91.d:
ततो ऽष्टमातरः पूज्या ब्राह्माद्याः प्रोक्तलक्षणाः ।
इन्द्रादिकान्लोकपालान्स्वस्वदिक्षु समर्चयेत् ॥
1.91.m:
Then the eight mothers beginning with Brāhmī, endowed with the stated characteristics, are to be worshipped;
he should worship the world-guardians beginning with Indra in their respective directions,

1.91.s:
vajrādīni tadastrāṇi tadbahiḥ kramator'cayet /
evaṃ yo bhajate mantrī devaṃ śaṃbhumumāpatim //
1.91.d:
वज्रादीनि तदस्त्राणि तद्बहिः क्रमतोर्ऽचयेत् ।
एवं यो भजते मन्त्री देवं शंभुमुमापतिम् ॥
1.91.m:
and outside them their weapons beginning with the thunderbolt, in order.
The mantra-practitioner who thus reveres the god Śambhu, the Lord of Umā,

1.91.s:
sa bhavetsarvalokānāṃ saubhāgyaśreyasāṃ padam /
sāṃtasadyāntasaṃyukto bindubhūṣitamastakaḥ //
1.91.d:
स भवेत्सर्वलोकानां सौभाग्यश्रेयसां पदम् ।
सांतसद्यान्तसंयुक्तो बिन्दुभूषितमस्तकः ॥
1.91.m: He becomes the receptacle of fortune and the highest good for all worlds. / Joined with 'sa' and ending in the [bīja] of Sadyo[jāta], with its head adorned with a bindu,

1.91.s:
prāsādākhyo manuḥ prokto bhajatāṃ sarvasiddhidaḥ /
ṣaḍdīrghayuktabījena ṣaḍaṅgavidhirīritaḥ //
1.91.d:
प्रासादाख्यो मनुः प्रोक्तो भजतां सर्वसिद्धिदः ।
षड्दीर्घयुक्तबीजेन षडङ्गविधिरीरितः ॥
1.91.m: the mantra called Prāsāda is proclaimed, bestowing all accomplishments on those who worship it. / The rule for the six limbs has been stated using the seed-syllable combined with the six long [vowels].

1.91.s:
ṣaḍarṇavattu munyādyāḥ proktāścāsyāpi nārada /
īśānādyā nyasenmūrtīraṅguṣṭhādiṣu deśikaḥ //
1.91.d:
षडर्णवत्तु मुन्याद्याः प्रोक्ताश्चास्यापि नारद ।
ईशानाद्या न्यसेन्मूर्तीरङ्गुष्ठादिषु देशिकः ॥
1.91.m: Its sage and other [deities] are also declared like those of the six-syllabled mantra, O Nārada. / The preceptor should place the forms beginning with Īśāna on the thumb and other [fingers].

1.91.s:
īśānākhyaṃ tatpuruṣamaghoraṃ tadanantaram /
vāmadevāhvayaṃ sadyojātabījaṃ kramādviduḥ //
1.91.d:
ईशानाख्यं तत्पुरुषमघोरं तदनन्तरम् ।
वामदेवाह्वयं सद्योजातबीजं क्रमाद्विदुः ॥
1.91.m: They know in order the seed-syllables called Īśāna, Tatpuruṣa, and next Aghora, / that named Vāmadeva, and Sadyojāta,

1.91.s:
ukārādyaiḥ pañcahrasvaurvilomānsaṃyutaṃ ca yat /
tattadaṅgulibhirbhūyastattadikānnyaset //
1.91.d:
उकाराद्यैः पञ्चह्रस्वौर्विलोमान्संयुतं च यत् ।
तत्तदङ्गुलिभिर्भूयस्तत्तदिकान्न्यसेत् ॥
1.91.m: combined in reverse order with the five short [vowels] beginning with 'u'. / With those respective fingers, he should repeatedly place the respective [mantras] in those directions:

1.91.s:
śirovadanahṛdguhyapādadeśe yathākramāt /
urddhaprāgdakṣiṇodīcyapaścimeṣu mukheṣu ca //
1.91.d:
शिरोवदनहृद्गुह्यपाददेशे यथाक्रमात् ।
उर्द्धप्राग्दक्षिणोदीच्यपश्चिमेषु मुखेषु च ॥
1.91.m: on the head, face, heart, secret region, and feet, in proper order, / and on the upward, eastern, southern, northern, and western faces.

1.91.s:
tataḥ pravinyasedvidvānaṣṭatriṃśatkalāstanau /
īśānādyā ṛcaḥ samyagaṅgulīṣu yathākramāt //
1.91.d:
ततः प्रविन्यसेद्विद्वानष्टत्रिंशत्कलास्तनौ ।
ईशानाद्या ऋचः सम्यगङ्गुलीषु यथाक्रमात् ॥
1.91.m: Then the learned practitioner should place the thirty-eight Kalās on his body; / the verses beginning with Īśāna [should be placed] properly on the fingers in order.

1.91.s:
aṅguṣṭhādikaniṣṭhāntaṃ nyaseddeśikasattamaḥ /
mūrddhāsyahṛdayāṃbhojaguhyapāde tu tāḥ punaḥ //
1.91.d:
अङ्गुष्ठादिकनिष्ठान्तं न्यसेद्देशिकसत्तमः ।
मूर्द्धास्यहृदयांभोजगुह्यपादे तु ताः पुनः ॥
1.91.m: The excellent preceptor should place them from the thumb to the little finger; / and again, those [should be placed] on the head, face, heart-lotus, secret region, and feet.

1.91.s:
vaktre mūrdhādiṣu nyasya bhūyo 'ṅgāni prakalpayet /
tārapañcakamuccārya sarvajñāya hṛdīritam //
1.91.d:
वक्त्रे मूर्धादिषु न्यस्य भूयो ऽङ्गानि प्रकल्पयेत् ।
तारपञ्चकमुच्चार्य सर्वज्ञाय हृदीरितम् ॥
1.91.m: Having placed them on the mouth, head, and so forth, he should once more arrange the limbs: / uttering five Praṇavas, 'to the all-knowing one' is said to be the heart;

1.91.s:
amṛte tejo mālini tṛptāyeti padaṃ punaḥ /
tadante brahmaśiḥse śirogaṃ jvalitaṃ tataḥ //
1.91.d:
अमृते तेजो मालिनि तृप्तायेति पदं पुनः ।
तदन्ते ब्रह्मशिःसे शिरोगं ज्वलितं ततः ॥
1.91.m: 'amṛte tejo mālini tṛptāya' is the word next; / at the end of that, 'brahmaśirase' goes to the head; then 'jvalitaṃ'

1.91.s:
śikhiṃ śikhāya parato 'nādibodhāya tacchikhā /
vajriṇe vajrahastāya svatantrāya tanucchadam //
1.91.d:
शिखिं शिखाय परतो ऽनादिबोधाय तच्छिखा ।
वज्रिणे वज्रहस्ताय स्वतन्त्राय तनुच्छदम् ॥
1.91.m: and 'śikhiṃ' to the topknot; thereafter, 'anādibodhāya' is that topknot; / 'vajriṇe vajrahastāya svatantrāya' is the armor;

1.91.s:
saiṃ saiṃ haumiti saṃbhāṣya parato toṃ guhyaśaktaye /
netramuktaṃ ślīpaśuṃ huṃ phaḍante netraṃ śaktaye //
1.91.d:
सैं सैं हौमिति संभाष्य परतो तों गुह्यशक्तये ।
नेत्रमुक्तं श्लीपशुं हुं फडन्ते नेत्रं शक्तये ॥
1.91.m: having uttered 'saiṃ saiṃ haum', thereafter 'oṃ' to the secret power / is spoken as the eye; ending with 'ślīpaśuṃ huṃ phaṭ', to the power of the eye,

1.91.s:
astramuktaṃ ṣaḍaṅgāni kuryādevaṃ samāhitaḥ /
pūrvadakṣiṇapaścātprāksaumyamadhyeṣu pañcasu //
1.91.d:
अस्त्रमुक्तं षडङ्गानि कुर्यादेवं समाहितः ।
पूर्वदक्षिणपश्चात्प्राक्सौम्यमध्येषु पञ्चसु ॥
1.91.m: the weapon is pronounced. One should compose the six limbs thus with concentrated mind. / In the five faces—in the eastern, southern, western, northern, and central—

1.91.s:
vaktreṣu pañca vinyasyedīśānasya kalāḥ kramāt /
īśānaḥ sarvavidyānāṃ śaśinī prathamā kalā //
1.91.d:
वक्त्रेषु पञ्च विन्यस्येदीशानस्य कलाः क्रमात् ।
ईशानः सर्वविद्यानां शशिनी प्रथमा कला ॥
1.91.m: he should place in order the five Kalās of Īśāna: / Īśānaḥ sarvavidyānāṃ, Śaśinī being the first Kalā;

1.91.s:
īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ maṅgalā tadanantaram /
brahmādhipatiḥ śabdānte brahmaṇo 'dhipatiḥ punaḥ //
1.91.d:
ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां मङ्गला तदनन्तरम् ।
ब्रह्माधिपतिः शब्दान्ते ब्रह्मणो ऽधिपतिः पुनः ॥
1.91.m: īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ, and Maṅgalā thereafter; / brahmādhipatiḥ, followed by the word brahmaṇo 'dhipatiḥ;

1.91.s:
brahmeṣṭadā tṛtīyāsyācchivo me astu tatparā /
marīciḥ kathitā vipra caturthī ca sadāśive //
1.91.d:
ब्रह्मेष्टदा तृतीयास्याच्छिवो मे अस्तु तत्परा ।
मरीचिः कथिता विप्र चतुर्थी च सदाशिवे ॥
1.91.m: Brahmeṣṭadā is the third; śivo me astu is the next; / Marīci is declared the fourth, O brāhmaṇa; in Sadāśiva,

1.91.s:
aṃśumālinyatha parā praṇavādyā namonvitāḥ /
pūrvapaścimayāmyodagvaktreṣu tadanantaram //
1.91.d:
अंशुमालिन्यथ परा प्रणवाद्या नमोन्विताः ।
पूर्वपश्चिमयाम्योदग्वक्त्रेषु तदनन्तरम् ॥
1.91.m: Aṃśumalinī is next. These are preceded by Praṇava and accompanied by 'namaḥ'. / Thereafter, on the eastern, western, southern, and northern faces,

1.91.s:
catasro vinyasenmantrī puruṣasya kalāḥ kramāt /
ādyā tatpurupāyeti vidmahe śāntirīritā //
1.91.d:
चतस्रो विन्यसेन्मन्त्री पुरुषस्य कलाः क्रमात् ।
आद्या तत्पुरुपायेति विद्महे शान्तिरीरिता ॥
1.91.m: the practitioner should place the four Kalās of Tatpuruṣa in order: / the first, 'tatpuruṣāya vidmahe', is declared to be Śānti;

1.91.s:
mahādevāya śabdānte dhīmahi syāttataḥ param /
vidyā dvitīyā kathitā tanno rudraḥ padaṃ tataḥ //
1.91.d:
महादेवाय शब्दान्ते धीमहि स्यात्ततः परम् ।
विद्या द्वितीया कथिता तन्नो रुद्रः पदं ततः ॥
1.91.m: 'mahādevāya', at the end of which word is 'dhīmahi', is next; / Vidyā is declared the second; then the phrase 'tanno rudraḥ';

1.91.s:
pratiṣṭhā kathitā paścāttṛtīyā syātpracodayāt /
nivṛttistatparā sarvā praṇavādyā namonvitā //
1.91.d:
प्रतिष्ठा कथिता पश्चात्तृतीया स्यात्प्रचोदयात् ।
निवृत्तिस्तत्परा सर्वा प्रणवाद्या नमोन्विता ॥
1.91.m: Pratiṣṭhā is declared next as the third; from 'pracodayāt', / Nivṛtti follows. All of them are preceded by Praṇava and joined with 'namaḥ'.

1.91.s:
hṛdi cāṃsadvaye nābhikukṣau pṛṣṭhe 'tha vakṣasi /
athorasi kalā nyasyedaṣṭau mantrī yathāvidhi //
1.91.d:
हृदि चांसद्वये नाभिकुक्षौ पृष्ठे ऽथ वक्षसि ।
अथोरसि कला न्यस्येदष्टौ मन्त्री यथाविधि ॥
1.91.m: In the heart, on both shoulders, on the navel, the belly, the back, and the chest, / and then on the breast, the practitioner should place the eight Kalās according to the rule.

1.91.s:
aghorebhyastathā pūrvamīritā prathamā kalā /
atha ghorebhya ityante mohāsyāttadanantaram //
1.91.d:
अघोरेभ्यस्तथा पूर्वमीरिता प्रथमा कला ।
अथ घोरेभ्य इत्यन्ते मोहास्यात्तदनन्तरम् ॥
1.91.m: The first kalā has previously been spoken of with *aghorebhyaḥ*; / then, with *atha ghorebhyaḥ* at the end, Mohā follows next.

1.91.s:
aghorānte kṣamā paścāttṛtīyā parikīrtitā /
ghoratarebhyo nidrā syātsarvebhyaḥ sarvatatparā //
1.91.d:
अघोरान्ते क्षमा पश्चात्तृतीया परिकीर्तिता ।
घोरतरेभ्यो निद्रा स्यात्सर्वेभ्यः सर्वतत्परा ॥
1.91.m: After *aghora*, Kṣamā is declared as the third; / with *ghoratarebhyaḥ* it is Nidrā; with *sarvebhyaḥ sarva* is next;

1.91.s:
vyādhistu pañcamī proktā śarvebhyastadanantaram /
mṛtyurnigaditā ṣaṣṭhī namaste astu tatparam //
1.91.d:
व्याधिस्तु पञ्चमी प्रोक्ता शर्वेभ्यस्तदनन्तरम् ।
मृत्युर्निगदिता षष्ठी नमस्ते अस्तु तत्परम् ॥
1.91.m: Vyādhi is spoken of as the fifth, and then with *śarvebhyaḥ*; / Mṛtyu is proclaimed as the sixth, and next is *namas te astu*;

1.91.s:
kṣudhā syātsaptamī rudrarūpebhyaḥ kathitā tṛṣā /
aṣṭamī kathitā etādhruvādyā namasānvitāḥ //
1.91.d:
क्षुधा स्यात्सप्तमी रुद्ररूपेभ्यः कथिता तृषा ।
अष्टमी कथिता एताध्रुवाद्या नमसान्विताः ॥
1.91.m: Kṣudhā is the seventh; with *rudrarūpebhyaḥ*, Tṛṣā / is declared as the eighth. These begin with Praṇava and end with *namaḥ*.

1.91.s:
guhyayugmoruyugmeṣu jānujaṅghāsphijoḥ punaḥ /
kaṭyāṃ pārśvadvaye vāmakalā nyasyettrayodaśa //
1.91.d:
गुह्ययुग्मोरुयुग्मेषु जानुजङ्घास्फिजोः पुनः ।
कट्यां पार्श्वद्वये वामकला न्यस्येत्त्रयोदश ॥
1.91.m: On the two genitals, the two thighs, knees, shanks, and buttocks, / on the waist and both flanks, one should place the thirteen Vāma-kalās:

1.91.s:
prathamā vāmadevāya namonte syādrujā kalā /
syājjyeṣṭhāya namo rakṣā dvitīyā parikīrtitā //
1.91.d:
प्रथमा वामदेवाय नमोन्ते स्याद्रुजा कला ।
स्याज्ज्येष्ठाय नमो रक्षा द्वितीया परिकीर्तिता ॥
1.91.m: The first is the kalā Rujā, ending with *vāmadevāya namaḥ*; / ending with *jyeṣṭhāya namaḥ* is Rakṣā, declared as the second;

1.91.s:
kalakāmā pañcamī syāttato vikaraṇāya ca /
namaḥ saṃyamanī ṣaṣṭhī kathitā tadanantaram //
1.91.d:
कलकामा पञ्चमी स्यात्ततो विकरणाय च ।
नमः संयमनी षष्ठी कथिता तदनन्तरम् ॥
1.91.m: Kāma is the fifth kalā; then with *vikaraṇāya ca / namaḥ* is Saṃyamanī, declared next as the sixth;

1.91.s:
balakriyā saptamīṣṭā kalā vikaraṇāya ca /
namo vṛddhistvaṣṭamī syādbalānte ca sthirā kalā //
1.91.d:
बलक्रिया सप्तमीष्टा कला विकरणाय च ।
नमो वृद्धिस्त्वष्टमी स्याद्बलान्ते च स्थिरा कला ॥
1.91.m: Balakriyā is desired as the seventh kalā; with *vikaraṇāya ca / namaḥ* is Vṛddhi as the eighth; and after *bala* is the kalā Sthirā;

1.91.s:
paścātpramathanāyānte namo rātrirudīritā /
sarvabhūtadamanāya namonte bhrāmaṇī kalā //
1.91.d:
पश्चात्प्रमथनायान्ते नमो रात्रिरुदीरिता ।
सर्वभूतदमनाय नमोन्ते भ्रामणी कला ॥
1.91.m: Next, ending with *pramathanāya namaḥ*, Rātri is declared; / with *sarvabhūtadamanāya namaḥ* at the end is the kalā Bhrāmaṇī;

1.91.s:
namonte mohinī proktā mantrajñairdvādaśī kalā /
manonmanyai namaḥ paścājjvarā proktā trayodaśī //
1.91.d:
नमोन्ते मोहिनी प्रोक्ता मन्त्रज्ञैर्द्वादशी कला ।
मनोन्मन्यै नमः पश्चाज्ज्वरा प्रोक्ता त्रयोदशी ॥
1.91.m: ending with *namaḥ*, Mohinī is spoken of by knowers of mantra as the twelfth kalā; / then with *manonmanyai namaḥ*, Jvarā is spoken of as the thirteenth.

1.91.s:
praṇavādyāścaturthyantā namontāstu prakīrtitāḥ /
pādadostananāsāsu mūrdhni bāhuyuge nyaset //
1.91.d:
प्रणवाद्याश्चतुर्थ्यन्ता नमोन्तास्तु प्रकीर्तिताः ।
पाददोस्तननासासु मूर्ध्नि बाहुयुगे न्यसेत् ॥
1.91.m: They are proclaimed as beginning with Praṇava, ending with the dative, and ending with *namaḥ*. / One should place on the feet, arms, breasts, nose, head, and the two arms

1.91.s:
sadyojātabhavāḥ samyagaṣṭau mantrāḥ kalāḥ kramāt /
sadyojātaṃ prapadyāmi siddhiḥ syātprathamā kalā //
1.91.d:
सद्योजातभवाः सम्यगष्टौ मन्त्राः कलाः क्रमात् ।
सद्योजातं प्रपद्यामि सिद्धिः स्यात्प्रथमा कला ॥
1.91.m: the eight mantras that arise from Sadyojāta, the kalās in order: / with *sadyojātaṃ prapadyāmi*, Siddhi is the first kalā;

1.91.s:
sadyojātāya vai bhūyo namaḥ syād vṛddhirīritā /
bhavedyutistṛtīyā syādabhave tadanandaram //
1.91.d:
सद्योजाताय वै भूयो नमः स्याद् वृद्धिरीरिता ।
भवेद्युतिस्तृतीया स्यादभवे तदनन्दरम् ॥
1.91.m: with *sadyojātāya vai bhūyo namaḥ*, Vṛddhi is declared; / with *bhave* is Dyuti, the third; next, with *abhave*,

1.91.s:
lakṣmī caturthī kathitā tato nātibhavepadam /
medhā syātpañcamī proktā kalābhūyo bhavasva mām //
1.91.d:
लक्ष्मी चतुर्थी कथिता ततो नातिभवेपदम् ।
मेधा स्यात्पञ्चमी प्रोक्ता कलाभूयो भवस्व माम् ॥
1.91.m: Lakṣmī is declared as the fourth; then with the word *nātibhave* / is Medhā, spoken of as the fifth kalā; with *bhūyo bhavasva mām*

1.91.s:
prājñā samīritā ṣaṣṭhī bhavānte syātprabhā kalā /
udbhavāya namaḥ paścātsudhā syādaṣṭamī kalā //
1.91.d:
प्राज्ञा समीरिता षष्ठी भवान्ते स्यात्प्रभा कला ।
उद्भवाय नमः पश्चात्सुधा स्यादष्टमी कला ॥
1.91.m: Prājñā is proclaimed as the sixth; ending with *bhava* is the kalā Prabhā; / next, with *udbhavāya namaḥ*, the eighth kalā is Sudhā.

1.91.s:
praṇavādyāścaturthyantā kalāḥ sarvā namonvitāḥ /
aṣṭātriṃśatkalāḥ proktāḥ pañca brahmapadādikāḥ //
1.91.d:
प्रणवाद्याश्चतुर्थ्यन्ता कलाः सर्वा नमोन्विताः ।
अष्टात्रिंशत्कलाः प्रोक्ताः पञ्च ब्रह्मपदादिकाः ॥
1.91.m: All the kalās begin with Praṇava, end with the dative, and are accompanied by *namaḥ*. / The thirty-eight kalās beginning with the five Brahman-words have been declared.

1.91.s:
iti vinyastadeho 'sau bhavedgaṅgādharaḥ svayam /
tataḥ samāhito bhūtvā dhyāyedevaṃ sadāśivam //
1.91.d:
इति विन्यस्तदेहो ऽसौ भवेद्गङ्गाधरः स्वयम् ।
ततः समाहितो भूत्वा ध्यायेदेवं सदाशिवम् ॥
1.91.m: Having thus placed [them] upon his body, he becomes Gaṅgādhara himself. / Then, having become concentrated, one should meditate upon Sadāśiva in this way:

1.91.s:
sitapītāsitaśvetajapābhaiḥ pañcabhirmukhaiḥ /
akṣairyutaṃ glaumukuṭaṃ koṭipūrṇendusaṃprabham //
1.91.d:
सितपीतासितश्वेतजपाभैः पञ्चभिर्मुखैः ।
अक्षैर्युतं ग्लौमुकुटं कोटिपूर्णेन्दुसंप्रभम् ॥
1.91.m: with five faces shining like white, yellow, black, white, and hibiscus flowers, / endowed with eyes, with a crown adorned with the moon, radiant as ten million full moons,

1.91.s:
śūlaṃ ṭaṅkaṃ kṛpāṇaṃ ca vajrāgnyahipatīnkaraiḥ /
dadhānaṃbhūṣaṇoddīptaṃ ghaṇṭāpāśavarābhayān //
1.91.d:
शूलं टङ्कं कृपाणं च वज्राग्न्यहिपतीन्करैः ।
दधानंभूषणोद्दीप्तं घण्टापाशवराभयान् ॥
1.91.m: bearing in his hands a trident, a chisel, a sword, a thunderbolt, fire, and serpent-kings, / blazing with ornaments, and [holding] a bell, a noose, the boon-giving and fear-dispelling gestures.

1.91.s:
evaṃ dhyātvā japenmantraṃ pañcalakṣaṃ madhuplutaiḥ /
prasūnaiḥ karavīrotthairjuhuyāttahṛśāṃśataḥ //
1.91.d:
एवं ध्यात्वा जपेन्मन्त्रं पञ्चलक्षं मधुप्लुतैः ।
प्रसूनैः करवीरोत्थैर्जुहुयात्तहृशांशतः ॥
1.91.m: Meditating thus, one should recite the mantra five hundred thousand times; / with oleander blossoms soaked in honey, one should offer oblations amounting to one-tenth of that.

1.91.s:
pūrvodite yajetpīṭhe martiṃ mūlena kalpayet /
āvāhya pūjayettasyāṃ mūrtāvāvaraṇaiḥ saha //
1.91.d:
पूर्वोदिते यजेत्पीठे मर्तिं मूलेन कल्पयेत् ।
आवाह्य पूजयेत्तस्यां मूर्तावावरणैः सह ॥
1.91.m: On the previously described ritual seat, one should fashion the form with the root mantra; / having invoked [him], one should worship [him] in that form along with the surrounding deities.

1.91.s:
śaktiṃ ḍamarukābhītivarānsaṃdadhataṃ karaiḥ /
īśānaṃ trīkṣaṇaṃ śubhramaiśānyāṃ diśi pūjayet //
1.91.d:
शक्तिं डमरुकाभीतिवरान्संदधतं करैः ।
ईशानं त्रीक्षणं शुभ्रमैशान्यां दिशि पूजयेत् ॥
1.91.m: Holding in his hands a spear, a drum, and the gestures of fearlessness and boon-giving, / one should worship white, three-eyed Īśāna in the northeast quarter;

1.91.s:
paraśveṇavarābhītīrdadhānaṃ vidyudujjvalam /
caturmukhaṃ tatpuruṣaṃ trinetraṃ pūrvantor'cayet //
1.91.d:
परश्वेणवराभीतीर्दधानं विद्युदुज्ज्वलम् ।
चतुर्मुखं तत्पुरुषं त्रिनेत्रं पूर्वन्तोर्ऽचयेत् ॥
1.91.m: bearing an axe, an antelope, and the gestures of boon-giving and fearlessness, blazing like lightning, / one should worship four-faced, three-eyed Tatpuruṣa in the east;

1.91.s:
akṣasrajaṃ vedapāśau ṛṣiṇḍamarukaṃ tataḥ /
khaṭvāṅgaṃ niśitaṃ śūlaṃ kapālaṃ bibhrataṃ karaiḥ //
1.91.d:
अक्षस्रजं वेदपाशौ ऋषिण्डमरुकं ततः ।
खट्वाङ्गं निशितं शूलं कपालं बिभ्रतं करैः ॥
1.91.m: holding in his hands a rosary, the Veda, a noose, a sword, a drum, / a skull-staff, a sharp trident, and a skull-cup,

1.91.s:
añjanābhaṃ caturvaktraṃ bhīmadantaṃ bhayāvaham /
aghoraṃ trīkṣaṇaṃ yāmye pūjayenmantravittamaḥ //
1.91.d:
अञ्जनाभं चतुर्वक्त्रं भीमदन्तं भयावहम् ।
अघोरं त्रीक्षणं याम्ये पूजयेन्मन्त्रवित्तमः ॥
1.91.m: resembling collyrium, four-faced, with dreadful fangs, terrifying, / the best knower of mantras should worship three-eyed Aghora in the south;

1.91.s:
kuṅkumābhacaturvaktraṃ vāmadevaṃ trilocanam /
hariṇākṣaguṇābhītivarahastaṃ caturmukham //
1.91.d:
कुङ्कुमाभचतुर्वक्त्रं वामदेवं त्रिलोचनम् ।
हरिणाक्षगुणाभीतिवरहस्तं चतुर्मुखम् ॥
1.91.m: having four faces resembling saffron, three-eyed Vāmadeva, / having hands with an antelope, a rosary, and the gestures of fearlessness and boon-giving, four-faced,

1.91.s:
bālenduśekharollāsimukuṭaṃ paścime yajet /
karpūredunibhaṃ saumyaṃ sadyojātaṃ trilocanam //
1.91.d:
बालेन्दुशेखरोल्लासिमुकुटं पश्चिमे यजेत् ।
कर्पूरेदुनिभं सौम्यं सद्योजातं त्रिलोचनम् ॥
1.91.m: with a crown radiant with the crest of the young moon, one should worship in the west; / resembling camphor and the moon, gentle, three-eyed Sadyojāta,

1.91.s:
varābhayākṣavalayakuṭhārāndadhataṃ karaiḥ /
vilāsinaṃ smeravaktraṃ saumye samyaksamarcayet //
1.91.d:
वराभयाक्षवलयकुठारान्दधतं करैः ।
विलासिनं स्मेरवक्त्रं सौम्ये सम्यक्समर्चयेत् ॥
1.91.m: holding in his hands the gestures of boon-giving and fearlessness, a rosary, and an axe, / graceful, with a smiling face, one should properly worship in the north.

1.91.s:
koṇeṣvarcennivṛttyādyāstejorūpāḥ kalāḥ kramāt /
vighneśvarānanantādyānpatreṣu parito yajet //
1.91.d:
कोणेष्वर्चेन्निवृत्त्याद्यास्तेजोरूपाः कलाः क्रमात् ।
विघ्नेश्वराननन्ताद्यान्पत्रेषु परितो यजेत् ॥
1.91.m: In the intermediate corners one should worship the kalās beginning with Nivṛtti, whose form is light, in order; / one should worship Vighneśvara and those beginning with Ananta all around on the petals;

1.91.s:
umādikāstato bāhye śakrādyānāyudhaiḥ saha /
iti saṃpūjya deveśaṃ bhaktyā paramayā yutaḥ //
1.91.d:
उमादिकास्ततो बाह्ये शक्राद्यानायुधैः सह ।
इति संपूज्य देवेशं भक्त्या परमया युतः ॥
1.91.m: outside them, those beginning with Umā; and then those beginning with Śakra along with their weapons. / Having thus worshipped the Lord of gods, endowed with supreme devotion,

1.91.s:
praṇīyennṛtyagītādyaiḥ stotramairtrīṃ manoharaiḥ /
tāro māyāviyadbindumanusvarasamanvitaḥ //
1.91.d:
प्रणीयेन्नृत्यगीताद्यैः स्तोत्रमैर्त्रीं मनोहरैः ।
तारो मायावियद्बिन्दुमनुस्वरसमन्वितः ॥
1.91.m: one should present charming hymns of praise with dances, songs, and the like. / The praṇava, the Māyā-bīja, ether, bindu, accompanied by the anusvāra,

1.91.s:
pañcākṣarasamāyukto vasuvarṇo manurmataḥ /
pañcākṣaroktavatkuryādaṅganyāsādikaṃ budhaḥ //
1.91.d:
पञ्चाक्षरसमायुक्तो वसुवर्णो मनुर्मतः ।
पञ्चाक्षरोक्तवत्कुर्यादङ्गन्यासादिकं बुधः ॥
1.91.m: combined with the five-syllable mantra, is considered the eight-syllabled mantra. / The wise man should perform the ritual placement of limbs and other rites as spoken for the five-syllable mantra:

1.91.s:
siṃdūrābhaṃ lasadratnamukuṭaṃ candramaulinam /
divyabhūṣāṅgarāgaṃ ca nāgayajñopavītinam //
1.91.d:
सिंदूराभं लसद्रत्नमुकुटं चन्द्रमौलिनम् ।
दिव्यभूषाङ्गरागं च नागयज्ञोपवीतिनम् ॥
1.91.m: resembling vermilion, having a glittering crown of gems, bearing the moon on his crest, / having divine ornaments and unguents, wearing a serpent as a sacred thread,

1.91.s:
vāmorusthapriyorojanyastahastaṃ ca bibhratam /
vedaṭaṅkeṣmabhayaṃ dhyāyetsarveśvaraṃ śivam //
1.91.d:
वामोरुस्थप्रियोरोजन्यस्तहस्तं च बिभ्रतम् ।
वेदटङ्केष्मभयं ध्यायेत्सर्वेश्वरं शिवम् ॥
1.91.m: holding the gestures of the Veda, a chisel, arrows, and fearlessness, / with a hand placed upon the breast of his beloved on his left thigh—one should meditate on Śiva, the Lord of all.

1.91.s:
aṣṭalakṣaṃ japenmantraṃ tatsahasraṃ ghṛtānvitaiḥ /
pāyasairjuhuyātpīṭhemūrtiṃ saṃkalpya mūlataḥ //
1.91.d:
अष्टलक्षं जपेन्मन्त्रं तत्सहस्रं घृतान्वितैः ।
पायसैर्जुहुयात्पीठेमूर्तिं संकल्प्य मूलतः ॥
1.91.m: One should recite the mantra eight hundred thousand times, and offer eight thousand oblations of milk-rice / mixed with clarified butter on the ritual seat, having fashioned the form with the root mantra.

1.91.s:
aṅgairāvaraṇaṃ pūrvamanantādyairanantaram /
umādibhiḥ samuddiṣṭaṃ tṛtīyaṃ lokanāyakaiḥ //
1.91.d:
अङ्गैरावरणं पूर्वमनन्ताद्यैरनन्तरम् ।
उमादिभिः समुद्दिष्टं तृतीयं लोकनायकैः ॥
1.91.m: The first enclosure is with the limbs; the next is with those beginning with Ananta; / the third is indicated with those beginning with Umā; with the world-guardians

1.91.s:
caturthaṃ pañcamaṃ teṣāmāyudhaiḥ parikīrtitam /
evaṃ pratidinaṃ devaṃ pūjayetsādhakottamaḥ //
1.91.d:
चतुर्थं पञ्चमं तेषामायुधैः परिकीर्तितम् ।
एवं प्रतिदिनं देवं पूजयेत्साधकोत्तमः ॥
1.91.m: is the fourth; and the fifth is proclaimed with their weapons. / Thus every day the excellent practitioner should worship the god;

1.91.s:
putrapautrādigāṃ lakṣmīṃ saṃprāpyahyatra modate /
tāraḥ sthirā sakarṇendurbhaghṛguḥ sargasamanvitaḥ //
1.91.d:
पुत्रपौत्रादिगां लक्ष्मीं संप्राप्यह्यत्र मोदते ।
तारः स्थिरा सकर्णेन्दुर्भघृगुः सर्गसमन्वितः ॥
1.91.m: having obtained fortune that extends to sons and grandsons, he rejoices here in this world. / The praṇava, Sthirā with the ear and moon, Bha, and Bhṛgu with the visarga—

1.91.s:
akṣarātmā nigadito mantro mṛtyuñjayātmakaḥ /
ṛṣaiḥ kaholo devyādigāyatrī chanda īritam //
1.91.d:
अक्षरात्मा निगदितो मन्त्रो मृत्युञ्जयात्मकः ।
ऋषैः कहोलो देव्यादिगायत्री छन्द ईरितम् ॥
1.91.m: this is proclaimed as the mantra composed of syllables, whose essence is Mṛtyuñjaya. / The sage is Kahola; the meter is declared as Daivī-Gāyatrī;

1.91.s:
mṛtyuñjayo mahādevo devatāsya samīritaḥ /
bhṛguṇā dīrghayuktena ṣaḍaṅgāni samācaret //
1.91.d:
मृत्युञ्जयो महादेवो देवतास्य समीरितः ।
भृगुणा दीर्घयुक्तेन षडङ्गानि समाचरेत् ॥
1.91.m: the deity of this is declared as Mṛtyuñjaya Mahādeva. / With Bhṛgu accompanied by the long vowels, one should perform the six limbs.

1.91.s:
candrārkahutabhuṅnetraṃ smitāsyaṃ yugmapadmagam /
mudrāpāśaiṇākṣasūtralasatpāṇiṃ śaśiprabham //
1.91.d:
चन्द्रार्कहुतभुङ्नेत्रं स्मितास्यं युग्मपद्मगम् ।
मुद्रापाशैणाक्षसूत्रलसत्पाणिं शशिप्रभम् ॥
1.91.m: With the moon, sun, and fire as his eyes, with a smiling face, seated on twin lotuses, / his hands shining with the mudrā, noose, antelope, and rosary, having the radiance of the moon,

1.91.s:
bhālenduvigalantpīyūṣaplutāṅgamalaṅkṛtam /
hārādyairnijakāntyā tu dhyāyedviśvavimohanam //
1.91.d:
भालेन्दुविगलन्त्पीयूषप्लुताङ्गमलङ्कृतम् ।
हाराद्यैर्निजकान्त्या तु ध्यायेद्विश्वविमोहनम् ॥
1.91.m: his body bathed in the nectar trickling from the crest-moon, adorned / with necklaces and the like, enchanting the universe with his own splendor, one should meditate on him.

1.91.s:
guṇalakṣaṃ japenmantraṃ taddaśāṃśaṃ hunetsudhīḥ /
amṛtāśakalaiḥ śuddhadugdhājyasamabhiplutaiḥ //
1.91.d:
गुणलक्षं जपेन्मन्त्रं तद्दशांशं हुनेत्सुधीः ।
अमृताशकलैः शुद्धदुग्धाज्यसमभिप्लुतैः ॥
1.91.m: The wise person should recite the mantra three hundred thousand times, and offer oblations of one-tenth of that / with pieces of guḍūcī drenched in pure milk and clarified butter.

1.91.s:
śaive saṃpūjayetpīṭhe mūrtiṃ saṃkalpamūlataḥ /
aṅgāvaraṇamārādhyapaścāllokeśvarānyajet //
1.91.d:
शैवे संपूजयेत्पीठे मूर्तिं संकल्पमूलतः ।
अङ्गावरणमाराध्यपश्चाल्लोकेश्वरान्यजेत् ॥
1.91.m: On a Śaiva ritual seat, having fashioned the form with the root mantra, one should worship [him]; / having worshiped the enclosure of the limbs, one should next worship the world-guardians;

1.91.s:
tadastrāṇi tato bāhye pūjayetsādhakottamaḥ /
japapūjādibhiḥ siddhe mantre 'sminmunisattama //
1.91.d:
तदस्त्राणि ततो बाह्ये पूजयेत्साधकोत्तमः ।
जपपूजादिभिः सिद्धे मन्त्रे ऽस्मिन्मुनिसत्तम ॥
1.91.m: outside them, the excellent practitioner should worship their weapons. / When this mantra has been perfected through recitation, worship, and the like, O best of sages,

1.91.s:
kuryātprayogānkalyoktānabhīṣṭaphalasiddhaye /
dugdhasiktaiḥ sudhākhaṇḍairhutvā pratyahamādarāt //
1.91.d:
कुर्यात्प्रयोगान्कल्योक्तानभीष्टफलसिद्धये ।
दुग्धसिक्तैः सुधाखण्डैर्हुत्वा प्रत्यहमादरात् ॥
1.91.m: one should perform the ritual applications spoken for ceremonies to accomplish desired fruits. / By offering daily with respect one thousand oblations of pieces of guḍūcī

1.91.s:
sahasramāsaparyantaṃ labhedāyurdhanaṃ sutān /
sudhāvaṭatitānpūrvā payaḥ sarpiḥ payo haviḥ //
1.91.d:
सहस्रमासपर्यन्तं लभेदायुर्धनं सुतान् ।
सुधावटतितान्पूर्वा पयः सर्पिः पयो हविः ॥
1.91.m: moistened with milk for a month, one attains lifespan, wealth, and sons. / Guḍūcī, banyan, sesame, and those previously mentioned, milk, clarified butter, and sacrificial food—

1.91.s:
sapta dravyāṇi vāreṣu kramāddaśaśataṃ hunet /
saptādhikān dvijānnityaṃ bhojayenmadhurānvitam //
1.91.d:
सप्त द्रव्याणि वारेषु क्रमाद्दशशतं हुनेत् ।
सप्ताधिकान् द्विजान्नित्यं भोजयेन्मधुरान्वितम् ॥
1.91.m: one should offer one thousand oblations of these seven substances in sequence on the days of the week; / daily one should feed seven and more twice-born men with sweet food.

1.91.s:
ṛtvigbhyo dakṣiṇāṃ dadyādaruṇāṃ gāṃ payasvinīm /
guruṃ saṃprīṇayetpaścāddhanādyairdevatādhiyā //
1.91.d:
ऋत्विग्भ्यो दक्षिणां दद्यादरुणां गां पयस्विनीम् ।
गुरुं संप्रीणयेत्पश्चाद्धनाद्यैर्देवताधिया ॥
1.91.m: He should give a sacrificial fee to the officiating priests consisting of a red milch cow; / afterwards, he should gratify the guru with wealth and other gifts, regarding him as the deity.

1.91.s:
anena vidhinā sādhyaḥ kṛtyādrohajvaṃrādibhiḥ /
vimuktaḥ suciraṃ jīveccharadāṃ śatamañjasā //
1.91.d:
अनेन विधिना साध्यः कृत्याद्रोहज्वंरादिभिः ।
विमुक्तः सुचिरं जीवेच्छरदां शतमञ्जसा ॥
1.91.m: By this procedure, the person to be cured is freed from malignant sorcery, enmity, fever, and the like, / and will certainly live for a full hundred autumns for a very long time.

1.91.s:
abhicāre jvare staṃbhaghoronmāde śirogade /
asādhyaroge kṣveḍārtauṃ mohe dāhe mahābhaye //
1.91.d:
अभिचारे ज्वरे स्तंभघोरोन्मादे शिरोगदे ।
असाध्यरोगे क्ष्वेडार्तौं मोहे दाहे महाभये ॥
1.91.m: In sorcery, fever, paralysis, terrible madness, head diseases, / incurable illness, affliction by poison, delusion, burning fever, and great peril,

1.91.s:
homo 'yaṃ śāntidaḥ proktaḥ sarvābhayapradāyakaḥ /
dravyairetaiḥ prajuhuyāttrijanmasu yathāvidhi //
1.91.d:
होमो ऽयं शान्तिदः प्रोक्तः सर्वाभयप्रदायकः ।
द्रव्यैरेतैः प्रजुहुयात्त्रिजन्मसु यथाविधि ॥
1.91.m: this fire oblation is declared to bring pacification and bestow freedom from all fears. / One should offer oblations with these substances according to the rules during three consecutive birth-stars.

1.91.s:
bhojayenmadhurairbhojyairbrāhmaṇānvedapāragān /
dīrghamāyuravāpnoti vāñchitāṃ vindati śriyam //
1.91.d:
भोजयेन्मधुरैर्भोज्यैर्ब्राह्मणान्वेदपारगान् ।
दीर्घमायुरवाप्नोति वाञ्छितां विन्दति श्रियम् ॥
1.91.m: One should feed brāhmaṇas who have mastered the Vedas with sweet foods; / [then] he attains a long lifespan and obtains the wealth he desires.

1.91.s:
ekādaśāhutīrnityaṃ dūrvābhirjuhuyād budhaḥ /
apamṛtyujideva syādāyurārogyavarddhanam //
1.91.d:
एकादशाहुतीर्नित्यं दूर्वाभिर्जुहुयाद् बुधः ।
अपमृत्युजिदेव स्यादायुरारोग्यवर्द्धनम् ॥
1.91.m: A wise man should daily offer eleven oblations of dūrvā grass; / he indeed overcomes untimely death, and his lifespan and health increase.

1.91.s:
trijanmasu sudhāvallīkāśmīrībakulodbhavaiḥ /
samidvaraiḥ kṛto homaḥ sarvamṛtyugadāpahaḥ //
1.91.d:
त्रिजन्मसु सुधावल्लीकाश्मीरीबकुलोद्भवैः ।
समिद्वरैः कृतो होमः सर्वमृत्युगदापहः ॥
1.91.m: During three consecutive birth-stars, a fire oblation performed with excellent kindling-sticks / from the amṛtavallī vine, the kāśmīrī tree, and the bakula tree removes all deaths and diseases.

1.91.s:
siddhārthairvihito homo mahājvaravināśanaḥ /
apāmārgasamiddhomaḥ sarvāmayaniṣūdanaḥ //
1.91.d:
सिद्धार्थैर्विहितो होमो महाज्वरविनाशनः ।
अपामार्गसमिद्धोमः सर्वामयनिषूदनः ॥
1.91.m: A fire oblation performed with white mustard seeds destroys severe fever; / a fire oblation with apāmārga kindling-sticks eradicates all sicknesses.

1.91.s:
dakṣiṇāmūrtaye pūrvaṃ tubhyaṃ padamanantaram /
vaṭamūlapadasyānte pravadecca nivāsine //
1.91.d:
दक्षिणामूर्तये पूर्वं तुभ्यं पदमनन्तरम् ।
वटमूलपदस्यान्ते प्रवदेच्च निवासिने ॥
1.91.m: First the word 'dakṣiṇāmūrtaye', followed by the word 'tubhyam', / and after the word 'vaṭamūla' one should say 'nivāsine';

1.91.s:
dhyānaikaniratāṅgāya paścād brūyānnamaḥ padam /
rudrāya śaṃbhave tāraśaktiruddho 'yamīritaḥ //
1.91.d:
ध्यानैकनिरताङ्गाय पश्चाद् ब्रूयान्नमः पदम् ।
रुद्राय शंभवे तारशक्तिरुद्धो ऽयमीरितः ॥
1.91.m: then one should say 'dhyānaikaniratāṅgāya', followed by the word 'namaḥ', / and 'rudrāya śaṃbhave'; this [mantra] is declared to be enclosed by the tāra and śakti [bījas].

1.91.s:
ṣaṭtriṃśadakṣaro mantraḥ sarvakāmaphalapradaḥ /
muniḥ śukaḥ samuddiṣṭaśchando 'nuṣṭupprakīrtitam //
1.91.d:
षट्त्रिंशदक्षरो मन्त्रः सर्वकामफलप्रदः ।
मुनिः शुकः समुद्दिष्टश्छन्दो ऽनुष्टुप्प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
1.91.m: This thirty-six-syllable mantra bestows the fruit of all desires. / The sage is declared to be Śuka, the meter is proclaimed to be anuṣṭubh,

1.91.s:
devatā dakṣiṇāmūrtirnāmnā śaṃbhurudīritaḥ /
tāraśaktiyuktaiḥ pūrvaṃ hrīmādyantaiśca mantrajaiḥ //
1.91.d:
देवता दक्षिणामूर्तिर्नाम्ना शंभुरुदीरितः ।
तारशक्तियुक्तैः पूर्वं ह्रीमाद्यन्तैश्च मन्त्रजैः ॥
1.91.m: and the deity is stated to be Dakṣiṇāmūrti, named Śambhu. / Enjoined with the tāra and śakti [bījas] preceded and followed by hrīm, generated from the mantra,

1.91.s:
ṣaṭṣaṣṭhāṣṭeṣu vahnyarṇairhṛdayādyaṅgakalpanam /
mūrdhni bhāle dṛśoḥ śrotre gaṇḍayugme sanāsike //
1.91.d:
षट्षष्ठाष्टेषु वह्न्यर्णैर्हृदयाद्यङ्गकल्पनम् ।
मूर्ध्नि भाले दृशोः श्रोत्रे गण्डयुग्मे सनासिके ॥
1.91.m: with syllables of fire, the assignment of the limbs beginning with the heart is performed on the sixth, sixth, and eighth. / On the crown of the head, the forehead, the eyes, the ears, the pair of cheeks, along with the nose,

1.91.s:
āsyadoḥsaṃdhiṣu gale stanahṛnnābhimaṇḍale /
kaṭyāṃ guhye punaḥ pādasaṃdhiṣvarṇānnyasenmanoḥ //
1.91.d:
आस्यदोःसंधिषु गले स्तनहृन्नाभिमण्डले ।
कट्यां गुह्ये पुनः पादसंधिष्वर्णान्न्यसेन्मनोः ॥
1.91.m: in the mouth, the arm-joints, the neck, the breast, heart, and navel-circle, / on the waist, the secret organ, and the foot-joints, one should rituals place the syllables of the mantra.

1.91.s:
vyāpakaṃ tāraśaktibhyāṃ kuryāddehe tataḥ param /
himācalataṭe ramye siddhikinnarasevite //
1.91.d:
व्यापकं तारशक्तिभ्यां कुर्याद्देहे ततः परम् ।
हिमाचलतटे रम्ये सिद्धिकिन्नरसेविते ॥
1.91.m: After that, he should perform the pervasive ritual placement on his body with the tāra and śakti [bījas]. / On the lovely slope of the Himālaya, frequented by Siddhas and Kinnaras,

1.91.s:
vividhadrumaśākhābhiḥ sarvato vāritātape /
supuṣpitairlatājālairāśliṣṭakusumadrume //
1.91.d:
विविधद्रुमशाखाभिः सर्वतो वारितातपे ।
सुपुष्पितैर्लताजालैराश्लिष्टकुसुमद्रुमे ॥
1.91.m: where the heat of the sun is kept away on all sides by the branches of various trees, / where flowering trees are embraced by networks of creepers in full bloom,

1.91.s:
śilāvivaranirgacchannirjharānilaśītale /
gāyaddevāṅganāsaṃghe nṛtyadbarhi kadambake //
1.91.d:
शिलाविवरनिर्गच्छन्निर्झरानिलशीतले ।
गायद्देवाङ्गनासंघे नृत्यद्बर्हि कदम्बके ॥
1.91.m: cooled by the breezes of waterfalls emerging from crevices in the rocks, / where groups of celestial maidens sing and flocks of peacocks dance,

1.91.s:
kūjatkokilasaṃghena mukharīkṛtadiṅmukhe /
parasparavinirmuktamātsaryamṛgasevite //
1.91.d:
कूजत्कोकिलसंघेन मुखरीकृतदिङ्मुखे ।
परस्परविनिर्मुक्तमात्सर्यमृगसेविते ॥
1.91.m: the quarters of which are resounded by the cooing of cuckoo flocks, / frequented by beasts that have mutually cast aside their animosity,

1.91.s:
jalajaiḥ sthalajaiḥ puṣpairāmodibhiralaṅkṛte /
ādyaiḥ śukādyairmunibhirajasrasukhasevite //
1.91.d:
जलजैः स्थलजैः पुष्पैरामोदिभिरलङ्कृते ।
आद्यैः शुकाद्यैर्मुनिभिरजस्रसुखसेविते ॥
1.91.m: adorned with fragrant water-born and land-born flowers, / attended continually with joy by primal sages beginning with Śuka,

1.91.s:
purandaramukhairdevaiḥ sāṃganādyairvilokite /
vaṭavṛkṣaṃ mahocchrāyaṃ padmarāgaphalojjlam //
1.91.d:
पुरन्दरमुखैर्देवैः सांगनाद्यैर्विलोकिते ।
वटवृक्षं महोच्छ्रायं पद्मरागफलोज्ज्लम् ॥
1.91.m: and gazed upon by gods headed by Indra accompanied by their wives; / [there stands] a banyan tree of great height, brilliant with ruby fruits,

1.91.s:
gārutmatamayaiḥ patrairnibiḍairupaśobhitam /
navaratnamayākalpairlaṃbamānairalaṅkṛtam //
1.91.d:
गारुत्मतमयैः पत्रैर्निबिडैरुपशोभितम् ।
नवरत्नमयाकल्पैर्लंबमानैरलङ्कृतम् ॥
1.91.m: beautified by dense leaves made of emerald, / and decorated with hanging ornaments made of the nine gems,

1.91.s:
saṃsāratāpavicchedakuśalacchāyamadbhutam /
tasya mūle susaṃkḷptaratnasiṃhāsane śubhe //
1.91.d:
संसारतापविच्छेदकुशलच्छायमद्भुतम् ।
तस्य मूले सुसंकॢप्तरत्नसिंहासने शुभे ॥
1.91.m: whose wondrous shade is capable of cutting off the distress of saṃsāra. / At its base, upon an auspicious, well-fashioned lion-seat of jewels,

1.91.s:
āsīnamasitākalpaṃ śaraccandranibhānanam /
kailāsādrinibhaṃ tryakṣaṃ candrāṅkitakapardakam //
1.91.d:
आसीनमसिताकल्पं शरच्चन्द्रनिभाननम् ।
कैलासाद्रिनिभं त्र्यक्षं चन्द्राङ्कितकपर्दकम् ॥
1.91.m: seated, wearing dark ornaments, with a face resembling the autumn moon, / resembling Mount Kailāsa, three-eyed, with matted hair adorned by the moon,

1.91.s:
nāsāgrālokanaparaṃ vīrāsanasamāsthitam /
bhadrāṭake kuraṅgāḍhyajānusthakarapallavam //
1.91.d:
नासाग्रालोकनपरं वीरासनसमास्थितम् ।
भद्राटके कुरङ्गाढ्यजानुस्थकरपल्लवम् ॥
1.91.m: intent on gazing at the tip of his nose, seated firmly in the vīrāsana posture, / his sprout-like hands resting on his knees, adorned with a deer upon an auspicious cloth,

1.91.s:
kakṣābaddhabhujaṅgaṃ ca suprasannaṃ haraṃ smaret /
ayutadvayasaṃyuktaguṇalakṣaṃ japenmanum //
1.91.d:
कक्षाबद्धभुजङ्गं च सुप्रसन्नं हरं स्मरेत् ।
अयुतद्वयसंयुक्तगुणलक्षं जपेन्मनुम् ॥
1.91.m: with a serpent bound around his chest, one should meditate on Hara, exceedingly serene. / One should recite the mantra for three hundred and twenty thousand times.

1.91.s:
taddaśāṃśaṃ tilaiḥ śuddhairjuhuyātkṣīrasaṃyutaiḥ /
pañcākṣarodite pīṭhe tadvidhānena pūjayet //
1.91.d:
तद्दशांशं तिलैः शुद्धैर्जुहुयात्क्षीरसंयुतैः ।
पञ्चाक्षरोदिते पीठे तद्विधानेन पूजयेत् ॥
1.91.m: One should offer one-tenth of that as fire oblations with pure sesame seeds mixed with milk; / he should worship him on the seat prescribed for the five-syllable [mantra] in accordance with its procedure.

1.91.s:
bhikṣāhāro japenmāsaṃ manumenaṃ jitendriyaḥ /
nityaṃ sahasramaṣṭārddhaṃ parāṃ vindati vākchriyam //
1.91.d:
भिक्षाहारो जपेन्मासं मनुमेनं जितेन्द्रियः ।
नित्यं सहस्रमष्टार्द्धं परां विन्दति वाक्छ्रियम् ॥
1.91.m: Subsisting on begged food, with senses conquered, one should recite this mantra for a month; / reciting four thousand [times] daily, he attains supreme eloquence.

1.91.s:
trivāraṃ japtametena payastu manunā pibet /
dakṣiṇāmūrtiṃsaṃdhyānācchāstravyākhyānakṛdbhavet //
1.91.d:
त्रिवारं जप्तमेतेन पयस्तु मनुना पिबेत् ।
दक्षिणामूर्तिंसंध्यानाच्छास्त्रव्याख्यानकृद्भवेत् ॥
1.91.m: One should drink milk consecrated three times with this mantra; / through intense meditation on Dakṣiṇāmūrti, he will become an expositor of the scriptures.

1.91.s:
praṇavo hṛdayaṃ paścādvadedbhagavatepadam /
ṅeyutaṃ dakṣiṇāmūrtiṃ mahyaṃmedhāmudīrayet //
1.91.d:
प्रणवो हृदयं पश्चाद्वदेद्भगवतेपदम् ।
ङेयुतं दक्षिणामूर्तिं मह्यंमेधामुदीरयेत् ॥
1.91.m: The praṇava, then the heart [mantra], and one should say the word 'bhagavate'; / accompanied by the dative case, one should pronounce 'Dakṣiṇāmūrti', [then] 'mahyam' and 'medhām'.

1.91.s:
prayaccha ṭhadvayānto 'yaṃ dvāviṃśatyakṣaro manuḥ /
muniścaturmukhaśchando gāyatrī devatoditā //
1.91.d:
प्रयच्छ ठद्वयान्तो ऽयं द्वाविंशत्यक्षरो मनुः ।
मुनिश्चतुर्मुखश्छन्दो गायत्री देवतोदिता ॥
1.91.m: 'prayaccha', ending in a pair of ṭhas—this is the twenty-two-syllable mantra. / The four-faced Brahmā is the sage, the meter is gāyatrī, and the deity is proclaimed [to be Dakṣiṇāmūrti].

1.91.s:
tāraruddhaiḥ svarairdīrghaiḥ ṣaḍbhiraṅgāni kalpayet /
padairmantrabhavairvāpidhyānādyaṃ pūrvavanmatam //
1.91.d:
ताररुद्धैः स्वरैर्दीर्घैः षड्भिरङ्गानि कल्पयेत् ।
पदैर्मन्त्रभवैर्वापिध्यानाद्यं पूर्ववन्मतम् ॥
1.91.m: One should configure the limbs with the six long vowels enclosed by the tāra, / or else with the words arising from the mantra; the meditation and other rites are held to be as before.

1.91.s:
lohitogryāsanaḥ sadyo bindumānprathamaṃ tataḥ /
dvitīyaṃ vahnibījasthā dīrghā śāntīndubhūṣitā //
1.91.d:
लोहितोग्र्यासनः सद्यो बिन्दुमान्प्रथमं ततः ।
द्वितीयं वह्निबीजस्था दीर्घा शान्तीन्दुभूषिता ॥
1.91.m: Red, with a fierce seat, sadyo[jāta], with the bindu is the first; then / the second is situated in the seed-syllable of fire, long, and adorned with peace and the moon;

1.91.s:
tṛtīyā lāṅgalīśārṇamantro bījatrayānvitaḥ /
nīlakaṇṭhātmakaḥ prokto viṣadvayaharaḥ paraḥ //
1.91.d:
तृतीया लाङ्गलीशार्णमन्त्रो बीजत्रयान्वितः ।
नीलकण्ठात्मकः प्रोक्तो विषद्वयहरः परः ॥
1.91.m: the third is the syllable of the holder of the plow; this mantra endowed with the three seed-syllables / is declared to be the embodiment of Nīlakaṇṭha, the supreme remover of both types of poison.

1.91.s:
haradvayaṃ vahnijāyā hṛdayaṃ parikīrtitam /
kaparddine padayugaṃ śiromantra udāhṛtaḥ //
1.91.d:
हरद्वयं वह्निजाया हृदयं परिकीर्तितम् ।
कपर्द्दिने पदयुगं शिरोमन्त्र उदाहृतः ॥
1.91.m: The two Haras with the wife of Agni are declared to be the heart mantra; / the pair of words 'kapardine' is said to be the head mantra.

1.91.s:
nīlakaṇṭhāya ṭhadvandvaṃ śikhāmantro 'yamīritaḥ /
kālakūṭapadasyānte viṣabhakṣaṇaṅeyutam //
1.91.d:
नीलकण्ठाय ठद्वन्द्वं शिखामन्त्रो ऽयमीरितः ।
कालकूटपदस्यान्ते विषभक्षणङेयुतम् ॥
1.91.m: 'To Nīlakaṇṭha' followed by a pair of ṭhas is declared to be the tuft mantra; / after the word 'kālakūṭa', 'viṣabhakṣaṇāya' ending in the fourth case-ending,

1.91.s:
huṃ phaṭ kavacamuddiṣṭaṃ nīlakaṇṭhina ityataḥ /
svāhāntamastrametāni pañcāgāni manorviduḥ //
1.91.d:
हुं फट् कवचमुद्दिष्टं नीलकण्ठिन इत्यतः ।
स्वाहान्तमस्त्रमेतानि पञ्चागानि मनोर्विदुः ॥
1.91.m: huṃ phaṭ is stated to be the armor mantra; from 'nīlakaṇṭhine' / ending with svāhā is the weapon mantra; they know these as the five limbs of the mantra.

1.91.s:
mūrdhni kaṇṭhe hṛdaṃbhoje kramādvījatrayaṃ nyaset /
bālārkāyutavarcaskaṃ jaṭājūṭenduśobhitam //
1.91.d:
मूर्ध्नि कण्ठे हृदंभोजे क्रमाद्वीजत्रयं न्यसेत् ।
बालार्कायुतवर्चस्कं जटाजूटेन्दुशोभितम् ॥
1.91.m: On the crown of the head, the throat, and the heart lotus, one should place the three seed-syllables in order. / Possessing the luster of ten thousand morning suns, adorned by the moon in his matted locks,

1.91.s:
nāgābhūṣaṃ japavaṭīṃ śūlaṃ brahmakapālakam /
khaṭvāṅgaṃ dadhataṃ dorbhistrinetraṃ cintayeddharam //
1.91.d:
नागाभूषं जपवटीं शूलं ब्रह्मकपालकम् ।
खट्वाङ्गं दधतं दोर्भिस्त्रिनेत्रं चिन्तयेद्धरम् ॥
1.91.m: wearing serpent ornaments, holding a rosary, a trident, Brahmā’s skull, / and a khaṭvāṅga staff in his arms, one should contemplate the three-eyed Hara.

1.91.s:
lakṣatrayaṃ japenmantraṃ taddaśāṃśaṃ sasarpiṣā /
haviṣā juhuyātsamyaksaṃskṛte havyavāhane //
1.91.d:
लक्षत्रयं जपेन्मन्त्रं तद्दशांशं ससर्पिषा ।
हविषा जुहुयात्सम्यक्संस्कृते हव्यवाहने ॥
1.91.m: One should recite the mantra three hundred thousand times; one should offer one-tenth of that as fire oblations / with sacrificial offerings along with ghee, in the properly consecrated fire.

1.91.s:
śaivaṃ pīṭhe yajeddevaṃ nīlakaṇṭhaṃ samāhitaḥ /
mṛtyuṃ jayavidhānena viṣadvayavināśanam //
1.91.d:
शैवं पीठे यजेद्देवं नीलकण्ठं समाहितः ।
मृत्युं जयविधानेन विषद्वयविनाशनम् ॥
1.91.m: With a concentrated mind, he should worship Lord Nīlakaṇṭha on the Śaiva seat, / according to the procedure of Mṛtyuñjaya, for the destruction of both types of poison.

1.91.s:
agniḥ saṃvartakādityarānilau ṣaṣṭibindumān /
cintāmaṇiriti khyātaṃ bījaṃ sarvasamṛddhidam //
1.91.d:
अग्निः संवर्तकादित्यरानिलौ षष्टिबिन्दुमान् ।
चिन्तामणिरिति ख्यातं बीजं सर्वसमृद्धिदम् ॥
1.91.m: Agni, Saṃvartaka, Aditya, Ra, and Anila, with the sixtieth [letter] and the bindu, / is the seed-syllable renowned as Cintāmaṇi, which bestows all prosperity.

1.91.s:
kaśyapo munirākhyātaśchando 'nuṣṭubudāhṛtam /
arddhanārīśvaraḥ prokto devatā jagatāṃ patiḥ //
1.91.d:
कश्यपो मुनिराख्यातश्छन्दो ऽनुष्टुबुदाहृतम् ।
अर्द्धनारीश्वरः प्रोक्तो देवता जगतां पतिः ॥
1.91.m: Kaśyapa is declared to be the sage, the meter is said to be anuṣṭubh, / and Ardhanārīśvara, the Lord of the worlds, is declared to be the deity.

1.91.s:
rephaādivyañjanaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ kuryādaṅgāni ṣaṭ kramāt /
trinetraṃ nīlamaṇibhaṃ śūlapāśaṃ kapālakam //
1.91.d:
रेफआदिव्यञ्जनैः षड्भिः कुर्यादङ्गानि षट् क्रमात् ।
त्रिनेत्रं नीलमणिभं शूलपाशं कपालकम् ॥
1.91.m: With the six consonants beginning with the letter 'ra', one should perform the six limbs in order. / Having three eyes, resembling a sapphire, bearing a trident, a noose, a skull,

1.91.s:
raktotpalaṃ ca hastābjairdadhataṃ cārubhūṣaṇam /
bālendubaddhamukuṭamarddhanārīśvaraṃ smaret //
1.91.d:
रक्तोत्पलं च हस्ताब्जैर्दधतं चारुभूषणम् ।
बालेन्दुबद्धमुकुटमर्द्धनारीश्वरं स्मरेत् ॥
1.91.m: and a red lotus with his lotus hands, having beautiful ornaments, / his crown bound with the crescent moon, one should meditate on Ardhanārīśvara.

1.91.s:
ekalakṣaṃ japenmantraṃ triśataṃ madhurāplutaiḥ /
tilairhunedyajetpīṭhe śaiveṅgāvaraṇaiḥ saha //
1.91.d:
एकलक्षं जपेन्मन्त्रं त्रिशतं मधुराप्लुतैः ।
तिलैर्हुनेद्यजेत्पीठे शैवेङ्गावरणैः सह ॥
1.91.m: One should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times, and offer three hundred oblations of sesame seeds / soaked in sweets; he should worship him on the Śaiva seat together with the limbs and enclosing deities,

1.91.s:
vṛṣādyairmātṛbhiḥ paścāllokapālaistadāyudhaiḥ /
prāsādādyaṃ japenmantramayutaṃ rogaśāntaye //
1.91.d:
वृषाद्यैर्मातृभिः पश्चाल्लोकपालैस्तदायुधैः ।
प्रासादाद्यं जपेन्मन्त्रमयुतं रोगशान्तये ॥
1.91.m: and then with the retinue beginning with the Bull, the Mothers, the world guardians, and their weapons. / One should recite the prāsāda mantra ten thousand times for the pacification of disease.

1.91.s:
svāhāvṛttamidaṃ bījaṃ vigalatparamāmṛtam /
candrabiṃbasthitaṃ mūrdhni dhyātaṃ kṣveḍagadāpaham //
1.91.d:
स्वाहावृत्तमिदं बीजं विगलत्परमामृतम् ।
चन्द्रबिंबस्थितं मूर्ध्नि ध्यातं क्ष्वेडगदापहम् ॥
1.91.m: This seed-syllable surrounded by 'svāhā', trickling supreme nectar, / situated in the orb of the moon, when meditated upon in the crown of the head, removes poison and disease.

1.91.s:
pratilomasvarāḍhyā ca bījaṃ vahnigṛhe sthitam /
rephaādivyañjanollāsiṣaṭkoṇābhivṛtaṃ bahiḥ //
1.91.d:
प्रतिलोमस्वराढ्या च बीजं वह्निगृहे स्थितम् ।
रेफआदिव्यञ्जनोल्लासिषट्कोणाभिवृतं बहिः ॥
1.91.m: Endowed with vowels in reverse order, the seed-syllable resides in the house of fire, / surrounded externally by a six-pointed figure shining with the consonants beginning with 'ra'.

1.91.s:
bhūtārtasya smṛtaṃ mūrdhni bhūtamāśu vināśayet /
pīḍitāṅge smṛtaṃ tattatpīḍāṃ śamayati dhruvam //
1.91.d:
भूतार्तस्य स्मृतं मूर्ध्नि भूतमाशु विनाशयेत् ।
पीडिताङ्गे स्मृतं तत्तत्पीडां शमयति ध्रुवम् ॥
1.91.m: Remembered on the head of one afflicted by spirits, it quickly destroys the spirit; / remembered on an aching limb, it certainly pacifies that particular pain.

1.91.s:
praṇavo hṛdayaṃ paścān ṅeṃtaḥ paśupatiḥ punaḥ /
tāro namo bhūtapadaṃ tato 'dhipataye dhruvam //
1.91.d:
प्रणवो हृदयं पश्चान् ङेंतः पशुपतिः पुनः ।
तारो नमो भूतपदं ततो ऽधिपतये ध्रुवम् ॥
1.91.m: The praṇava, the heart [namaḥ], next Paśupati in the dative case, / the tāra [oṃ], the word namaḥ, the word bhūta, and then certainly adhipataye;

1.91.s:
namorudrāya yugalaṃ khaḍgarāvaṇa śabdataḥ /
viharadvitayaṃ paścānnarīnṛtyayugaṃ pṛthak //
1.91.d:
नमोरुद्राय युगलं खड्गरावण शब्दतः ।
विहरद्वितयं पश्चान्नरीनृत्ययुगं पृथक् ॥
1.91.m: the pair namo rudrāya, from the words khaḍgarāvaṇa; / the pair vihara, next the pair narīnṛtya separately;

1.91.s:
śmaśānabhasmācitānte śaraṇyāya tataḥ param /
ghaṇṭākapālamālādidharāyeti padaṃ punaḥ //
1.91.d:
श्मशानभस्माचितान्ते शरण्याय ततः परम् ।
घण्टाकपालमालादिधरायेति पदं पुनः ॥
1.91.m: śmaśānabhasmācita, followed by the word śaraṇyāya, / then the word ghaṇṭākapālamālādidharāya;

1.91.s:
vyāghracarmapadasyānte paridhānāya tatparam /
śaśāṅkakṛtaśabdānte śekharāya tataḥ param //
1.91.d:
व्याघ्रचर्मपदस्यान्ते परिधानाय तत्परम् ।
शशाङ्ककृतशब्दान्ते शेखराय ततः परम् ॥
1.91.m: after the word vyāghracarma, then paridhānāya; / after the word śaśāṅkakṛta, then śekharāya;

1.91.s:
kṛṣṇasarpapadātpaścādvadedyajñopavītine /
balayugmaṃ calāyugmamanivartakapāline //
1.91.d:
कृष्णसर्पपदात्पश्चाद्वदेद्यज्ञोपवीतिने ।
बलयुग्मं चलायुग्ममनिवर्तकपालिने ॥
1.91.m: after the word kṛṣṇasarpa, one should utter yajñopavītine; / the pair bala, the pair calā, to anivartakapālin;

1.91.s:
hanuyugmaṃ tato bhūtāṃstrāsayadvitayaṃ punaḥ /
bhūyo maṇḍalamadhye syātkaṭayugmaṃ tataḥ param //
1.91.d:
हनुयुग्मं ततो भूतांस्त्रासयद्वितयं पुनः ।
भूयो मण्डलमध्ये स्यात्कटयुग्मं ततः परम् ॥
1.91.m: the pair hanu, then twice the word bhūtāṃstrāsaya; / further, in the middle of the diagram, the pair kaṭa should follow next;

1.91.s:
rudrāṅkuśena śamaya praveśayayugaṃ tataḥ /
āveśayayugaṃ paścāñcaṇḍāsipadamīrayet //
1.91.d:
रुद्राङ्कुशेन शमय प्रवेशययुगं ततः ।
आवेशययुगं पश्चाञ्चण्डासिपदमीरयेत् ॥
1.91.m: rudrāṅkuśena śamaya, then the pair praveśaya; / next the pair āveśaya, and one should utter the word caṇḍāsi;

1.91.s:
dhārādhipatirudro 'yaṃ jñāpayatyagnisuṃdarī /
khaḍgarāvaṇamantro 'yaṃ saptatyūrddhaśatākṣaraḥ //
1.91.d:
धाराधिपतिरुद्रो ऽयं ज्ञापयत्यग्निसुंदरी ।
खड्गरावणमन्त्रो ऽयं सप्तत्यूर्द्धशताक्षरः ॥
1.91.m: dhārādhipatirudro 'yaṃ jñāpayati, and agnisundarī [svāhā]— / this Khaḍgarāvaṇa mantra consists of one hundred and seventy syllables.

1.91.s:
bhūtādhipataye svāhā pūjāmantro 'yamīritaḥ /
siddhamantro 'yamudito japādeva prasiddhyati //
1.91.d:
भूताधिपतये स्वाहा पूजामन्त्रो ऽयमीरितः ।
सिद्धमन्त्रो ऽयमुदितो जपादेव प्रसिद्ध्यति ॥
1.91.m: ‘Bhūtādhipataye svāhā’ is declared to be the worship mantra. / This is declared to be a perfected mantra; it is accomplished merely by recitation.

1.91.s:
ayutadvitayātpaścādbhūtādigrahaṇe kṣamaḥ /
māyā sphuradvayaṃ bhūyaḥ prasphuradvitayaṃ punaḥ //
1.91.d:
अयुतद्वितयात्पश्चाद्भूतादिग्रहणे क्षमः ।
माया स्फुरद्वयं भूयः प्रस्फुरद्वितयं पुनः ॥
1.91.m: After twenty thousand [recitations], one is capable of seizing spirits and the like. / Māyā [hrīṃ], twice sphura, then twice prasphura;

1.91.s:
ghātayadvitayaṃ varmaphaḍantaḥ samudīritaḥ /
ekapañcāśadarṇo 'yamaghorāstraṃ mahāmanuḥ //
1.91.d:
घातयद्वितयं वर्मफडन्तः समुदीरितः ।
एकपञ्चाशदर्णो ऽयमघोरास्त्रं महामनुः ॥
1.91.m: twice ghātaya, concluding with the armour [huṃ] and phaṭ— / this great mantra of fifty-one syllables is the Aghorāstra.

1.91.s:
aghoro 'sya nuniḥ proktastrivṛcchandaṃ udāhṛtam /
aghorarudraḥ saṃdiṣṭo devatā mantranāyakaḥ //
1.91.d:
अघोरो ऽस्य नुनिः प्रोक्तस्त्रिवृच्छन्दं उदाहृतम् ।
अघोररुद्रः संदिष्टो देवता मन्त्रनायकः ॥
1.91.m: Its sage is said to be Aghora; the metre is declared to be Trivṛt; / Aghorarudra is designated as the deity, the lord of the mantra.

1.91.s:
hṛdayaṃ pañcabhiḥ proktaṃ śiraḥ ṣaḍbhirudāhṛtam /
śikhā daśabhirākhyātā navabhiḥ kavacaṃ matam //
1.91.d:
हृदयं पञ्चभिः प्रोक्तं शिरः षड्भिरुदाहृतम् ।
शिखा दशभिराख्याता नवभिः कवचं मतम् ॥
1.91.m: The heart is proclaimed by five [syllables]; the head is declared by six; / the topknot is spoken of by ten; the armour is considered to be of nine;

1.91.s:
vasuvarṇaiḥ smṛtaṃ netraṃ daśārṇairastramīritam /
mūrdhni netrāsyakaṇṭheṣu hṛnnābhyāmūruṣu kramāt //
1.91.d:
वसुवर्णैः स्मृतं नेत्रं दशार्णैरस्त्रमीरितम् ।
मूर्ध्नि नेत्रास्यकण्ठेषु हृन्नाभ्यामूरुषु क्रमात् ॥
1.91.m: the eye is remembered by eight syllables; the weapon is declared by ten syllables. / On the crown of the head, eyes, mouth, throat, heart, navel, and thighs in order,

1.91.s:
jānujaṅghāpadadvandve rudrabhinnākṣarairnyaset /
pañcaṣaṭkāṣṭavedāṅgadvivdyabdhirasalocanaiḥ //
1.91.d:
जानुजङ्घापदद्वन्द्वे रुद्रभिन्नाक्षरैर्न्यसेत् ।
पञ्चषट्काष्टवेदाङ्गद्विव्द्यब्धिरसलोचनैः ॥
1.91.m: on the pair of knees, shanks, and feet, one should perform ritual placement with the syllables divided among the Rudras / by five, six, eight, four, six, two, two, four, six, and two [syllables].

1.91.s:
śyāmaṃ trinetraṃ sapārḍhyaṃ raktavastrāṅgarāṅgakam /
nānāśastradharaṃ dhyāyenadaghorākhyaṃ sadāśivam //
1.91.d:
श्यामं त्रिनेत्रं सपार्ढ्यं रक्तवस्त्राङ्गराङ्गकम् ।
नानाशस्त्रधरं ध्यायेनदघोराख्यं सदाशिवम् ॥
1.91.m: One should meditate upon Sadāśiva named Aghora: dark, three-eyed, terrible, / his limbs clad in red garments and ointments, bearing various weapons.

1.91.s:
bhūtavetālakādīnāṃ kṣayo 'yaṃ nigrahe manuḥ /
tāro vānto dharāsaṃstho vāmanetrendubhūṣitaḥ //
1.91.d:
भूतवेतालकादीनां क्षयो ऽयं निग्रहे मनुः ।
तारो वान्तो धरासंस्थो वामनेत्रेन्दुभूषितः ॥
1.91.m: This is the mantra for subduing and destroying spirits, vetālas, and the like. / The tāra [oṃ], the end of the semi-vowels [ha], seated on the earth [l], adorned with the left eye [ī] and the moon [ṃ]—

1.91.s:
pāśī bakaḥ karṇanetravarmāstrāntaḥ ṣaḍakṣaraḥ /
manuḥ pāśupatāstrākhyo grahakṣudranivāraṇaḥ //
1.91.d:
पाशी बकः कर्णनेत्रवर्मास्त्रान्तः षडक्षरः ।
मनुः पाशुपतास्त्राख्यो ग्रहक्षुद्रनिवारणः ॥
1.91.m: Pāśin [p], baka [pha], ending with the ear, eye, armour, and weapon [śu-pa-ta-ye huṃ phaṭ]—a six-syllable / mantra known as Pāśupatāstra, warding off seizing spirits and petty sorceries.

1.91.s:
ṣaḍbhirvarṇaiḥ ṣaḍaṅgāni huṃphaḍantaiḥ sajātibhiḥ /
madhyāhnārkaprabhaṃ bhīmaṃ tryakṣaṃ pannagabhūṣaṇam //
1.91.d:
षड्भिर्वर्णैः षडङ्गानि हुंफडन्तैः सजातिभिः ।
मध्याह्नार्कप्रभं भीमं त्र्यक्षं पन्नगभूषणम् ॥
1.91.m: With the six syllables, the six limbs [are formed], ending with huṃ and phaṭ and having their proper invocations. / Resplendent like the midday sun, fierce, three-eyed, adorned with serpents,

1.91.s:
nānāśastraṃ caturvaktraṃ smaretpaśupatiṃ haram /
varṇalakṣaṃ japenmantraṃ juhuyāttaddaśāṃśataḥ //
1.91.d:
नानाशस्त्रं चतुर्वक्त्रं स्मरेत्पशुपतिं हरम् ।
वर्णलक्षं जपेन्मन्त्रं जुहुयात्तद्दशांशतः ॥
1.91.m: bearing various weapons, four-faced—one should meditate on Paśupati, Hara. / One should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times, and offer oblations of a tenth part thereof

1.91.s:
gavyena sarpiṣā mantro saṃskṛte havyavāhane /
śaive pīṭhe yajedaṅgamātṛlokeśvarāyudhaiḥ //
1.91.d:
गव्येन सर्पिषा मन्त्रो संस्कृते हव्यवाहने ।
शैवे पीठे यजेदङ्गमातृलोकेश्वरायुधैः ॥
1.91.m: with cow’s ghee, the mantra-practitioner, in the consecrated fire. / On a Śaiva seat, he should worship with the limbs, the Mothers, the guardians of the world, and weapons.

1.91.s:
anena mantritaṃ toyaṃ bhūtagrastamukhe kṣipet /
sadyaḥ sa muñcati krandānmahāmantraprabhāvataḥ //
1.91.d:
अनेन मन्त्रितं तोयं भूतग्रस्तमुखे क्षिपेत् ।
सद्यः स मुञ्चति क्रन्दान्महामन्त्रप्रभावतः ॥
1.91.m: Water consecrated with this [mantra] should be cast into the mouth of one seized by a spirit; / immediately he is released, crying out, by the power of the great mantra.

1.91.s:
anena mantritānbāṇānvisṛjedyudhi yo naraḥ /
jayetkṣaṇena nikhilāñchatrūnpārtha ivāparaḥ //
1.91.d:
अनेन मन्त्रितान्बाणान्विसृजेद्युधि यो नरः ।
जयेत्क्षणेन निखिलाञ्छत्रून्पार्थ इवापरः ॥
1.91.m: The man who discharges arrows consecrated with this [mantra] in battle / would conquer all enemies in an instant, like another Pārtha.

1.91.s: varṇāntimo binduyutaḥ kṣetrapālāya hṛnmanuḥ //
1.91.d: वर्णान्तिमो बिन्दुयुतः क्षेत्रपालाय हृन्मनुः ॥
1.91.m: The last of the letters [kṣa], accompanied by the bindu [ṃ], followed by kṣetrapālāya and the heart-mantra [namaḥ]:

1.91.s:
tārādyo vasuvarṇo 'yaṃ kṣetrapālasya kīrtitaḥ /
ṣaḍdīrghayuktabījena ṣaḍaṅgaṃ nyasya cintayet //
1.91.d:
ताराद्यो वसुवर्णो ऽयं क्षेत्रपालस्य कीर्तितः ।
षड्दीर्घयुक्तबीजेन षडङ्गं न्यस्य चिन्तयेत् ॥
1.91.m: this eight-syllable [mantra] beginning with the tāra [oṃ] is proclaimed for Kṣetrapāla. / Having performed the ritual placement of the six limbs with the seed-syllable joined with the six long vowels, one should visualize:

1.91.s:
nīlācalābhaṃ digvastraṃ sarpabhūṣaṃ trilocanam /
piṅgordhvakeśāndadhataṃ kapālaṃ ca gadāṃ smaret //
1.91.d:
नीलाचलाभं दिग्वस्त्रं सर्पभूषं त्रिलोचनम् ।
पिङ्गोर्ध्वकेशान्दधतं कपालं च गदां स्मरेत् ॥
1.91.m: one should meditate on him resembling a blue mountain, space-clad, serpent-adorned, three-eyed, / having reddish-brown upright hair, and holding a skull-bowl and a mace.

1.91.s:
lakṣamekaṃ japenmantraṃ juhuyāttaddaśāṃśataḥ /
caruṇā ghṛtasiktena tataḥ kṣetre samarcayet //
1.91.d:
लक्षमेकं जपेन्मन्त्रं जुहुयात्तद्दशांशतः ।
चरुणा घृतसिक्तेन ततः क्षेत्रे समर्चयेत् ॥
1.91.m: One should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times, and offer in fire a tenth part thereof / with sacrificial cooked rice moistened with ghee; then he should worship him in the sacred field.

1.91.s:
dharmādikalpite pīṭhe sāṃgāvaraṇamādarāt /
tasmai saparivārāya balimetena nirharet //
1.91.d:
धर्मादिकल्पिते पीठे सांगावरणमादरात् ।
तस्मै सपरिवाराय बलिमेतेन निर्हरेत् ॥
1.91.m: Upon a seat conceived with Dharma and the rest, along with his limbs and surrounding deities, with reverence, / one should offer a food offering to him and his retinue with this [mantra]:

1.91.s:
pūrvamehidvayaṃ paścādvidviṣaṃ puruṣaṃ dvayam /
bhañjayadvitayaṃ bhūyo nartayadvitayaṃ punaḥ //
1.91.d:
पूर्वमेहिद्वयं पश्चाद्विद्विषं पुरुषं द्वयम् ।
भञ्जयद्वितयं भूयो नर्तयद्वितयं पुनः ॥
1.91.m: ‘First twice ehi, then twice vidviṣaṃ puruṣaṃ; / twice bhañjaya, again twice nartaya;

1.91.s:
tato vighnapadadvandvaṃ mahābhairava tatparam /
kṣetrapālabaliṃ gṛhṇadvayaṃ pāvakasundarī //
1.91.d:
ततो विघ्नपदद्वन्द्वं महाभैरव तत्परम् ।
क्षेत्रपालबलिं गृह्णद्वयं पावकसुन्दरी ॥
1.91.m: then the pair of words vighna, then mahābhairava; / kṣetrapālabaliṃ gṛhṇa twice, and the beloved of fire [svāhā].’

1.91.s:
balimantro 'yamākhyātaḥ sarvakāmaphalapradaḥ /
sopadeśaṃ bṛhatpiṇḍe kṛtvā rātriṣu sādhakaḥ //
1.91.d:
बलिमन्त्रो ऽयमाख्यातः सर्वकामफलप्रदः ।
सोपदेशं बृहत्पिण्डे कृत्वा रात्रिषु साधकः ॥
1.91.m: This is declared to be the bali mantra, yielding the fruit of all desires. / Having made a large lump according to instruction at night, the practitioner,

1.91.s:
smṛtvā yathoktaṃ kṣetreśaṃ tasya haste baliṃ haret /
balinānena santuṣṭaḥ kṣetrapālaḥ prayacchati //
1.91.d:
स्मृत्वा यथोक्तं क्षेत्रेशं तस्य हस्ते बलिं हरेत् ।
बलिनानेन सन्तुष्टः क्षेत्रपालः प्रयच्छति ॥
1.91.m: having recollected the Lord of the Field as described, should place the food offering into his hand. / Satisfied by this food offering, Kṣetrapāla bestows

1.91.s:
kāntiṃ medhāṃ balāyogyaṃ tejaḥ puṣṭiṃ yaśaḥ śriyam /
uddharedbaṭukaṃ ṅeṃtamāpaduddhāraṇaṃ tathā //
1.91.d:
कान्तिं मेधां बलायोग्यं तेजः पुष्टिं यशः श्रियम् ।
उद्धरेद्बटुकं ङेंतमापदुद्धारणं तथा ॥
1.91.m: radiance, intellect, strength, health, splendour, nourishment, fame, and fortune. / One should pronounce baṭuka in the dative case [baṭukāya], and āpaduddhāraṇa;

1.91.s:
kurudvayaṃ tataḥ paścādvaṭukaṃ ṅeṃtamuccaret /
śaktiruddho dhruvādiśca dvāviṃśatyakṣaro manuḥ //
1.91.d:
कुरुद्वयं ततः पश्चाद्वटुकं ङेंतमुच्चरेत् ।
शक्तिरुद्धो ध्रुवादिश्च द्वाविंशत्यक्षरो मनुः ॥
1.91.m: then twice kuru, and after that one should utter vaṭuka in the dative case; / stopped by Śakti [hrīṃ], beginning with dhruva [oṃ]—this is a mantra of twenty-two syllables.

1.91.s:
dvicatuḥsaptavedābdhicandrārṇairaṅgakaṃ manoḥ /
bālaṃ sphaṭikasaṃkāśaṃ tallolalasitānanam //
1.91.d:
द्विचतुःसप्तवेदाब्धिचन्द्रार्णैरङ्गकं मनोः ।
बालं स्फटिकसंकाशं तल्लोललसिताननम् ॥
1.91.m: The limbs of the mantra are [formed] by two, four, seven, four, four, and one syllables. / A boy resembling crystal, his charming face trembling and brilliant,

1.91.s:
divyākalpaiḥ pradīptāṅgaṃ tryakṣaṃ daṇḍatriśūlinam /
suprasannaṃ smareddhaktyā bhaktānāmabhayaṅkaram //
1.91.d:
दिव्याकल्पैः प्रदीप्ताङ्गं त्र्यक्षं दण्डत्रिशूलिनम् ।
सुप्रसन्नं स्मरेद्धक्त्या भक्तानामभयङ्करम् ॥
1.91.m: his limbs radiant with divine ornaments, three-eyed, holding a staff and a trident, / completely serene—one should meditate on him with devotion, the grantor of fearlessness to devotees.

1.91.s:
varṇalakṣaṃ japenmantraṃ haviṣyāśī jitendriyaḥ /
taddaśāṃśaṃ prajuhuyānttilairmadhurasaṃyutaiḥ //
1.91.d:
वर्णलक्षं जपेन्मन्त्रं हविष्याशी जितेन्द्रियः ।
तद्दशांशं प्रजुहुयान्त्तिलैर्मधुरसंयुतैः ॥
1.91.m: Eating sacrificial food, with senses subdued, one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times; / one should offer into fire a tenth of that with sesame seeds mixed with sweets,

1.91.s:
dharmādikalpite pīṭhe paṅkaje cātiśobhane /
ṣaṭkoṇāntastrikoṇasthavyomapaṅkajasaṃyute //
1.91.d:
धर्मादिकल्पिते पीठे पङ्कजे चातिशोभने ।
षट्कोणान्तस्त्रिकोणस्थव्योमपङ्कजसंयुते ॥
1.91.m: upon a seat conceived with Dharma and the rest, upon an exceedingly beautiful lotus, / having an empty lotus situated in a triangle within a hexagon.

1.91.s:
baṭukaṃ pūjayeddevaṃ sāṃgāvaraṇakaṃ kramāt /
śatrupakṣasya rudhiraṃ piśinta ca dinedine /
bhakṣayasva gaṇaiḥ sārddhaṃ sārameyasamanvitaḥ //
1.91.d:
बटुकं पूजयेद्देवं सांगावरणकं क्रमात् ।
शत्रुपक्षस्य रुधिरं पिशिन्त च दिनेदिने ।
भक्षयस्व गणैः सार्द्धं सारमेयसमन्वितः ॥
1.91.m: He should worship the deity Baṭuka along with his limbs and surrounding deities in proper order. / ‘Day after day, drink the blood and flesh of the host of enemies; / eat it together with your attendants, accompanied by dogs!’

1.91.s:
balimantro 'yamākhyātaḥ śatrunāmnā vidarbhitaḥ /
anena balinā hṛṣṭo baṭukaḥ parasainyakam //
1.91.d:
बलिमन्त्रो ऽयमाख्यातः शत्रुनाम्ना विदर्भितः ।
अनेन बलिना हृष्टो बटुकः परसैन्यकम् ॥
1.91.m: This bali mantra is proclaimed, interwoven with the name of the enemy. / Delighted by this food offering, Baṭuka, with an enraged mind,

1.91.s:
chitvā gaṇebhyo vibhajedāmiṣaṃ kruddhamānasaḥ /
aṅkaśo vahniśikharo lāntadānta itīritaḥ //
1.91.d:
छित्वा गणेभ्यो विभजेदामिषं क्रुद्धमानसः ।
अङ्कशो वह्निशिखरो लान्तदान्त इतीरितः ॥
1.91.m: cuts down the enemy's army and distributes their flesh to his attendants. / The hook [kṣ], the crest of fire [r], ending in la and da [auṃ] is pronounced;

1.91.s:
phaḍantaścaṇḍamantro 'yaṃ trivarṇātmā samīritaḥ /
asya trito muniḥ proktaśchando 'nuṣṭubudāhṛtam //
1.91.d:
फडन्तश्चण्डमन्त्रो ऽयं त्रिवर्णात्मा समीरितः ।
अस्य त्रितो मुनिः प्रोक्तश्छन्दो ऽनुष्टुबुदाहृतम् ॥
1.91.m: ending with phaṭ, this Caṇḍa mantra is proclaimed to consist of three syllables. / His sage is stated to be Trita; the metre is declared to be Anuṣṭubh;

1.91.s:
caṇḍeśo devatā proktā vakṣyateṃ'gaprakalpanam /
hṛdayaṃ dīptaphaṭ proktaṃ jvalaphaṭ śira īritam //
1.91.d:
चण्डेशो देवता प्रोक्ता वक्ष्यतेंऽगप्रकल्पनम् ।
हृदयं दीप्तफट् प्रोक्तं ज्वलफट् शिर ईरितम् ॥
1.91.m: the deity is declared to be Caṇḍeśa; the arrangement of the limbs will be stated: / ‘dīptaphaṭ’ is stated to be the heart; ‘jvalaphaṭ’ is declared to be the head;

1.91.s:
śikhājvālini phaṭ proktā vahaphaṭ kavacaṃ matam /
halaphaṭ netramākhyātaṃ sarvajvāniniphaṭ param //
1.91.d:
शिखाज्वालिनि फट् प्रोक्ता वहफट् कवचं मतम् ।
हलफट् नेत्रमाख्यातं सर्वज्वानिनिफट् परम् ॥
1.91.m: ‘jvālini phaṭ’ is stated to be the topknot; ‘vahaphaṭ’ is considered the armour; / ‘halaphaṭ’ is declared to be the eye; and ‘sarvajvālini phaṭ’ the ultimate [weapon].

1.91.s:
vinyasyaivaṃ ṣaḍaṅgāni tato devaṃ vicintayet /
caṇḍeśvaraṃ raktatanuntryakṣaṃ raktāṃbarāvṛtam //
1.91.d:
विन्यस्यैवं षडङ्गानि ततो देवं विचिन्तयेत् ।
चण्डेश्वरं रक्ततनुन्त्र्यक्षं रक्तांबरावृतम् ॥
1.91.m: Having thus ritually placed the six limbs, one should then meditate upon the deity: / Caṇḍeśvara, red-bodied, three-eyed, clad in red garments,

1.91.s:
dadhataṃ ca triśūlākṣamālāṭaṃ kakamaṇḍalūn /
varṇalakṣaṃ japenmantraṃ homaṃ kuryāddaśāṃśataḥ //
1.91.d:
दधतं च त्रिशूलाक्षमालाटं ककमण्डलून् ।
वर्णलक्षं जपेन्मन्त्रं होमं कुर्याद्दशांशतः ॥
1.91.m: holding a trident, a rosary, an axe, and a water-pot. / One should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times, and perform fire oblations of a tenth part thereof.

1.91.s:
madhuratrayasaṃyuktairviśuddhaistilataṇḍulaiḥ /
pañcākṣarodite pīṭhe mūrtiṃ mūlena kalpayet //
1.91.d:
मधुरत्रयसंयुक्तैर्विशुद्धैस्तिलतण्डुलैः ।
पञ्चाक्षरोदिते पीठे मूर्तिं मूलेन कल्पयेत् ॥
1.91.m: with pure sesamum and rice grains mixed with the three sweets. / On the ritual seat declared for the five-syllabled [formula], one should fashion the form with the root [mantra].

1.91.s:
kūrmeśo bindusaṃyuktastataścaṇḍeśvarāya ca /
hṛdayaṃ manurākhyātaścaṇḍeśasya prapūjane //
1.91.d:
कूर्मेशो बिन्दुसंयुक्तस्ततश्चण्डेश्वराय च ।
हृदयं मनुराख्यातश्चण्डेशस्य प्रपूजने ॥
1.91.m: Kūrmeśa accompanied by the bindu, then ‘to Caṇḍeśvara’, / [and] the heart [mantra] (namaḥ) are declared as the mantra in the worship of Caṇḍeśa.

1.91.s:
aṅgairmātṛbhirāśeśairvajrādyairāvṛtirbhavet /
śaivamantreṣu niṣṇātaścaṇḍeśvaramanuṃ japet //
1.91.d:
अङ्गैर्मातृभिराशेशैर्वज्राद्यैरावृतिर्भवेत् ।
शैवमन्त्रेषु निष्णातश्चण्डेश्वरमनुं जपेत् ॥
1.91.m: There should be an enclosure of the limbs, the Mothers, the regents of the quarters, and [the weapons] beginning with the thunderbolt. / Versed in Śaiva mantras, he should recite the mantra of Caṇḍeśvara.

1.91.s:
sarvānkāmānavāpnoti paratreha ca nandati /
śṛṇu nārada vakṣyāmi divyaṃ māheśvaraṃ stavam //
1.91.d:
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति परत्रेह च नन्दति ।
शृणु नारद वक्ष्यामि दिव्यं माहेश्वरं स्तवम् ॥
1.91.m: He obtains all desires and rejoices in the hereafter and here. / Listen, O Nārada, I will proclaim the divine eulogy of Maheśvara,

1.91.s: yasya pāṭhena pūjāyāṃ siddhyanti manavo 'khilāḥ //
1.91.d: यस्य पाठेन पूजायां सिद्ध्यन्ति मनवो ऽखिलाः ॥
1.91.m: through the reading of which in worship all mantras become accomplished.

1.91.s:
dharāmbvagnimaruvdyomamakheśendvarkamūrtaye /
sarvabhūtāntarasthāya śaṅkarāya namonamaḥ //
1.91.d:
धराम्ब्वग्निमरुव्द्योममखेशेन्द्वर्कमूर्तये ।
सर्वभूतान्तरस्थाय शङ्कराय नमोनमः ॥
1.91.m: Homage, homage to Śaṅkara, whose forms are earth, water, fire, wind, ether, the sacrificer, the moon, and the sun, / who abides within all beings!

1.91.s:
śrutyaṃ takṛtavāsāya śrutaye śrutijanmane /
atīndriyāya mahase śāśvatāya namonamaḥ //
1.91.d:
श्रुत्यं तकृतवासाय श्रुतये श्रुतिजन्मने ।
अतीन्द्रियाय महसे शाश्वताय नमोनमः ॥
1.91.m: Homage, homage to the Eternal One, who resides at the end of the Vedic revelation, who is Vedic revelation itself, the origin of revelation, / the beyond-sensory radiance!

1.91.s:
sthūlasūkṣmavibhāgābhyāmanirdeśyāya śaṃbhave /
bhavāya bhavasaṃbhūtaduḥkhahantre namonamaḥ //
1.91.d:
स्थूलसूक्ष्मविभागाभ्यामनिर्देश्याय शंभवे ।
भवाय भवसंभूतदुःखहन्त्रे नमोनमः ॥
1.91.m: Homage, homage to Śambhu, who cannot be designated through gross and subtle distinctions, / to Bhava, the destroyer of suffering born of worldly existence!

1.91.s:
tarkamārgātidūrāya tapasāṃ phaladāyine /
caturvargavadānyāya sarvajñāya namonamaḥ //
1.91.d:
तर्कमार्गातिदूराय तपसां फलदायिने ।
चतुर्वर्गवदान्याय सर्वज्ञाय नमोनमः ॥
1.91.m: Homage, homage to the Omniscient One, who is exceedingly far from the path of reasoning, the giver of the fruits of austerities, / the bountiful granter of the four aims of life!

1.91.s:
ādimadhyāntaśūnyāya nirastāśeṣabhītaye /
yogidhyeyāya mahate nirguṇāya namonamaḥ //
1.91.d:
आदिमध्यान्तशून्याय निरस्ताशेषभीतये ।
योगिध्येयाय महते निर्गुणाय नमोनमः ॥
1.91.m: Homage, homage to the Great One, free from beginning, middle, and end, who has dispelled all fear, / the object of meditation for yogins, devoid of qualities!

1.91.s:
viśvātmane viviktāya vilasaccandramaulaye /
kandarppadarppanāśāya kālahṝntre namonamaḥ //
1.91.d:
विश्वात्मने विविक्ताय विलसच्चन्द्रमौलये ।
कन्दर्प्पदर्प्पनाशाय कालहॄन्त्रे नमोनमः ॥
1.91.m: Homage, homage to the Soul of the universe, the Solitary One, who has the gleaming moon on his crest, / the destroyer of the pride of Kandarpa, the slayer of Kāla!

1.91.s:
viṣāśanāya viharadvṛṣaskandhamupeyuṣe /
sariddāmasamābaddhakapadārya namonamaḥ //
1.91.d:
विषाशनाय विहरद्वृषस्कन्धमुपेयुषे ।
सरिद्दामसमाबद्धकपदार्य नमोनमः ॥
1.91.m: Homage, homage to the poison-eater, who mounted the shoulder of the sporting bull, / whose matted hair is bound with the garland of the river [Gaṅgā]!

1.91.s:
śuddhāya śuddhabhāvā śuddhānāmantarātmane /
purāntakāya pūrṇāya puṇyanāmno namonamaḥ //
1.91.d:
शुद्धाय शुद्धभावा शुद्धानामन्तरात्मने ।
पुरान्तकाय पूर्णाय पुण्यनाम्नो नमोनमः ॥
1.91.m: Homage, homage to the Pure One, of pure nature, the inner Self of the pure, / the destroyer of the [demon] cities, the Full One, whose name is holy!

1.91.s:
bhaktāya nijabhaktānāṃ bhuktimuktipradāyine /
vivāsase nivāsāya viśveṣāṃ pataye namaḥ //
1.91.d:
भक्ताय निजभक्तानां भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायिने ।
विवाससे निवासाय विश्वेषां पतये नमः ॥
1.91.m: Homage to the Lord of all, who is affectionate to his own devotees, the giver of worldly enjoyment and liberation, / the unclothed one, the dwelling-place!

1.91.s:
trimūrtimūlabhūtāya trinetrāya triśūline /
tridhāmne dhāmarūpāya janmadāya namonamaḥ //
1.91.d:
त्रिमूर्तिमूलभूताय त्रिनेत्राय त्रिशूलिने ।
त्रिधाम्ने धामरूपाय जन्मदाय नमोनमः ॥
1.91.m: Homage, homage to the source of the three forms, the three-eyed one, the bearer of the trident, / the threefold realm, the embodiment of radiance, the giver of birth!

1.91.s:
devāsuraśiroratnakirīṭāruṇitāṅghraye /
kāntāya nijakāntāyai dattārddhāya namonamaḥ //
1.91.d:
देवासुरशिरोरत्नकिरीटारुणिताङ्घ्रये ।
कान्ताय निजकान्तायै दत्तार्द्धाय नमोनमः ॥
1.91.m: Homage, homage to the Beloved, whose feet are reddened by the crested diadems of gods and asuras, / who gave half his body to his own beloved!

1.91.s:
etatstotraṃ maheśasya proktaṃ sarvāghanāśanam /
śivasānnidhyadaṃ vipra sarpatantraprakāśakam //
1.91.d:
एतत्स्तोत्रं महेशस्य प्रोक्तं सर्वाघनाशनम् ।
शिवसान्निध्यदं विप्र सर्पतन्त्रप्रकाशकम् ॥
1.91.m: This eulogy of Maheśa, proclaimed [here], destroys all sins; / it grants the presence of Śiva, O brāhmaṇa, and illuminates all tantras.

1.91.s:
etatte sumahattantreṃ sarvadevaprakāśakam /
lokābhilāṣasaṃpūrtikriyāsādhanasaṃgatam //
1.91.d:
एतत्ते सुमहत्तन्त्रें सर्वदेवप्रकाशकम् ।
लोकाभिलाषसंपूर्तिक्रियासाधनसंगतम् ॥
1.91.m: This great tantra, revealing all the gods, / joined with the ritual procedures that fulfill worldly desires, has been declared to you.

1.91.s:
ye tu sāmānyataḥ proktāstantre 'sminmanavo dvija /
te tu lokopakārāya jñātavyāḥ siddhidāyakāḥ //
1.91.d:
ये तु सामान्यतः प्रोक्तास्तन्त्रे ऽस्मिन्मनवो द्विज ।
ते तु लोकोपकाराय ज्ञातव्याः सिद्धिदायकाः ॥
1.91.m: And the mantras that have been proclaimed in general terms in this tantra, O twice-born, / are to be understood as conferring accomplishment for the welfare of the world.

1.91.s:
viśeṣato vaiṣṇavā ye mantrāḥ sarvottamottamāḥ /
ta eva sādhanīyāḥ syuścaturvargaphalāptaye //
1.91.d:
विशेषतो वैष्णवा ये मन्त्राः सर्वोत्तमोत्तमाः ।
त एव साधनीयाः स्युश्चतुर्वर्गफलाप्तये ॥
1.91.m: In particular, the Vaiṣṇava mantras, which are the highest of the high, / are precisely those that should be mastered to attain the fruit of the four aims of life.

1.91.s:
rāmamantrāḥ kṛṣṇamantrāḥ sāṃgā rāseśimantrakāḥ /
śāktāḥ saurāśca gāṇeśāḥ śaivāḥ proktāḥ śubhāvahāḥ //
1.91.d:
राममन्त्राः कृष्णमन्त्राः सांगा रासेशिमन्त्रकाः ।
शाक्ताः सौराश्च गाणेशाः शैवाः प्रोक्ताः शुभावहाः ॥
1.91.m: The Rāma mantras, Kṛṣṇa mantras, together with their limbs, the mantras of Rādhā, / and the Śākta, Saura, Gāṇeśa, and Śaiva [mantras] have been proclaimed as conferring auspiciousness.

1.91.s:
teṣu svātmaprakāśāya bhajenmuktiphalapradān /
etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ yattvayābhyarthitaṃ mune /
devatārādhanaṃ bhaktyā kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne tṛtīyapāde maheśamantrakathanaṃ nāmaikanavatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
iti tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ
1.91.d:
तेषु स्वात्मप्रकाशाय भजेन्मुक्तिफलप्रदान् ।
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं यत्त्वयाभ्यर्थितं मुने ।
देवताराधनं भक्त्या किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने तृतीयपादे महेशमन्त्रकथनं नामैकनवतितमो ऽध्यायः
इति तृतीयः पादः
1.91.m:
Among them, for the manifestation of one’s own self, one should worship those that bestow the fruit of liberation. / All this has been related to you as requested by you, O sage: / the worship of deities with devotion. What further do you wish to hear?

Thus ends the ninety-first chapter, named ‘The Exposition of the Mantras of Maheśa’, in the third quarter of the great narrative in the first section of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

1.92.s:
sūta uvāca
etacchrutvā nāradastu kumārasya vaco mudā /
punarapyāha suprīto jijñāsuḥ śreya uttamam //
1.92.d:
सूत उवाच
एतच्छ्रुत्वा नारदस्तु कुमारस्य वचो मुदा ।
पुनरप्याह सुप्रीतो जिज्ञासुः श्रेय उत्तमम् ॥
1.92.m: Sūta said: / Hearing this speech of Kumāra with joy, Nārada, / exceedingly pleased, spoke again, desirous of knowing the highest good:

1.92.s:
nārada uvāca
sādhu sādhu mahābhāga sarvalokopakārakam /
mahātantraṃ tvayā proktaṃ sarvatantrottamottamam //
1.92.d:
नारद उवाच
साधु साधु महाभाग सर्वलोकोपकारकम् ।
महातन्त्रं त्वया प्रोक्तं सर्वतन्त्रोत्तमोत्तमम् ॥
1.92.m: Nārada said: / Excellent, excellent, O blessed one! Beneficent to all the world, / the great tantra, the highest of all tantras, has been spoken by you.

1.92.s:
adhunā śrotumicchāmi purāṇākhyānamuttamam /
yasminyasminpurāṇe tu yadyadākhyānakaṃ mune /
tatsarvaṃ me samācakṣva sarvajñastvaṃ yato mataḥ //
1.92.d:
अधुना श्रोतुमिच्छामि पुराणाख्यानमुत्तमम् ।
यस्मिन्यस्मिन्पुराणे तु यद्यदाख्यानकं मुने ।
तत्सर्वं मे समाचक्ष्व सर्वज्ञस्त्वं यतो मतः ॥
1.92.m: Now I desire to hear the supreme narrative of the Purāṇas. / Whatever narrative is in whichever Purāṇa, O sage, / declare all of that to me, since you are considered omniscient.

1.92.s:
sūta uvāca
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ viprā nāradasya śubhāvaham /
purāṇākhyānasaṃpraśnaṃ kumāraḥ pratyuvāca ha //
1.92.d:
सूत उवाच
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं विप्रा नारदस्य शुभावहम् ।
पुराणाख्यानसंप्रश्नं कुमारः प्रत्युवाच ह ॥
1.92.m: Sūta said: / Hearing that auspicious speech of Nārada, / that question regarding the narratives of the Purāṇas, Kumāra replied, O brāhmaṇas:

1.92.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca
pārāṇākhyānakaṃ vipra nānākalpasamudbhavam /
nānākathāsamāyuktamadbhutaṃ bahuvistaram //
1.92.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
पाराणाख्यानकं विप्र नानाकल्पसमुद्भवम् ।
नानाकथासमायुक्तमद्भुतं बहुविस्तरम् ॥
1.92.m: Sanatkumāra said: / The narrative of the Purāṇas, O brāhmaṇa, originating from various kalpas, / endowed with diverse stories, is wonderful and of great extent.

1.92.s:
ṛṣiḥ sanātanaścāyaṃ yathā veda tathāparaḥ /
na veda tasmātpṛccha tvaṃ bahukalpavidāṃ varam //
1.92.d:
ऋषिः सनातनश्चायं यथा वेद तथापरः ।
न वेद तस्मात्पृच्छ त्वं बहुकल्पविदां वरम् ॥
1.92.m: This sage Sanātana knows it as no other / knows. Therefore, ask him, the foremost of those who know many kalpas.

1.92.s:
śrutvetthaṃ nārado vākyaṃ kumārasya mahātmanaḥ /
praṇamya vinayopetaḥ sanātanamathābravīt //
1.92.d:
श्रुत्वेत्थं नारदो वाक्यं कुमारस्य महात्मनः ।
प्रणम्य विनयोपेतः सनातनमथाब्रवीत् ॥
1.92.m: Having heard this word of the high-souled Kumāra, Nārada / bowed down and, filled with humility, then addressed Sanātana:

1.92.s:
nārada uvāca
brahmanpurāṇavicchreṣṭha jñānavijñānatatpara /
purāṇānāṃ vibhāgaṃ me sākalye nānukīrtaya //
1.92.d:
नारद उवाच
ब्रह्मन्पुराणविच्छ्रेष्ठ ज्ञानविज्ञानतत्पर ।
पुराणानां विभागं मे साकल्ये नानुकीर्तय ॥
1.92.m: Nārada said: / O holy one, foremost among knowers of the Purāṇas, devoted to knowledge and experiential wisdom, / recount to me the division of the Purāṇas in its entirety,

1.92.s: yasmiñ śrute śrutaṃ sarvaṃ jñātaṃ kṛte kṛtam //
1.92.d: यस्मिञ् श्रुते श्रुतं सर्वं ज्ञातं कृते कृतम् ॥
1.92.m: hearing which, everything is heard, known, and when done, all is done.

1.92.s:
varṇāśramācāradharmaṃ sākṣātkāramupaiṣyati /
kiyanti ca purāṇāni kiyatsaṃkhyāni mānataḥ //
1.92.d:
वर्णाश्रमाचारधर्मं साक्षात्कारमुपैष्यति ।
कियन्ति च पुराणानि कियत्संख्यानि मानतः ॥
1.92.m: The duties and conduct of the castes and stages of life will attain direct realization. / And how many are the Purāṇas, of what count by measure,

1.92.s:
kiṅkimākhyānayuktāni tadvadasva mama prabho /
cāturvarṇyāśrayā nānāvratādīnāṃ kathāstathā //
1.92.d:
किङ्किमाख्यानयुक्तानि तद्वदस्व मम प्रभो ।
चातुर्वर्ण्याश्रया नानाव्रतादीनां कथास्तथा ॥
1.92.m: joined with what narratives? Tell me that, O lord! / Likewise the stories of diverse observances and so forth based on the four castes;

1.92.s:
sṛṣṭikrameṇa vaṃśānāṃ kathāḥ samyakprakāśaya /
tvatto 'dhiko na cānyo 'sti purāṇākhyānavitprabho //
1.92.d:
सृष्टिक्रमेण वंशानां कथाः सम्यक्प्रकाशय ।
त्वत्तो ऽधिको न चान्यो ऽस्ति पुराणाख्यानवित्प्रभो ॥
1.92.m: illuminate fully the histories of the lineages in order of creation. / There is none other greater than you who knows the narratives of the Purāṇas, O lord.

1.92.s:
tasmādākhyāhi mahyaṃ tvaṃ sarvasandehabhañjanam /
sūta uvāca
tataḥ sanātano viprāḥ śrutvā nāradabhāṣitam //
1.92.d:
तस्मादाख्याहि मह्यं त्वं सर्वसन्देहभञ्जनम् ।
सूत उवाच
ततः सनातनो विप्राः श्रुत्वा नारदभाषितम् ॥
1.92.m: Therefore, narrate to me that which dispels all doubt. / Sūta said: / Then Sanātana, O brāhmaṇas, having heard what Nārada spoke,

1.92.s:
nārāyaṇaṃ kṣaṇaṃ dhyātvā provācātha vidāṃ varaḥ /
sanātana uvāca
sādhu sādhu muniśreṣṭha sarvalokopakārikā //
1.92.d:
नारायणं क्षणं ध्यात्वा प्रोवाचाथ विदां वरः ।
सनातन उवाच
साधु साधु मुनिश्रेष्ठ सर्वलोकोपकारिका ॥
1.92.m: and having meditated for a moment on Nārāyaṇa, the foremost of knowers then spoke: / Sanātana said: / Excellent, excellent, O foremost of sages, beneficent to all the worlds,

1.92.s:
purāṇākhyānavijñāne yajjātā neṣṭhikī matiḥ /
tubhyaṃ samabhidhāsyāmi yatproktaṃ brahmaṇā purā //
1.92.d:
पुराणाख्यानविज्ञाने यज्जाता नेष्ठिकी मतिः ।
तुभ्यं समभिधास्यामि यत्प्रोक्तं ब्रह्मणा पुरा ॥
1.92.m: is this resolute mind that has arisen in you regarding the understanding of the narratives of the Purāṇas. / I shall declare to you what was spoken formerly by Brahmā

1.92.s:
marīcyādiṛṣibhyastu putrasnehāvṛtātmanā /
ekadā brahmaṇaḥ putro marīcirnāma viśrutaḥ //
1.92.d:
मरीच्यादिऋषिभ्यस्तु पुत्रस्नेहावृतात्मना ।
एकदा ब्रह्मणः पुत्रो मरीचिर्नाम विश्रुतः ॥
1.92.m: to the sages beginning with Marīci, with his mind overwhelmed by love for his sons. / Once, the son of Brahmā, famed by the name Marīci,

1.92.s:
svādhyāyaśrutasaṃpanno vedavedāgapāragaḥ /
upasṛtya svapitaraṃ brahmaṇaṃ lokabhāvanam //
1.92.d:
स्वाध्यायश्रुतसंपन्नो वेदवेदागपारगः ।
उपसृत्य स्वपितरं ब्रह्मणं लोकभावनम् ॥
1.92.m: endowed with Vedic study and sacred learning, gone to the end of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, / approached his father Brahmā, the creator of the worlds.

1.92.s:
praṇamya bhaktyā papraccha idameva muniśvara /
purāṇākhyānamamalaṃ yattvaṃ pṛcchasi mānada //
1.92.d:
प्रणम्य भक्त्या पप्रच्छ इदमेव मुनिश्वर ।
पुराणाख्यानममलं यत्त्वं पृच्छसि मानद ॥
1.92.m: Bowing with devotion, he asked this very thing, O lord of sages, / this immaculate narrative of the Purāṇas that you, O honor-giver, ask.

1.92.s:
marīciruvāca
bhagavandevadeveśa lokānāṃ prabhavāpyaya /
sarvajña sarvakalyāṇa sarvādhyakṣa namo 'stu te //
1.92.d:
मरीचिरुवाच
भगवन्देवदेवेश लोकानां प्रभवाप्यय ।
सर्वज्ञ सर्वकल्याण सर्वाध्यक्ष नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
1.92.m: Marīci said: / O Lord, O Ruler of the gods of gods, O origin and dissolution of the worlds, / O Omniscient One, O All-auspicious, O Presider over all, homage be to you!

1.92.s:
purāṇabījamākhyahi mahyaṃ śuśrūṣave pitaḥ /
lakṣaṇaṃ ca pramāṇaṃ ca pramāṇaṃ caṃ vaktāraṃ pṛcchakaṃ tathā //
1.92.d:
पुराणबीजमाख्यहि मह्यं शुश्रूषवे पितः ।
लक्षणं च प्रमाणं च प्रमाणं चं वक्तारं पृच्छकं तथा ॥
1.92.m: Declare to me, who wish to hear, O father, the seed of the Purāṇas, / the defining characteristics, the extent, the speaker, and likewise the inquirer.

1.92.s:
brahmovāca
śṛṇu vatsa pravakṣyāmi purāṇānāṃ samuccayam /
yasmiñjñāte bhavejjñātaṃ vāṅmayaṃ sacarācaram //
1.92.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
शृणु वत्स प्रवक्ष्यामि पुराणानां समुच्चयम् ।
यस्मिञ्ज्ञाते भवेज्ज्ञातं वाङ्मयं सचराचरम् ॥
