1.92.m: Brahmā said: / Listen, dear child, I shall declare the collection of the Purāṇas, / knowing which, the entire realm of speech, moving and unmoving, becomes known.

1.92.s:
purāṇamekamevāsītsarvakalpeṣu mānada /
caturvargasya bījaṃ ca śatakoṭipravistaram //
1.92.d:
पुराणमेकमेवासीत्सर्वकल्पेषु मानद ।
चतुर्वर्गस्य बीजं च शतकोटिप्रविस्तरम् ॥
1.92.m: There was only one Purāṇa in all kalpas, O honor-giver, / the seed of the four aims of life, extending to one billion [verses].

1.92.s:
pravṛttiḥ sarvaśāstrāṇāṃ purāṇādabhavattataḥ /
kālenāgrahaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā purāmasya mahāmatiḥ //
1.92.d:
प्रवृत्तिः सर्वशास्त्राणां पुराणादभवत्ततः ।
कालेनाग्रहणं दृष्ट्वा पुरामस्य महामतिः ॥
1.92.m: From that Purāṇa proceeded all the treatises. / Then, seeing the lack of comprehension of the Purāṇa over time, the great-minded

1.92.s:
harirvyāsasvarūpeṇa jāyate ca yuge yuge /
caturlakṣapramāṇena dvāpare dvāpare sadā //
1.92.d:
हरिर्व्यासस्वरूपेण जायते च युगे युगे ।
चतुर्लक्षप्रमाणेन द्वापरे द्वापरे सदा ॥
1.92.m: Hari, in the form of Vyāsa, is born age after age, / always in each Dvāpara age, [condensing it] to a measure of four hundred thousand [verses].

1.92.s:
tadaṣṭādaśadhā kṛtvā bhūrloke nirddiśatyapi /
adyāpi devaloke tu śatakoṭipravistaram //
1.92.d:
तदष्टादशधा कृत्वा भूर्लोके निर्द्दिशत्यपि ।
अद्यापि देवलोके तु शतकोटिप्रविस्तरम् ॥
1.92.m:
Dividing it into eighteen parts, he teaches it on the earth;
yet even today in the world of the gods it extends to a billion [verses].

1.92.s:
astyeva tasya sārastu caturlakṣeṇa varṇyate /
brāhmaṃ pādmaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ ca vāyavīyaṃ tathaiva ca //
1.92.d:
अस्त्येव तस्य सारस्तु चतुर्लक्षेण वर्ण्यते ।
ब्राह्मं पाद्मं वैष्णवं च वायवीयं तथैव च ॥
1.92.m:
Its essence is indeed related in four hundred thousand [verses]:
the Brāhma, Pādma, Vaiṣṇava, and likewise Vāyavīya,

1.92.s:
bhāgavataṃ nāradīyaṃ mārkaṇḍeyaṃ ca kīrtitam /
āgneyaṃ ca bhaviṣyaṃ ca brahmavaivarttaliṅgake //
1.92.d:
भागवतं नारदीयं मार्कण्डेयं च कीर्तितम् ।
आग्नेयं च भविष्यं च ब्रह्मवैवर्त्तलिङ्गके ॥
1.92.m:
the Bhāgavata, Nāradīya, and the Mārkaṇḍeya are proclaimed,
the Āgneya, Bhaviṣya, Brahmavaivarta, and Liṅga,

1.92.s:
vārāhaṃ ca tathā skāndaṃ vāmanaṃ kūrmasaṃjñakam /
mātsyaṃ ca gāruḍaṃ tadvadbrahmāṇḍākhyamiti triṣaṭ //
1.92.d:
वाराहं च तथा स्कान्दं वामनं कूर्मसंज्ञकम् ।
मात्स्यं च गारुडं तद्वद्ब्रह्माण्डाख्यमिति त्रिषट् ॥
1.92.m:
the Vārāha, Skānda, Vāmana, the one called Kūrma,
the Mātsya, Gāruḍa, and the one named Brahmāṇḍa—thus eighteen.

1.92.s:
ekaṃ kathānakaṃ sūtraṃ vaktuḥ śrotuḥ samāhvayam /
pravakṣyāmi samāsena niśāmaya samāhitaḥ //
1.92.d:
एकं कथानकं सूत्रं वक्तुः श्रोतुः समाह्वयम् ।
प्रवक्ष्यामि समासेन निशामय समाहितः ॥
1.92.m:
I shall relate in brief the single narrative thread,
with the designation of speaker and listener; listen with concentrated mind.

1.92.s:
brahmaṃ purāṇaṃ tatrādau sarvalokahitāya vai /
vyāsena vedaviduṣā samākhyātaṃ mahātmanā //
1.92.d:
ब्रह्मं पुराणं तत्रादौ सर्वलोकहिताय वै ।
व्यासेन वेदविदुषा समाख्यातं महात्मना ॥
1.92.m:
Among them, first the Brahma Purāṇa was recounted
by the great-souled Vyāsa, knower of the Vedas, for the welfare of all the worlds.

1.92.s:
tadvai sarvapurāṇāgryaṃ dharmakāmārthamokṣadam /
nānākhyānetihāsāḍhyaṃ daśasāhasramucyate //
1.92.d:
तद्वै सर्वपुराणाग्र्यं धर्मकामार्थमोक्षदम् ।
नानाख्यानेतिहासाढ्यं दशसाहस्रमुच्यते ॥
1.92.m:
It is indeed the foremost of all Purāṇas, bestowing dharma, desire, wealth, and liberation;
rich in various tales and histories, it is said to have ten thousand [verses].

1.92.s:
devānāṃ ca surāṇāṃ ca yatrotpattiḥ prakīrtitā /
prajāpatīnāṃ ca tathā dakṣādīnāṃ munīśvara //
1.92.d:
देवानां च सुराणां च यत्रोत्पत्तिः प्रकीर्तिता ।
प्रजापतीनां च तथा दक्षादीनां मुनीश्वर ॥
1.92.m:
Wherein the origin of the gods and deities is recounted,
and likewise of the lords of creatures beginning with Dakṣa, O lord of sages;

1.92.s:
tato lokeśvarasyātra sūryasya paramātmanaḥ /
vaṃśānukīrtanaṃ puṇyaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam //
1.92.d:
ततो लोकेश्वरस्यात्र सूर्यस्य परमात्मनः ।
वंशानुकीर्तनं पुण्यं महापातकनाशनम् ॥
1.92.m:
then the holy recitation of the lineage of the Sun, the supreme self
and lord of the world, which destroys great sins;

1.92.s:
yatrāvatāraḥ kathitaḥ paramānandarūpiṇaḥ /
śrīmato rāmacandrasya caturvyūhāvatāriṇaḥ //
1.92.d:
यत्रावतारः कथितः परमानन्दरूपिणः ।
श्रीमतो रामचन्द्रस्य चतुर्व्यूहावतारिणः ॥
1.92.m:
wherein is told the descent of the blessed Rāmacandra,
whose nature is supreme bliss, descended in the fourfold manifestation;

1.92.s:
tataśca somavaṃśasyaṃ kīrtanaṃ yatra varṇitam /
kṛṣṇasya jagadīśasya caritaṃ kalmaṣāpaham //
1.92.d:
ततश्च सोमवंशस्यं कीर्तनं यत्र वर्णितम् ।
कृष्णस्य जगदीशस्य चरितं कल्मषापहम् ॥
1.92.m:
and then wherein the glorification of the Lunar lineage is described,
along with the deed of Kṛṣṇa, lord of the world, which takes away sins;

1.92.s:
dvīpānāṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ varṣāṇāṃ cāpyaśeṣataḥ /
varṇanaṃ yatra pātālasvargāṇāṃ ca pradṛśyate //
1.92.d:
द्वीपानां चैव सर्वेषां वर्षाणां चाप्यशेषतः ।
वर्णनं यत्र पातालस्वर्गाणां च प्रदृश्यते ॥
1.92.m:
and where a description of all the continents and all the realms
is seen in full, as well as of the netherworlds and heavens;

1.92.s:
narakāṇāṃ samākhyānaṃ sūryastutikathānakam /
pārvatyāśca tathā janma vivāhaśca nigadyate //
1.92.d:
नरकाणां समाख्यानं सूर्यस्तुतिकथानकम् ।
पार्वत्याश्च तथा जन्म विवाहश्च निगद्यते ॥
1.92.m:
the account of the hells, the story of the praise of the Sun,
and the birth and marriage of Pārvatī are related;

1.92.s:
dakṣākhyānaṃ tataḥ proktamekāmrakṣetravarṇanam /
pūrvabhāgo 'yamuditaḥ purāṇasyāsya nārada //
1.92.d:
दक्षाख्यानं ततः प्रोक्तमेकाम्रक्षेत्रवर्णनम् ।
पूर्वभागो ऽयमुदितः पुराणस्यास्य नारद ॥
1.92.m:
then the tale of Dakṣa is told, and the description of the sacred field of Ekāmra—
this is declared to be the first part of this Purāṇa, O Nārada.

1.92.s:
asyottare vibhāge tu puruṣottamavarṇanam /
vistareṇa samākhyātaṃ tīrthayātrāvidhānataḥ //
1.92.d:
अस्योत्तरे विभागे तु पुरुषोत्तमवर्णनम् ।
विस्तरेण समाख्यातं तीर्थयात्राविधानतः ॥
1.92.m:
In its second part, however, the description of Puruṣottama
is recounted at length, by way of the rules for pilgrimage to sacred fords;

1.92.s:
atraiva kṛṣṇacaritaṃ vistarātsamudīritam /
varṇanaṃ yamalokasya pitṛśrāddhavidhistathā //
1.92.d:
अत्रैव कृष्णचरितं विस्तरात्समुदीरितम् ।
वर्णनं यमलोकस्य पितृश्राद्धविधिस्तथा ॥
1.92.m:
right here the deed of Kṛṣṇa is uttered in detail,
the description of Yama's realm, and the rule for ancestral rites for the ancestors;

1.92.s:
varṇāśramāṇāṃ dharmāśca kīrtitā yatra vistarāt /
viṣṇudharmayugākhyānaṃ pralayasya ca varṇanam //
1.92.d:
वर्णाश्रमाणां धर्माश्च कीर्तिता यत्र विस्तरात् ।
विष्णुधर्मयुगाख्यानं प्रलयस्य च वर्णनम् ॥
1.92.m:
and wherein the duties of the classes and stages of life are proclaimed at length,
the account of Viṣṇu's dharma and the ages, and the description of the cosmic dissolution;

1.92.s:
yogānāṃ ca samākhyānaṃ sāṃkhyānāṃ cāpi varṇanam /
brahmavādasamuddeśaḥ purāṇasya praśaṃsanam //
1.92.d:
योगानां च समाख्यानं सांख्यानां चापि वर्णनम् ।
ब्रह्मवादसमुद्देशः पुराणस्य प्रशंसनम् ॥
1.92.m:
the account of yogas and the description of Sāṃkhya systems,
the exposition of the doctrine of Brahman, and the praise of the Purāṇa.

1.92.s:
etadbrahmapurāṇaṃ tu bhāgadvayasamanvitam /
varṇitaṃ sarvapāpaghnaṃ sarvasaukhyapradāyakam //
1.92.d:
एतद्ब्रह्मपुराणं तु भागद्वयसमन्वितम् ।
वर्णितं सर्वपापघ्नं सर्वसौख्यप्रदायकम् ॥
1.92.m:
This Brahma Purāṇa, complete with two parts,
has been described as destroying all sins and bestowing all happiness,

1.92.s:
sūtaśaunakasaṃvādaṃ bhuktimuktipradāyakam /
likhitvetatpurāṇaṃ yo vaiśākhyāṃ hemasaṃyutam //
1.92.d:
सूतशौनकसंवादं भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायकम् ।
लिखित्वेतत्पुराणं यो वैशाख्यां हेमसंयुतम् ॥
1.92.m:
consisting of a dialogue between Sūta and Śaunaka, granting worldly enjoyment and liberation.
Whoever writes out this Purāṇa on the full moon of Vaiśākha, together with gold,

1.92.s:
jaladhenuyutaṃ cāpi bhaktyā dadyāddvijātaye /
paurāṇikāya saṃpūjya vastrabhojyavibhūṣaṇaiḥ //
1.92.d:
जलधेनुयुतं चापि भक्त्या दद्याद्द्विजातये ।
पौराणिकाय संपूज्य वस्त्रभोज्यविभूषणैः ॥
1.92.m:
and with a water-pot cow, and gives it with devotion to a twice-born
reciter of the Purāṇa, having honoured him with garments, foods, and ornaments,

1.92.s:
sa vasedbrahmaṇo loke yāvaccandrārkatārakam /
yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi brāhmānukramaṇīṃ dvija //
1.92.d:
स वसेद्ब्रह्मणो लोके यावच्चन्द्रार्कतारकम् ।
यः पठेच्छृणुयाद्वापि ब्राह्मानुक्रमणीं द्विज ॥
1.92.m:
dwells in the world of Brahmā as long as the moon, sun, and stars endure.
Whoever reads or hears the table of contents of the Brāhma [Purāṇa], O twice-born,

1.92.s:
so 'pi sarvapurāṇasya śroturvaktuḥ phalaṃ labhet /
śṛṇoti yaḥ purāṇaṃ tu brahmaṃ sarvaṃ jitendriyaḥ //
1.92.d:
सो ऽपि सर्वपुराणस्य श्रोतुर्वक्तुः फलं लभेत् ।
शृणोति यः पुराणं तु ब्रह्मं सर्वं जितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.92.m:
he too attains the fruit of a hearer and speaker of the whole Purāṇa.
Whoever, with senses conquered, hears the entire Brahma Purāṇa

1.92.s:
haviṣyāśī ca niyamātsa labhedbrahmaṇaḥ padam /
kimatra bahunoktena yadyadicchati mānavaḥ /
tatsarvaṃ labhate vatsa purāṇasyāsya kīrtanāt //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne caturthapāde brāhmapurāṇetihāsakathanaṃ nāma dvinavatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.92.d:
हविष्याशी च नियमात्स लभेद्ब्रह्मणः पदम् ।
किमत्र बहुनोक्तेन यद्यदिच्छति मानवः ।
तत्सर्वं लभते वत्स पुराणस्यास्य कीर्तनात् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने चतुर्थपादे ब्राह्मपुराणेतिहासकथनं नाम द्विनवतितमो ऽध्यायः
1.92.m:
and eats sacrificial food according to the rule, attains the abode of Brahmā.
What need is there of saying much here? Whatever a person desires,
all that he attains, dear child, from reciting this Purāṇa.

Thus ends the ninety-second chapter, titled "Recounting the History of the Brahma Purāṇa", in the fourth quarter of the Great Narrative in the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.
